title: 吼猴為什麼吼叫
text: Howler monkeys are named for the long loud cries, or howls, that they make every day. They are the loudest land animal and their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests. Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory. Everyone starts and ends the day by howling to check out where their nearest competitors are.

Interestingly, when there are few howler monkeys in an area, the howling routine takes on a different pattern. In Belize, where howler monkeys were newly reintroduced into a wildlife sanctuary, the howler monkeys were heard only a few times a week rather than every day. Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors. At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild. In the future when the population grows, there will be no need for the recording because the howler monkeys will have more reason to check in with the neighbors to define their own territories.
pre: 這是一篇動物行為的科普文章，先說明吼猴為何叫，再談數量少時的變化。讀的時候留意「原因」與「結果」的連結。
gist: 吼猴每天吼叫，聲音極大，用來爭奪資源並確認對手的位置。
在貝里斯，吼猴數量少，不需確認對手，所以很少叫；保育員因此播放錄音，讓牠們維持領域叫聲。

qs.s: Why do howler monkeys howl?
o: To claim their territory.
To check how popular they are.
To tell others they are going to leave.
To show friendliness to their neighbors.
qs.hint: 回到第 1 段，找 use their loud voices to fight for … 後面列出的目的。
qs.ev: Male howler monkeys use their loud voices to fight for food, mates, or territory.
qs.ex: 第 1 段指出雄猴用叫聲爭奪食物、配偶或地盤，第 2 段也提到 territorial calls，因此吼叫是為了宣示地盤。
why: (A) 對，與 territory 吻合。
(B) 錯，文中未談受歡迎程度。
(C) 錯，沒有提到告知要離開。
(D) 錯，叫聲是與競爭者有關，不是示好。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: Why did the howler monkeys in Belize howl less often?
o: They lived too close to each other.
There was enough food for all of them.
There were no other competitors around.
They were not used to the weather there.
qs.hint: 回到第 2 段，找 Apparently 後面解釋為何不需要叫。
qs.ev: Apparently, with plenty of space and no other howler monkeys around, there was no need to check on the whereabouts of their competitors.
qs.ex: 貝里斯的猴子空間充裕、周圍沒有其他吼猴，沒有必要確認競爭者位置，所以叫得少。
why: (A) 錯，是相距遠、數量少。
(B) 錯，文中沒說食物夠。
(C) 對，no other howler monkeys around。
(D) 錯，與天氣無關。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: Why do the keepers at the sanctuary use recorded howls?
o: To prevent the howler monkeys from getting homesick.
To help howler monkeys maintain their howling ability.
To trick the monkeys into the belief that there is plenty of space around.
To teach the monkeys how to make the loudest cries to scare people away.
qs.hint: 找 recorded howler sounds 這句，看 so that 後面的目的。
qs.ev: At the sanctuary, keepers now use recorded howler sounds from a distance so that the monkeys feel the need to make the territorial calls as they would do in the wild.
qs.ex: 播放錄音是為了讓猴子覺得有必要像野外一樣發出領域叫聲，也就是維持牠們的吼叫習性與能力。
why: (A) 錯，沒提到想家。
(B) 對，讓牠們繼續做領域叫聲。
(C) 錯，錄音讓牠們覺得有對手，而不是空間很大。
(D) 錯，與嚇人無關。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following is true about howler monkeys?
o: They howl most often at noon.
They originally came from Belize.
People can hear their howls three miles away.
Female monkeys howl to protect their babies.
qs.hint: 逐項在第 1 段找：時間、距離、雄／雌。
qs.ev: their howls can be heard three miles away through dense forests
qs.ex: 第 1 段明說叫聲在茂密森林中三英里外都聽得到，其餘選項文中皆無依據。
why: (A) 錯，是一天的開始與結束。
(B) 錯，是被重新引進貝里斯。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，是雄猴爭奪資源。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 吼猴因每天發出又長又響的吼叫而得名。牠們是最吵的陸地動物，叫聲在茂密森林中可傳到三英里外。雄吼猴用響亮的聲音爭奪食物、配偶或地盤。每天一開始與結束時，大家都會吼叫，以確認最近的競爭者在哪裡。
有趣的是，當一個地區吼猴很少時，吼叫的習慣會出現不同的模式。在貝里斯，吼猴被重新引進野生動物保護區，那裡的吼猴一星期只聽得到幾次，而不是每天。顯然，空間充裕又沒有其他吼猴在附近，就不需要確認競爭者的位置。在保護區，管理員現在從遠處播放吼猴的錄音，讓猴子覺得有必要像在野外一樣發出領域叫聲。將來數量增加時，就不需要錄音了，因為吼猴會有更多理由向鄰居確認，以劃定自己的地盤。
summary: 吼猴吼叫是為了確認競爭者位置、劃分地盤；當同類很少時就不需要常叫，所以保育員用錄音來維持這項習性。

title: 冰河國家公園與和平公園
text: After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads. Eventually, the demand for a road across the mountains led to the building of the Going-to-the-Sun Road.

The construction of the Going-to-the-Sun Road was a huge task. After 11 years of work, the final section of the road was completed in 1932. The road is considered an engineering feat. Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built. It is one of the most scenic roads in North America. The construction of the road has changed the way visitors experience the Glacier National Park. Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see.

Just across the border, in Canada, is the Waterton Lakes National Park. In 1931, members of the Rotary Clubs of Alberta and Montana suggested joining the two parks as a symbol of peace and friendship between the two countries. In 1932, the United States and Canadian governments renamed the parks the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, the world’s first. More recently, the parks have received several international honors. They were named as a World Heritage Site in 1995. This international recognition highlights the importance of this area, not just to the United States and Canada, but to the entire world.
pre: 這篇介紹一座國家公園的道路與跨國和平公園。讀的時候注意年份、因果（為何修路）與「世界第一」的特色。
gist: 遊客增加，需要穿越山區的道路，因而興建了「通往太陽之路」。
這條路花十一年完成，是工程壯舉，讓遊客能在短時間內遊覽更多園區。
美加兩座公園合併為世界第一座國際和平公園，並獲世界遺產肯定。

qs.s: What made it necessary to build a road through the Glacier National Park?
o: There were too many parks in Montana.
The park was not sunny enough for visitors.
The existing mountain roads were destroyed.
More visitors were interested in going to the park.
qs.hint: 看第 1 段第一句，找 growing number of park visitors。
qs.ev: After the creation of the Glacier National Park in Montana, the growing number of park visitors increased the need for roads.
qs.ex: 遊客越來越多，道路需求增加，所以要修路。
why: (A) 錯，文中沒提公園過多。
(B) 錯，沒談日照。
(C) 錯，沒有道路被毀的敘述。
(D) 對，遊客增加。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: How has the Going-to-the-Sun Road influenced the way people experience the Glacier National Park?
o: The scenery along the road is too beautiful for visitors to drive carefully.
It has become a marvelous experience for people to ride horses on this road.
The road has allowed people to see more of the park in a shorter period of time.
The transportation on the road was so difficult that few people could really enjoy the trip.
qs.hint: 第 2 段最後一句比較「現在」與「以前」。
qs.ev: Visitors now can drive over sections of the park that previously took days of horseback riding to see.
qs.ex: 以前騎馬要花好幾天才看得到的地方，現在開車就能到，所以能在較短時間內看到更多。
why: (A) 錯，文中沒談開車危險。
(B) 錯，騎馬是過去的方式。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，與文意相反。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What does “an engineering feat” mean?
o: A big success in construction.
A magical building machine.
A great disaster for the travelers.
An enjoyable process for engineers.
qs.hint: 看前後句：11 年完成、遊客讚嘆怎麼蓋得出來。
qs.ev: Even today, visitors to the park marvel at how such a road could have been built.
qs.ex: 遊客至今仍驚嘆這條路如何建成，可見 feat 指了不起的成就，因此是建築上的大成功。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，feat 不是機器。
(C) 錯，是讚美不是災難。
(D) 錯，重點是成就而非過程愉快。
qs.strat: 字義與指涉題要回到該字前後句，看上下文的因果與對照。

qs.s: What is special about the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park?
o: It is where the glacier runs to the lake.
It is the first park funded by the whole world.
It is a special park built to protect wild animals.
It is composed of two parks located in two countries.
qs.hint: 看第 3 段，找 joining the two parks 與 the world’s first。
qs.ev: In 1932, the United States and Canadian governments renamed the parks the Waterton-Glacier International Peace Park, the world’s first.
qs.ex: 它由美國與加拿大兩座公園合併而成，是世界第一座國際和平公園。
why: (A) 錯，文中沒提冰河入湖。
(B) 錯，沒有世界出資。
(C) 錯，目的是和平友誼。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 蒙大拿州的冰河國家公園成立後，遊客愈來愈多，增加了對道路的需求。最後，橫越山區的道路需求促成了「通往太陽之路」的興建。
興建「通往太陽之路」是一項龐大工程。歷經十一年，道路最後一段於 1932 年完工。這條路被視為工程上的壯舉。即使在今天，造訪公園的遊客仍驚嘆怎麼可能蓋出這樣的路。它是北美風景最優美的道路之一。這條路改變了遊客體驗冰河國家公園的方式。現在遊客可以開車走過園區的一些路段，這些地方以前要騎馬好幾天才能看完。
就在國界另一邊的加拿大，是沃特頓湖國家公園。1931 年，亞伯達省與蒙大拿州的扶輪社成員建議把兩座公園合併，作為兩國和平與友誼的象徵。1932 年，美國與加拿大政府將兩座公園更名為沃特頓－冰河國際和平公園，這是世界第一座。近年來，這些公園獲得數項國際榮譽，1995 年被列為世界遺產。這項國際肯定凸顯了這個地區的重要性，不只對美國與加拿大，對全世界都是如此。
summary: 文章依序介紹為遊客增加而修建的公路、它帶來的便利，以及兩座公園合併成世界第一座國際和平公園。

title: 冰雕的難處
text: Ice sculpting is a difficult process. First, ice must be carefully selected so that it is suitable for sculpting. Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity. It should also have the minimum amount of air bubbles. Perfectly clear ice blocks weighing 140 kg and measuring 100 cm × 50 cm × 25 cm are available from the Clinebell Company in Colorado. Much larger clear blocks are produced in Europe and Canada or harvested from a frozen river in Sweden. These large ice blocks are used for large ice sculpting events and for building ice hotels.

Another difficulty in the process of ice sculpting is time control. The temperature of the environment affects how quickly the piece must be completed to avoid the effects of melting. If the sculpting does not take place in a cold environment, then the sculptor must work quickly to finish his piece. The tools used for sculpting also affect when the task can be accomplished. Some sculptures can be completed in as little as ten minutes if power tools are used. Ice sculptors also use razor-sharp chisels that are specifically designed for cutting ice. The best ice chisels are made in Japan, a country that, along with China, has a long tradition of magnificent ice sculptures.

Ice sculptures are used as decorations in some cuisines, especially in Asia. When holding a dinner party, some large restaurants or hotels will use an ice sculpture to decorate the table. For example, in a wedding banquet it is common to see a pair of ice-sculpted swans that represent the union of the new couple.
pre: 這篇說明冰雕為什麼困難，並介紹用途。注意 First、Another 等順序詞，以及每段的主題。
gist: 冰雕的第一個難處是要選對冰：純淨、透明、氣泡少。
第二個難處是控制時間，要考慮環境溫度與所用工具。
冰雕常用來裝飾宴席，例如婚宴上的天鵝。

qs.s: What kind of ice is ideal for sculpting?
o: Ice from ice hotels.
Ice from clean water.
Ice with lots of bubbles in it.
Ice weighing over 100 kilograms.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段找 ideal material。
qs.ev: Its ideal material is pure, clean water with high clarity.
qs.ex: 理想的冰來自純淨乾淨的水，透明度高。
why: (A) 錯，冰旅館是大冰塊的用途。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，氣泡越少越好。
(D) 錯，重量不是標準。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: Why is ice sculpting difficult?
o: It is hard to control the size and shape of the ice.
The right theme for ice sculpting is not easy to find.
The appropriate tools are only available in some countries.
It is not easy to find the right kind of ice and work environment.
qs.hint: 整合第 1、2 段各自的 difficulty：一個是選冰，一個是時間（環境溫度）。
qs.ev: First, ice must be carefully selected so that it is suitable for sculpting.
qs.ex: 第 1 段講選冰，第 2 段講環境溫度與時間控制，所以難在找到合適的冰與工作環境。
why: (A) 錯，沒談大小形狀難控制。
(B) 錯，沒談主題。
(C) 錯，只說最好的鑿子產自日本。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 整合題要把各段的重點合在一起，找涵蓋最多段落的選項。

qs.s: What is paragraph 3 mainly about?
o: The uses of ice sculptures.
The places where ice is sculpted.
The quality of ice sculptures.
The origin of ice sculpting parties.
qs.hint: 看第 3 段首句。
qs.ev: Ice sculptures are used as decorations in some cuisines, especially in Asia.
qs.ex: 第 3 段先說冰雕用來裝飾，再舉婚宴天鵝為例，主題是用途。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，沒討論地點。
(C) 錯，沒談品質。
(D) 錯，沒談起源。
qs.strat: 段落主旨題看該段首句與舉例。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about the process of sculpting ice?
o: It takes more time to carve with razor-sharp chisels.
It can be finished in 10 minutes if the right tools are used.
Larger blocks of ice from Sweden are easier to handle for sculptors.
The carver must work fast in a cold environment to avoid catching cold.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段找 ten minutes。
qs.ev: Some sculptures can be completed in as little as ten minutes if power tools are used.
qs.ex: 用電動工具，有些作品只要十分鐘就能完成，所以選擇對的工具可縮短時間。
why: (A) 錯，沒說鑿子更花時間。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，文中沒比較好不好處理。
(D) 錯，是不冷的環境才要快，避免融化。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 冰雕是一個困難的過程。首先，必須謹慎挑選適合雕刻的冰。理想的材料是透明度高、純淨乾淨的水，氣泡也要愈少愈好。重 140 公斤、尺寸為 100 × 50 × 25 公分的完全透明冰塊，可以向科羅拉多州的 Clinebell 公司購得。更大的透明冰塊產自歐洲與加拿大，或從瑞典的結冰河流中採收。這些大冰塊用於大型冰雕活動與建造冰旅館。
冰雕過程的另一個難處是時間控制。環境的溫度會影響作品必須多快完成，以免受融化影響。如果雕刻不是在寒冷環境中進行，雕刻家就必須快速完成作品。使用的工具也會影響完成的時間。有些作品如果使用電動工具，短短十分鐘就能完成。冰雕家也使用專為切割冰塊設計、鋒利如刀的鑿子。最好的冰鑿產自日本，這個國家與中國一樣，有悠久的精美冰雕傳統。
冰雕在某些飲食場合被用來當裝飾，尤其在亞洲。舉辦宴會時，有些大型餐廳或飯店會用冰雕來裝飾餐桌。例如，在婚宴上常可看到一對冰雕天鵝，象徵新人結合。
summary: 冰雕難在選冰與控制時間，並常作為宴席裝飾。

title: 預期會影響疼痛感
genre: 說明文・科學研究報導
text: If you touch your finger to a hot stove, you know it’s going to hurt. However, if you convince yourself beforehand that the pain won’t be so bad, you might not suffer as much. According to a recent study, the part of your brain that reacts to severe pain is largely the same part that reacts to expectation of pain.

Researchers in this study worked with 10 volunteers, ages 24 to 46. Each volunteer wore a device that gave out 20-second-long pulses of heat to the right leg. There were three levels of heat, producing mild, moderate, or strong pain. During training, the volunteers would first hear a tone, followed by a period of silence, and then feel a heat pulse. They then learned to associate the length of the silent pause with the intensity of the upcoming heat pulse. The longer the pause, the stronger the heat pulse would be, causing more severe pain.

A day or two later, the real experiment began. The researchers found that the parts of the brain involved in learning, memory, emotion, and touch became more active as the volunteers expected higher levels of pain. These were mainly the same areas that became active when participants actually felt pain. Interestingly, when the volunteers expected only mild or moderate pain but experienced severe pain, they reported feeling 28 percent less pain than when they expected severe pain and actually got it.

The new study emphasizes that pain has both physical and psychological elements. Understanding how pain works in the mind and brain could eventually give doctors tools for helping people cope with painful medical treatments.
pre: 這是一篇實驗報導：先講結論，再說明實驗設計與發現。讀的時候留意實驗怎麼做（步驟與數字）。
gist: 預期疼痛的腦區與感受劇痛的腦區大致相同。
實驗對十位志願者的腿部施加熱脈衝，並訓練他們用停頓長短預期疼痛。
正式實驗發現預期越痛，相關腦區越活躍；預期較輕卻遇到劇痛，感覺少 28%。
疼痛兼具生理與心理成分，了解它可幫助醫生協助病人。

qs.s: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: We should learn to be sensitive to pain.
Our feeling of pain is decided by our environment.
How people feel pain remains unknown to scientists.
Our reaction to pain is closely related to our expectation of pain.
qs.hint: 主旨常在首段與末段，看第 1 段最後一句。
qs.ev: According to a recent study, the part of your brain that reacts to severe pain is largely the same part that reacts to expectation of pain.
qs.ex: 文章自始至終討論預期與疼痛反應在腦中的關聯。
why: (A) 錯，沒有這種建議。
(B) 錯，談的是預期而非環境。
(C) 錯，研究正是在揭示原因。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與末段，再排除只談到細節或超出文章範圍的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about the pulses of heat in the study?
o: Each heat pulse lasted for 20 seconds.
The pulses were given to the arms of the volunteers.
Different devices gave out different levels of heat pulses.
There were two levels of heat intensity given to the volunteers.
qs.hint: 第 2 段逐一核對秒數、部位、等級。
qs.ev: Each volunteer wore a device that gave out 20-second-long pulses of heat to the right leg.
qs.ex: 每次脈衝 20 秒，部位是右腿。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，是右腿。
(C) 錯，是同一個裝置產生三種等級。
(D) 錯，有三種等級。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: How did the volunteers learn to expect different levels of heat?
o: From the loudness of the tone they heard.
From the instruction given to them by the researchers.
From the color of a light flashing on the device they wore.
From the length of the pause between a tone and the heat pulse.
qs.hint: 找 associate the length of the silent pause。
qs.ev: They then learned to associate the length of the silent pause with the intensity of the upcoming heat pulse.
qs.ex: 受試者學會把安靜停頓的長短與即將來的熱度強弱聯想在一起。
why: (A) 錯，是停頓長度而非音量。
(B) 錯，是自己訓練學會。
(C) 錯，沒有燈光。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: According to the passage, what may be the author’s advice to a doctor before a surgery?
o: To provide the patient with more pain killers.
To talk to the patient and ease his/her worries.
To give the patient strong heat pulses beforehand.
To emphasize the possible severe pain to the patient.
qs.hint: 看末段最後一句，了解心理與疼痛的關係後可做什麼。
qs.ev: Understanding how pain works in the mind and brain could eventually give doctors tools for helping people cope with painful medical treatments.
qs.ex: 預期會影響疼痛感，所以醫生手術前安撫病人、降低其擔心，可能減輕痛感。
why: (A) 錯，文中沒談止痛藥。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，那是實驗做法。
(D) 錯，強調疼痛會讓預期升高。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

zh: 如果你把手指碰到熱爐子，你知道會痛。然而，如果你事先說服自己疼痛不會那麼嚴重，你可能就不會那麼難受。根據最近的一項研究，大腦中對劇痛有反應的部位，與對疼痛預期有反應的部位大致相同。
這項研究的研究人員與 10 位年齡從 24 到 46 歲的志願者合作。每位志願者戴著一個裝置，對右腿發出長達 20 秒的熱脈衝。熱度分三種，分別造成輕微、中度或強烈的疼痛。訓練時，志願者會先聽到一個聲音，接著是一段安靜，然後感受到一次熱脈衝。他們接著學會把安靜停頓的長短與即將到來的熱脈衝強度聯想在一起。停頓越久，熱脈衝越強，造成的疼痛也越劇烈。
一兩天後，正式實驗開始。研究人員發現，隨著志願者預期更高程度的疼痛，大腦中與學習、記憶、情緒和觸覺有關的部位變得更活躍。這些主要就是參與者真正感到疼痛時活躍的同一些區域。有趣的是，當志願者預期只有輕微或中度疼痛，卻經歷了劇痛時，他們回報的疼痛感，比預期劇痛而真的遇到劇痛時少了 28%。
這項新研究強調，疼痛兼具生理與心理的成分。了解疼痛在心智與大腦中如何運作，最終可能提供醫生工具，幫助人們應付疼痛的醫療處置。
summary: 研究顯示對疼痛的預期與實際疼痛激活相似腦區，心理預期會改變疼痛感，未來可用於幫助病人。

title: 不做事協會的來信
text: To Whom It May Concern:

Your address was forwarded to us by Why Bother Magazine. All of us here think The International Institute of Not Doing Much is the best organization in the world. You know how to avoid unnecessary activities!

We closely followed the advice in your article. First, we replaced all our telephones with carrier pigeons. Simply removing the jingle of telephones and replacing them with the pleasant sounds of birds has had a remarkable effect on everyone. Besides, birds are cheaper than telephone service. After all, we are a business. We have to think of the bottom line. As a side benefit, the birds also fertilize the lawn outside the new employee sauna.

Next, we sold the computers off to Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty, a firm of lawyers nearby. Our electricity bill went way down. Big savings! The boss is impressed. We have completely embraced paper technology. Now that we all use pencils, doodling is on the increase, and the quality of pencilwomanship is impressive, as you can tell from my handwriting in this letter. By the way, if you can, please send this letter back to us. We can erase and reuse it. Just tie it to Maggie’s leg and she’ll know where to take it.

Now it’s very calm and quiet here. You can notice the difference. No more loud chatter on the telephones! All we hear is the scratching of pencil on paper, the sound of pigeons, and the delivery of inter-office correspondence by paper airplane.
Wonderful! I’ve always wanted to work for an insurance company ever since I was a little girl. Now it’s perfect.
Sincerely yours, Eleanor Lightly Spokeswoman and Company Hair Stylist ABC Activity Insurance: Insure against overdoing it
pre: 這是一封幽默的信，語氣誇張。讀的時候留意寄信人是誰、寄給誰，以及公司做了哪些「退回老方法」的改變。
gist: 抬頭：致相關人士。
說明收到地址，並稱讚不做事協會懂得避免不必要的活動。
第一步：用信鴿取代電話，更安靜、更便宜。
第二步：賣掉電腦、改用鉛筆紙張，信可擦掉重複使用，由鴿子 Maggie 送信。
現在公司變得安靜，只聽到鉛筆聲與鴿子聲。
寫信人說在保險公司工作正是她的心願。
署名與公司資訊。

qs.s: Which of the following best describes the life the author is leading?
o: A simple, slow-paced life.
A life of hard work and security.
A religious, peasant-like life.
A life away from paper and pencils.
qs.hint: 整體看信中描述的公司改變：電話換信鴿、電腦換鉛筆、環境安靜。
qs.ev: Now it’s very calm and quiet here.
qs.ex: 信中公司棄用電話和電腦，改用鴿子、鉛筆，環境平靜，是簡單而步調慢的生活。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，沒有努力工作的描述。
(C) 錯，與宗教無關。
(D) 錯，反而大量使用紙筆。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與末段，再排除只談到細節或超出文章範圍的選項。

qs.s: Where is Eleanor’s letter sent to?
o: Why Bother Magazine.
ABC Activity Insurance Company.
Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty Law Firm.
The International Institute of Not Doing Much.
qs.hint: 第 2 段稱讚的對象與「your article」暗示收信者。
qs.ev: All of us here think The International Institute of Not Doing Much is the best organization in the world.
qs.ex: 信中稱讚該機構並說依照「你們的文章」建議做，所以是寫給不做事協會。
why: (A) 錯，雜誌只是轉寄地址。
(B) 錯，這是寫信人的公司。
(C) 錯，是買電腦的律師事務所。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: Which of the following is practiced in the author’s company?
o: Replacing the manual work system with modern technology.
Turning off lights in the daytime to save electricity.
Recycling paper resources whenever possible.
Buying birds and pets as company for the staff.
qs.hint: 找信中提到可擦掉重複使用的東西。
qs.ev: We can erase and reuse it.
qs.ex: 公司擦掉信紙重複使用，屬於紙張資源回收再利用。
why: (A) 錯，是反過來用傳統方式取代科技。
(B) 錯，沒提關燈。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，鴿子是用來傳信，不是陪伴員工。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

qs.s: What is true about Maggie?
o: She works as a manager in the author’s company.
She sometimes helps fertilize the lawn outside the sauna.
She often helps with inter-office correspondence using e-mail.
Her handwriting has improved a lot after entering the company.
qs.hint: Maggie 是第 4 段出現的，腿上綁信，可知是鴿子；再對照第 3 段鳥的附帶好處。
qs.ev: As a side benefit, the birds also fertilize the lawn outside the new employee sauna.
qs.ex: Maggie 是信鴿，而鳥會替三溫暖外的草坪施肥。
why: (A) 錯，Maggie 是鴿子。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，已淘汰電腦，用紙飛機和鴿子。
(D) 錯，寫字的是 Eleanor。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

zh: 敬啟者：
貴機構的地址是由《何必麻煩》雜誌轉給我們的。我們這裡所有人都認為「國際少做事協會」是世界上最棒的組織。你們懂得如何避免不必要的活動！
我們嚴格遵循貴文章中的建議。首先，我們把所有電話換成了傳信鴿。光是移除電話的叮噹聲，換成鳥兒悅耳的聲音，就對每個人產生了顯著的效果。此外，鳥比電話服務便宜。畢竟我們是公司，必須考慮利潤底線。附帶的好處是，這些鳥也替新蓋的員工三溫暖外的草坪施肥。
接著，我們把電腦賣給附近的律師事務所 Stab, Grab, Grit, and Nasty。我們的電費大幅下降，省了很多錢！老闆印象深刻。我們已完全擁抱紙張科技。現在大家都用鉛筆，塗鴉增加了，而「鉛筆女書法」的品質令人印象深刻，從我這封信的字跡你就看得出來。順便一提，如果可以，請把這封信寄還給我們。我們可以擦掉重複使用。只要把它綁在 Maggie 的腿上，牠就知道要送到哪裡去。
現在這裡非常平靜安靜。你可以感覺得出差別。不再有電話裡的嘈雜聊天聲！我們聽到的只有鉛筆在紙上的沙沙聲、鴿子的叫聲，以及用紙飛機遞送的辦公室內部信件。
太棒了！我從小女孩時就一直想在保險公司工作。現在一切都太完美了。
誠摯的，Eleanor Lightly，發言人兼公司髮型師，ABC 活動保險：為過度勞累投保
summary: 這封幽默的信把公司改回鴿子與鉛筆，宣稱變得安靜、省錢，是對「少做事」生活的誇張讚美。

title: 全球第一座綠色機場
text: The Galápagos Islands are the Pacific island paradise where Darwin’s theory of evolution was born. They are places filled with giant tree lizards, sandy beaches, and tropical plants. Now they will be famous for one more thing: the world’s first green airport.

This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra. It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete the project by 2009. The new development has several important features: use of wind and solar energy, passive heating and cooling systems, as well as concrete runways in place of asphalt, which has a greater carbon footprint during its production cycle. This new development couldn’t be coming at a better time for the Galápagos, which were added to an environmental “danger list” in 2007.

Pacific islands like the Galápagos, Easter Island, and Tahiti, have economies that are driven almost completely by tourism. However, some people think these are “unsustainable models of development.” The number of visitors to the Galápagos rose more than 250% from 1990 to 2006, while the number of commercial flights to the area rose 193% from 2001 to 2006. These increases put great stress on the islands’ resources and environment. Air travel is especially criticized for exhausting natural resources and causing environmental damage. Thus, efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact of the tourism industry. The greening of airports is just one of these attempts.
pre: 這篇新聞報導介紹加拉巴哥群島的綠色機場計畫及其背景。注意「是什麼」「在哪裡」「為什麼需要」三個層次。
gist: 加拉巴哥群島將擁有世界第一座綠色機場。
巴爾特拉島機場重建，採用風能、太陽能與混凝土跑道，且群島已列入環境警戒名單。
旅遊業造成遊客與航班暴增，讓環境承受壓力，綠色機場是減少衝擊的一環。

qs.s: What is this article mainly about?
o: The problems of Darwin’s theory.
The background of building a green airport.
The history of the Galápagos Islands.
The ease of transportation to the Pacific islands.
qs.hint: 看首段最後一句與全文的發展：計畫內容與為何需要。
qs.ev: Now they will be famous for one more thing: the world’s first green airport.
qs.ex: 文章介紹綠色機場的內容，以及旅遊增加導致環境壓力的背景。
why: (A) 錯，只是順帶提到達爾文。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，沒有談歷史。
(D) 錯，談的是環境壓力而非交通方便。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與末段，再排除只談到細節或超出文章範圍的選項。

qs.s: Where will the world’s first green airport be built?
o: In Tahiti.
In Argentina.
In Baltra.
In the United States.
qs.hint: 找 airport on the island of ...。
qs.ev: This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador has recently contracted Argentine Corporación America to manage the redevelopment of the airport on the island of Baltra.
qs.ex: 機場在巴爾特拉島重建。
why: (A) 錯，大溪地只是舉例。
(B) 錯，阿根廷只是承包公司國別。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，未提到。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What is true about the Galápagos Islands?
o: They are located near Ecuador in the Pacific Ocean.
They have had a great increase in population since 2001.
They will invest US$20 million to promote their tourism.
They have become one of the most dangerous places in the world.
qs.hint: 第 2 段開頭，與選項逐一核對。
qs.ev: This group of islands off the coast of Ecuador
qs.ex: 群島位於厄瓜多外海，屬太平洋島嶼，所以選 A。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，增加的是遊客與航班，不是人口。
(C) 錯，這筆錢是建機場，不是推廣旅遊。
(D) 錯，danger list 指環境，不是危險地方。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What does the project in the second paragraph refer to?
o: The plan to build a green airport.
The research on the production of solar energy.
The task of calculating a carbon footprint.
The study on the exhaustion of natural resources.
qs.hint: 看 project 前面一句：誰簽約、做什麼、要多少錢。
qs.ev: It is estimated that US$20 million is needed to complete the project by 2009.
qs.ex: 前句說委託管理巴爾特拉機場重建，project 就是這個機場重建（綠色機場）計畫。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，太陽能只是特色之一。
(C) 錯，碳足跡只是比較用語。
(D) 錯，資源耗盡是背景。
qs.strat: 字義與指涉題要回到該字前後句，看上下文的因果與對照。

zh: 加拉巴哥群島是達爾文演化論誕生的太平洋島嶼天堂。那裡到處是巨大的樹蜥蜴、沙灘與熱帶植物。現在它們將因為另一件事而出名：世界第一座綠色機場。
這個位於厄瓜多外海的群島最近委託阿根廷的美洲公司負責巴爾特拉島機場的重建。估計到 2009 年完成這個計畫需要兩千萬美元。這項新開發有幾個重要特色：使用風能與太陽能、被動式加熱與冷卻系統，以及用混凝土跑道取代瀝青，因為瀝青在生產過程中的碳足跡較大。對於在 2007 年被列入環境「警戒名單」的加拉巴哥來說，這項新開發來得正是時候。

像加拉巴哥、復活節島和大溪地這些太平洋島嶼，經濟幾乎完全由觀光驅動。然而，有些人認為這是「不可持續的發展模式」。1990 到 2006 年間，造訪加拉巴哥的遊客增加超過 250%，而 2001 到 2006 年間，前往當地的商業航班增加了 193%。這些增長對島上的資源與環境造成很大壓力。航空旅行尤其受到批評，因為它耗盡自然資源並造成環境破壞。因此，人們正努力減少觀光業對環境的衝擊。機場綠化只是這些嘗試之一。
summary: 加拉巴哥群島將建世界第一座綠色機場，是為了回應觀光暴增造成的環境壓力。

title: 牛會當指南針嗎
genre: 說明文・科學研究報導
text: According to popular folklore, many animals are smarter than they appear. Dogs bark before earthquakes; cattle predict rainfall by sitting on the ground. But cattle may have another hidden talent in telling which way is north.

Small animals such as mole rats living underground are known for the use of magnetism to navigate. Dr. Begall and her colleagues wanted to know whether larger mammals also have the ability to perceive magnetic fields. They investigated this possibility by studying images of thousands of cattle captured on Google Earth, a website that stitches together satellite photographs to produce an image of the Earth’s surface.

Grazing animals are known to orient themselves in a way that minimizes wind chill from the north and maximizes the warmth of the sun when they are cold. The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors and see whether cattle could act like compass needles.

The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction. This north-south preference has also been noted in flies, termites and honeybees. But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail. The researchers were therefore unable to answer their research questions of whether cattle prefer to look north or south, and whether that differs in the northern and southern hemispheres.
pre: 這篇介紹一項用衛星影像研究牛的方向的研究。注意研究的問題、方法、控制的因素，以及結論與限制。
gist: 傳說動物比外表聰明，牛可能還有辨別北方的才能。
研究者用 Google Earth 的影像研究牛是否能感知磁場。
因吃草動物會受風與陽光影響方向，須大量樣本來平均掉這些因素。
結論是牛大致面向南北，但影像解析度不足，無法分辨頭尾。

qs.s: What is the article mainly about?
o: The usefulness of Google Earth.
Whether cattle are superior to other animals.
Animals’ sensitivity to natural disasters.
Whether cattle behave like compass needles.
qs.hint: 看首段末句與全文：研究者想知道牛能否像指南針。
qs.ev: But cattle may have another hidden talent in telling which way is north.
qs.ex: 全文圍繞牛是否像指南針指針般朝向南北。
why: (A) 錯，只是研究工具。
(B) 錯，沒有比較誰更優越。
(C) 錯，只在首段當開場。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與末段，再排除只談到細節或超出文章範圍的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following factors might affect Dr. Begall’s research result?
o: Rainfall.
Earthquakes.
Location.
Cost.
qs.hint: 第 3 段說明為何要研究不同地點與時間。
qs.ev: The researchers therefore had to study a lot of cows grazing in lots of different places at different times of day, in order to average out these factors
qs.ex: 研究者必須涵蓋不同地點與時間以平均掉風與日照等因素，可見地點會影響結果。
why: (A) 錯，下雨預測只是傳說。
(B) 錯，地震是首段傳說。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，文中沒談成本。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

qs.s: What is the major finding of Dr. Begall’s study?
o: Cattle point north-south.
Magnetism can’t be studied scientifically.
Animals prefer to look south.
Google Earth is a reliable research tool.
qs.hint: 看末段 concluded 那一句。
qs.ev: The researchers concluded that cattle do generally orient themselves in a north-south direction.
qs.ex: 主要發現是牛大致朝南北方向。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，文中並未否定。
(C) 錯，無法分辨朝南或朝北。
(D) 錯，其解析度仍有限。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: Why couldn’t the researchers get the answer to their research questions?
o: Many cattle in their study were sitting on the ground.
The cattle constantly change directions to avoid wind chill.
There is magnetic difference between the two hemispheres.
They couldn’t tell a cow’s head from its tail in the satellite pictures.
qs.hint: 末段 But unfortunately 後面。
qs.ev: But unfortunately, even the high resolution of Google Earth is not powerful enough to tell which end of the cow is its head, and which its tail.
qs.ex: 衛星影像分不出牛頭牛尾，所以無法回答牠們偏好朝北或朝南。
why: (A) 錯，沒有此原因。
(B) 錯，沒有這樣的說法。
(C) 錯，那是未解的問題之一而非原因。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 根據民間傳說，許多動物比看起來更聰明。狗會在地震前吠叫；牛會透過坐在地上來預測下雨。但牛可能還有另一項隱藏的才能：辨別哪邊是北方。
像鼴鼠這類住在地下的小動物，以利用磁性導航而聞名。貝加爾博士和她的同事想知道，體型較大的哺乳動物是否也有感知磁場的能力。他們透過研究 Google Earth 上拍到的數千頭牛的影像來探討這個可能性；Google Earth 是一個把衛星照片拼接起來、產生地球表面影像的網站。
眾所周知，吃草的動物會調整自己的朝向，以減少來自北方的風寒，並在寒冷時盡量多吸收陽光的溫暖。因此研究者必須研究在許多不同地點、一天中不同時間吃草的許多牛，以平均掉這些因素，看看牛是否能像指南針的指針一樣。
研究者的結論是，牛確實大致朝南北方向調整自己的方位。這種南北偏好在蒼蠅、白蟻和蜜蜂身上也曾被注意到。但可惜的是，即使 Google Earth 的解析度很高，仍不足以分辨牛的哪一端是頭、哪一端是尾。因此研究者無法回答他們的研究問題：牛偏好朝北還是朝南，以及這在南北半球是否不同。
summary: 研究以衛星影像發現牛大致朝南北，但因影像無法分辨頭尾，未能回答朝北或朝南的問題。

title: 讓孩子愛上多樣食物
text: Children normally have a distrust of new foods. But it’s the parents’ job to serve a variety of foods and expose their children to healthy dieting habits.

Some simple strategies can help even the pickiest eater learn to like a more varied diet. First of all, you don’t have to send children out of the kitchen. With hot stoves, boiling water and sharp knives at hand, it is understandable that parents don’t want children in the kitchen when they’re making dinner. But studies suggest that involving children in meal preparation is an important first step in getting them to try new foods.

In one study, nearly 600 children from kindergarten to sixth grade took part in a nutrition curriculum intended to get them to eat more vegetables and whole grains. The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not. Kids don’t usually like radishes, but if kids cut them up and put them in the salad, they will love the dish.

Another strategy is not to diet in front of your children. Kids are tuned into their parents’ eating preferences and are far more likely to try foods if they see their mother or father eating them. Given this powerful effect, parents who are trying to lose weight should be careful of how their dieting habits can influence a child’s perceptions about food and healthful eating. In one study of 5-year-old girls about dieting, one child noted that dieting involved drinking chocolate milkshakes, because her mother was using Slim-Fast drinks. Another child said dieting meant “you fix food but you don’t eat it.” By exposing young children to erratic dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.
pre: 這是給家長的建議文，提出兩個策略並用研究支持。讀的時候找 First of all、Another strategy 等標記。
gist: 孩子對新食物天生不信任，父母要提供多樣食物。
策略一：讓孩子參與備餐，有助於嘗試新食物。
研究顯示自己煮過的孩子更願意吃那些食物。
策略二：不要在孩子面前節食，否則可能讓孩子產生錯誤觀念與飲食失調風險。

qs.s: What is the main purpose of this article?
o: To explain what causes children’s eating disorder.
To teach children about the meal preparation process.
To advocate the importance of vegetables and whole grains.
To inform parents how they can help their children like varied foods.
qs.hint: 看首段與第 2 段的 strategies。
qs.ev: Some simple strategies can help even the pickiest eater learn to like a more varied diet.
qs.ex: 全文提供父母幫孩子接受多樣食物的策略。
why: (A) 錯，飲食失調只是最後提到的風險。
(B) 錯，對象是父母不是孩子。
(C) 錯，蔬菜全穀只是研究例子。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與末段，再排除只談到細節或超出文章範圍的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following groups will eat more balanced meals?
o: The children who help cook food.
The children whose parents are on a diet.
The children who do not love radishes.
The children whose parents work in a cafeteria.
qs.hint: 看第 3 段的研究結果。
qs.ev: The researchers found that children who had cooked their own foods were more likely to eat those foods in the cafeteria than children who had not.
qs.ex: 自己煮過食物的孩子更願意吃，因此飲食會更均衡。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，父母節食反而有害。
(C) 錯，文中沒這樣說。
(D) 錯，只是研究地點。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

qs.s: What does erratic in the last sentence imply?
o: Obvious.
Healthful.
Dishonest.
Inappropriate.
qs.hint: 看 By exposing ... 與後面的 risk for eating disorders，句意是負面的。
qs.ev: By exposing young children to erratic dieting habits, parents may be putting them at risk for eating disorders.
qs.ex: 接觸會導致飲食失調的節食習慣，所以 erratic 帶有不恰當、不正常的意思。
why: (A) 錯。
(B) 錯，與 risk 矛盾。
(C) 錯，與誠實無關。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 字義與指涉題要回到該字前後句，看上下文的因果與對照。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Slim-Fast?

qs.hint: 找 Slim-Fast 出現的地方，看孩子為何誤以為節食是喝奶昔。

qs.ex: 孩子把媽媽喝的 Slim-Fast 當成巧克力奶昔，可知它看起來像巧克力奶昔。
why: (A) 錯。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，沒提蔬菜。
(D) 錯，這是字面玩笑。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 孩子通常對新食物不信任。但提供多樣的食物、讓孩子接觸健康的飲食習慣，是父母的責任。
有些簡單的策略，可以幫助即使最挑食的孩子學會喜歡更多樣的飲食。首先，你不必把孩子趕出廚房。有熱爐子、滾水和利刀在旁，父母在做晚餐時不想讓孩子待在廚房是可以理解的。但研究顯示，讓孩子參與備餐，是讓他們嘗試新食物的重要第一步。
在一項研究中，近 600 名從幼稚園到六年級的孩子參加了一個營養課程，目的是讓他們多吃蔬菜與全穀類。研究者發現，自己煮過食物的孩子，比沒煮過的孩子更可能在餐廳吃這些食物。孩子通常不喜歡蘿蔔，但如果孩子自己把蘿蔔切好放進沙拉，他們就會愛上這道菜。
另一個策略是不要在孩子面前節食。孩子對父母的飲食偏好很敏感，如果看到爸爸或媽媽吃，他們會更願意嘗試。鑑於這種強大的影響，正在減重的父母應該留意自己的節食習慣如何影響孩子對食物與健康飲食的看法。在一項針對五歲女孩的節食研究中，有個孩子說節食就是喝巧克力奶昔，因為她媽媽在喝 Slim-Fast 飲品。另一個孩子說節食是「你煮了食物卻不吃」。讓幼童接觸不當的節食習慣，父母可能使他們面臨飲食失調的風險。
summary: 文章提出兩個策略：讓孩子參與備餐、不在孩子面前節食，並以研究支持，幫助孩子接受多樣食物。

title: 紐西蘭的「醜神」沙螽
text: On the island of New Zealand, there is a grasshopper-like species of insect that is found nowhere else on earth. New Zealanders have given it the nickname weta, which is a native Maori word meaning “god of bad looks.” It’s easy to see why anyone would call this insect a bad-looking bug. Most people feel disgusted at the sight of these bulky, slow-moving creatures.

Wetas are nocturnal creatures; they come out of their caves and holes only after dark. A giant weta can grow to over three inches long and weigh as much as 1.5 ounces. Giant wetas can hop up to two feet at a time. Some of them live in trees, and others live in caves. They are very long-lived for insects, and some adult wetas can live as long as two years. Just like their cousins grasshoppers and crickets, wetas are able to “sing” by rubbing their leg parts together, or against their lower bodies.

Most people probably don’t feel sympathy for these endangered creatures, but they do need protecting. The slow and clumsy wetas have been around on the island since the times of the dinosaurs, and have evolved and survived in an environment where they had no enemies until rats came to the island with European immigrants. Since rats love to hunt and eat wetas, the rat population on the island has grown into a real problem for many of the native species that are unaccustomed to its presence, and poses a serious threat to the native weta population.
pre: 這是一篇介紹特殊昆蟲的科普文。讀的時候留意牠的外表、習性，以及為什麼需要保護。
gist: 紐西蘭特有的沙螽外表醜陋，被取名為「醜神」。
牠們夜行、體型大、壽命長，也能摩擦腳發聲。
牠們因老鼠被引進而面臨威脅，需要保護。

(C) 錯，是人們給昆蟲取的綽號。

qs.ev: Most people probably don’t feel sympathy for these endangered creatures, but they do need protecting.

why: (A) 錯，牠們動作緩慢。
(B) 錯，牠們夜行。
(C) 對。

qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

The dinosaur’s.
qs.hint: its 前面一句在講老鼠數量成為問題，原生物種不習慣誰的存在？
qs.ev: Since rats love to hunt and eat wetas, the rat population on the island has grown into a real problem for many of the native species that are unaccustomed to its presence

(B) 錯，沙螽是受害的原生物種。
(C) 錯，島是所在地不是造成問題者。
(D) 錯，恐龍是時間背景。
qs.strat: 字義與指涉題要回到該字前後句，看上下文的因果與對照。

zh: 在紐西蘭島上，有一種像蚱蜢的昆蟲，世界上其他地方都找不到。紐西蘭人給牠取了「weta」的綽號，這是毛利語，意思是「醜相之神」。不難理解為何有人會稱這種昆蟲為長相難看的蟲。大多數人看到這些笨重、行動緩慢的生物都覺得噁心。
沙螽是夜行性生物，只在天黑後才從洞穴和洞口出來。一隻巨沙螽可長到超過三英寸長，重達 1.5 盎司。巨沙螽一次可以跳高達兩英尺。有些住在樹上，有些住在洞穴裡。對昆蟲來說，牠們壽命很長，有些成蟲可活到兩年。就像牠們的親戚蚱蜢和蟋蟀一樣，沙螽能透過把腿的部位互相摩擦，或與下半身摩擦來「唱歌」。
大多數人大概不會同情這些瀕危的生物，但牠們確實需要保護。行動緩慢又笨拙的沙螽，從恐龍時代起就在島上，在沒有天敵的環境中演化並存活，直到老鼠隨著歐洲移民來到島上。由於老鼠愛獵食沙螽，島上的老鼠數量已成為許多不習慣其存在的原生物種的一大問題，也對原生沙螽族群構成嚴重威脅。
summary: 沙螽外表醜、夜行、壽命長，但因入侵的老鼠而瀕危，需要保護。

title: 美國高中畢業舞會
text: The high school prom is the first formal social event for most American teenagers. It has also been a rite of passage for young Americans for nearly a century.

The word “prom” was first used in the 1890s, referring to formal dances in which the guests of a party would display their fashions and dancing skills during the evening’s grand march. In the United States, parents and educators have come to regard the prom as an important lesson in social skills. Therefore, proms have been held every year in high schools for students to learn proper social behavior.

The first high school proms were held in the 1920s in America. By the 1930s, proms were common across the country. For many older Americans, the prom was a modest, home-grown affair in the school gymnasium. Prom-goers were well dressed but not fancily dressed up for the occasion: boys wore jackets and ties and girls their Sunday dresses. Couples danced to music provided by a local amateur band or a record player. After the 1960s, and especially since the 1980s, the high school prom in many areas has become a serious exercise in excessive consumption, with boys renting expensive tuxedos and girls wearing designer gowns. Stretch limousines were hired to drive the prom-goers to expensive restaurants or discos for an all-night extravaganza.

Whether simple or lavish, proms have always been more or less traumatic events for adolescents who worry about self-image and fitting in with their peers. Prom night can be a dreadful experience for socially awkward teens or for those who do not secure dates. Since the 1990s, alternative proms have been organized in some areas to meet the needs of particular students. For example, proms organized by and for homeless youth were reported. There were also “couple-free” proms to which all students are welcome.
pre: 這篇介紹美國高中舞會的意義、演變與新型態。讀的時候留意時間線（1890s、1920s、1960s/80s、1990s）。

(D) 錯，1890 年代是 prom 一詞開始使用，不是高中舞會。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 高中畢業舞會是大多數美國青少年的第一場正式社交活動。它也已是美國年輕人的成年儀式將近一個世紀。
「prom」這個字最早在 1890 年代使用，指的是賓客在晚間的盛大遊行中展示服裝與舞技的正式舞會。在美國，家長和教育者逐漸把舞會視為社交技巧的重要一課。因此，高中每年都舉辦舞會，讓學生學習合宜的社交行為。

最早的高中舞會於 1920 年代在美國舉辦。到了 1930 年代，舞會已遍及全國。對許多年長的美國人而言，舞會是在學校體育館舉行的樸實、本地自辦的活動。參加者穿著得體，但並未為此盛裝打扮：男生穿外套打領帶，女生穿週日洋裝。舞伴們隨著當地業餘樂團或唱機播放的音樂跳舞。1960 年代之後，尤其是 1980 年代以來，許多地區的高中舞會變成嚴重的過度消費：男生租昂貴的晚禮服，女生穿設計師禮服。加長型禮車被租來載舞會參加者到昂貴的餐廳或迪斯可舞廳，進行通宵狂歡。
無論簡單或奢華，舞會對在意自我形象與合群的青少年而言，多少一直是令人壓力很大的場合。對於不善社交的青少年，或沒有找到舞伴的人，舞會之夜可能是很可怕的經驗。自 1990 年代起，一些地區開始舉辦另類舞會，以滿足特定學生的需求。例如曾有報導提到由無家可歸的青少年舉辦、也為他們而辦的舞會。也有歡迎所有學生參加的「不需伴侶」舞會。
summary: 文章說明舞會的起源與社交教育意義，從樸實變奢華，也因壓力與需求差異而出現另類舞會。

title: 房屋交換度假
text: No budget for your vacation? Try home exchanges－swapping houses with strangers. Agree to use each other’s cars, and you can save bucks on car rentals, too.

Home exchanges are not new. At least one group, Intervac, has been facilitating such an arrangement since 1953. But trading online is gaining popularity these days, with several sites in operation, including HomeExchanges. Founded in 1992, with some 28,000 listings, this company bills itself as the world’s largest home exchange club, reporting that membership has increased 30% this year.

The annual fee is usually less than US$100. Members can access thousands of listings for apartments, villas, suburban homes and farms around the world. Initial contact is made via e-mail, with subsequent communication usually by phone. Before a match is made, potential swappers tend to discuss a lot.

However, the concept may sound risky to some people. What about theft? Damage? These are reasonable causes for concern, but equally unlikely. As one swapper puts it, “Nobody is going to fly across the ocean or drive 600 miles to come steal your TV. Besides, at the same time they’re staying in your home, you are staying in their home.”

Exchange sites recommend that swappers discuss such matters ahead of time. They may fill out an agreement spelling out who shoulders which responsibilities if a problem arises. It does not matter if the agreement would hold up in court, but it does give the exchangers a little satisfaction.

Generally, the biggest complaint among home exchangers has to do with different standards of cleanliness. Swappers are supposed to make sure their home is in order before they depart, but one person’s idea of “clean” may be more forgiving than another’s. Some owners say if they come back to a less-than-sparkling kitchen, it may be inconvenient but would not sour them on future exchanges.
pre: 這篇介紹換屋度假的方式、風險與最常見的抱怨。每段各有重點，讀時用一句話記住各段主題。
gist: 沒預算度假可試試換屋，連車也可互用。
換屋早已有，近年線上網站愈來愈流行，HomeExchanges 自稱最大。
會員費不高，先用電子郵件聯絡，再用電話溝通。
有人擔心失竊與損壞，但可能性低，因為雙方互相住對方家。
網站建議事先討論並簽協議，說明責任歸屬。
最大的抱怨是清潔標準不同，但通常不影響下次交換。

qs.s: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
o: How to exchange homes.
How home exchange is becoming popular.
The biggest home exchange agency.
A contrast between Intervac and HomeExchange.
qs.hint: 看第 2 段的轉折詞 But，以及成長數字。
qs.ev: But trading online is gaining popularity these days, with several sites in operation, including HomeExchanges.
qs.ex: 本段先說換屋不新，再說線上交易日益流行，並舉會員成長 30% 為證。
why: (A) 錯，具體步驟在第 3 段。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，只是舉例，不是主題。
(D) 錯，沒有對比。
qs.strat: 段落主旨題看轉折詞後的重點，排除只是舉例的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “bills” in the second paragraph?
o: advertises
dedicates
replaces
participates
qs.hint: bills itself as 後面接的是公司宣稱的內容，是自稱、宣傳。
qs.ev: this company bills itself as the world’s largest home exchange club
qs.ex: bill oneself as 是「自稱為、宣傳為」，意思最接近 advertises。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，dedicate 是奉獻。
(C) 錯，replace 是取代。
(D) 錯，participate 是參與。
qs.strat: 字義與指涉題要回到該字前後句，看上下文的因果與對照。

qs.s: How do home exchangers normally begin their communication?
o: By phone.
By e-mail.
Via a matchmaker.
Via a face-to-face meeting.
qs.hint: 第 3 段說明 Initial contact。
qs.ev: Initial contact is made via e-mail, with subsequent communication usually by phone.
qs.ex: 最初聯絡是透過電子郵件，之後才打電話。
why: (A) 錯，電話是後續。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，沒有媒人。
(D) 錯，沒有面對面。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What is recommended in the passage to deal with theft and damage concerns?
o: One can file a lawsuit in court.
Both parties can trade online.
Both parties can sign an agreement beforehand.
One can damage the home of the other party in return.
qs.hint: 第 5 段的 recommend 與 agreement。
qs.ev: They may fill out an agreement spelling out who shoulders which responsibilities if a problem arises.
qs.ex: 網站建議先討論並填寫協議，載明出問題時誰負責。
why: (A) 錯，文中說協議不一定有法律效力。
(B) 錯，線上交易與防範無關。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，不合理。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

zh: 假期沒預算？試試換屋吧：和陌生人互換房子。如果同意互用對方的車，還能省下租車費。
換屋並不新鮮。至少有一個團體 Intervac 自 1953 年起就在促成這樣的安排。但近來網路交易愈來愈受歡迎，有好幾個網站在營運，包括 HomeExchanges。這家公司成立於 1992 年，有約 28,000 筆房源，自稱是全世界最大的換屋俱樂部，並表示今年會員數增加了 30%。
年費通常不到一百美元。會員可以瀏覽全世界數千筆公寓、別墅、郊區住宅與農場的房源。最初的聯絡是透過電子郵件，後續溝通通常用電話。在配對成功之前，潛在的換屋者往往會討論很多。
然而，這個概念對某些人來說可能聽起來有風險。失竊怎麼辦？損壞呢？這些是合理的擔憂，但發生的機率同樣很低。如一位換屋者所說：「沒有人會飛越大洋或開 600 英里的車來偷你的電視。而且，他們住在你家的同時，你也住在他們家。」
換屋網站建議換屋者事先討論這類事項。他們可以填寫一份協議，載明萬一出問題時由誰承擔哪些責任。協議在法庭上是否有效並不重要，但它確實能給換屋者一點安心。
一般來說，換屋者最大的抱怨與清潔標準不同有關。換屋者應該在離開前把家整理好，但一個人對「乾淨」的標準可能比另一個人寬鬆。有些屋主說，如果回家時廚房不是亮晶晶的，雖然不方便，但也不會讓他們對未來的換屋感到掃興。
summary: 換屋是省錢的度假方式，線上日益流行；風險可靠事前討論與協議處理，最大問題只是清潔標準不同。

title: 衣索比亞貝科吉的長跑奇蹟
genre: 說明文・人物與地方報導
text: Bekoji is a small town of farmers and herders in the Ethiopian highlands. There, time almost stands still, and horse-drawn carts outnumber motor vehicles. Yet, it has consistently yielded many of the world’s best distance runners.

It’s tempting, when breathing the thin air of Bekoji, to focus on the special conditions of the place. The town sits on the side of a volcano nearly 10,000 feet above sea level, making daily life a kind of high-altitude training. Children in this region often start running at an early age, covering great distances to fetch water and firewood or to reach the nearest school. Added to this early training is a physical trait shared by people there－disproportionately long legs, which is advantageous for distance runners.

A strong desire burns inside Bekoji’s young runners. Take the case of Million Abate. Forced to quit school in fifth grade after his father died, Abate worked as a shoe-shine boy for years. He saw a hope in running and joined Santayehu Eshetu’s training program. This 18-year-old sprinted to the finish of a 12-mile run with his bare feet bleeding. The coach took off his own Nikes and handed them to him. To help Abate continue running, the coach arranged a motel job for him, which pays $9 a month.

Most families in Bekoji live from hand to mouth, and distance running offers the younger generation a way out. Bekoji’s legend Derartu Tulu, who won the 10,000-meter Olympic gold medals in 1992 and 2000, is a national hero. As a reward, the government gave her a house. She also won millions of dollars in the races.

Motivated by such signs of success, thousands of kids from the villages surrounding Bekoji have moved into town. They crowd the classrooms at Bekoji Elementary School, where Eshetu works as a physical-education instructor. All these kids share the same dream: Some day they could become another Derartu Tulu.
pre: 這篇報導一個小鎮為何出長跑好手。讀的時候分辨「環境條件」與「個人動力」，並留意人物例子。
gist: 貝科吉是衣索比亞高地的小鎮，卻出了許多世界級長跑選手。
高海拔、從小長距離跑步與較長的腿是有利條件。
年輕人強烈渴望成功，如 Million Abate 的故事。
長跑能讓貧困家庭脫離困境，Derartu Tulu 是榜樣。
許多孩子搬到鎮上，夢想成為下一個 Derartu Tulu。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a factor for the excellence of distance runners in Ethiopia?
o: Well-known coaches.
Thin air in the highlands.
Extraordinarily long legs.
Long distance running in daily life.
qs.hint: 第 2 段列出三項因素，逐項對照；注意題目是 NOT。
qs.ev: The town sits on the side of a volcano nearly 10,000 feet above sea level, making daily life a kind of high-altitude training.
qs.ex: 文中提到高海拔稀薄空氣、日常長距離跑步、較長的腿，但沒有把知名教練當作因素。
why: (A) 對，文中未列為因素。
(B) 錯，有提到。
(C) 錯，有提到。
(D) 錯，有提到。
qs.strat: 遇到 NOT 題，把有提到的選項逐一劃掉，剩下沒提到的就是答案。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Bekoji?
o: It’s the capital of Ethiopia.
It has changed a lot over the years.
It’s located near a volcano.
It has trouble handling car accidents.
qs.hint: 第 2 段描述城鎮位置。
qs.ev: The town sits on the side of a volcano nearly 10,000 feet above sea level
qs.ex: 貝科吉位於火山的山坡上，所以靠近火山。
why: (A) 錯，是小鎮。
(B) 錯，文中說時間幾乎靜止。
(C) 對。
(D) 錯，沒提。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What is the goal of Bekoji’s school kids?
o: To work as motel managers.
To win in international competitions.
To become PE teachers.
To perform well academically at school.
qs.hint: 最後一段說明孩子們共同的夢想。
qs.ev: All these kids share the same dream: Some day they could become another Derartu Tulu.
qs.ex: 孩子們想成為像 Derartu Tulu 一樣的奧運冠軍，也就是在國際比賽中獲勝。
why: (A) 錯，那是 Abate 的工作。
(B) 對。
(C) 錯，Eshetu 才是體育老師。
(D) 錯，沒提學業目標。
qs.strat: 細節題先用題目關鍵字回文章定位，再逐字比對選項，注意數字與否定詞。

qs.s: What can be inferred from this passage?
o: More distance runners may emerge from Bekoji.
Nike will sponsor the young distance runners in Bekoji.
Bekoji will host an international long-distance competition.
The Ethiopian government has spared no efforts in promoting running.
qs.hint: 看最後兩段：成功示範激勵孩子湧入鎮上。
qs.ev: Motivated by such signs of success, thousands of kids from the villages surrounding Bekoji have moved into town.
qs.ex: 成千上萬孩子受鼓舞搬來，可推知未來可能出現更多長跑好手。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 錯，Nike 只是教練的鞋。
(C) 錯，沒提。
(D) 錯，只說給冠軍一棟房子，不能推論全力推動。
qs.strat: 推論題要根據文中明確的線索往前一步，不能憑自己的想像。

zh: 貝科吉是衣索比亞高地的農民與牧民小鎮。那裡時間幾乎靜止，馬車比機動車還多。然而，它一直持續培育出許多世界最優秀的長跑選手。
在貝科吉呼吸著稀薄的空氣，很容易讓人把注意力放在當地的特殊條件上。這個小鎮位於一座火山的山坡上，海拔將近一萬英尺，使日常生活成為一種高海拔訓練。這個地區的孩子常常很小就開始跑步，為了取水和柴火，或到最近的學校，要跑很長的距離。除了這種早期訓練，當地人還有一個共同的身體特徵：腿特別長，這對長跑選手很有利。
貝科吉的年輕跑者心中燃燒著強烈的渴望。以 Million Abate 為例。父親過世後，他被迫在五年級輟學，當了好幾年擦鞋童。他在跑步中看見希望，加入了 Santayehu Eshetu 的訓練計畫。這位 18 歲的年輕人赤腳流著血，衝刺跑完 12 英里。教練脫下自己的 Nike 鞋遞給他。為了幫助 Abate 繼續跑步，教練替他安排了一份汽車旅館的工作，月薪 9 美元。
貝科吉大多數家庭勉強餬口，長跑為年輕一代提供一條出路。貝科吉的傳奇人物 Derartu Tulu 在 1992 年和 2000 年贏得奧運一萬公尺金牌，是國家英雄。作為獎勵，政府送給她一棟房子。她在比賽中也贏得數百萬美元。
受到這些成功跡象的激勵，貝科吉周圍村莊的數千名孩子搬進了鎮上。他們擠滿貝科吉小學的教室，Eshetu 在那裡擔任體育老師。這些孩子都有相同的夢想：有一天，他們也能成為另一個 Derartu Tulu。
summary: 貝科吉的長跑傳統來自高海拔、日常跑步與身體特徵，更來自擺脫貧困的渴望與成功榜樣，吸引孩子追夢。

title: 肢體語言的常見迷思
text: There is a long-held belief that when meeting someone, the more eye contact we have with the person, the better. The result is an unfortunate tendency for people making initial contact—in a job interview, for example—to stare fixedly at the other individual. However, this behavior is likely to make the interviewer feel very uncomfortable. Most of us are comfortable with eye contact lasting a few seconds. But eye contact which persists longer than that can make us nervous.

Another widely accepted belief is that powerful people in a society—often men—show their dominance over others by touching them in a variety of ways. In fact, research shows that in almost all cases, lower-status people initiate touch. Women also initiate touch more often than men do.

The belief that rapid speech and lying go together is also widespread and enduring. We react strongly—and suspiciously—to fast talk. However, the opposite is a greater cause for suspicion. Speech that is slow, because it is laced with pauses or errors, is a more reliable indicator of lying than the opposite.
pre: 這篇在破除三個關於非語言溝通的「常識」：眼神接觸、碰觸、說話速度。讀的時候留意每段開頭的 belief，以及 However / In fact 之後的反轉。
gist: 人們以為眼神接觸越多越好，但太久反而讓人緊張。
常認為有權勢者會用碰觸展現支配，但研究顯示多半是地位較低者主動碰觸。
常認為說話快就是說謊，其實說話緩慢、夾雜停頓與錯誤才更可疑。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?
o: Rapid speech without mistakes is a reliable sign of intelligence.
Women often play a more dominant role than men in a community.
Speaking slowly is more often a sign of lying than speaking quickly.
Touching tends to be initiated first by people of higher social positions.
qs.hint: 看選項裡的 slowly / quickly，回第 3 段找 lying 的相關句。
qs.ev: Speech that is slow, because it is laced with pauses or errors, is a more reliable indicator of lying than the opposite.
qs.ex: 第 3 段說，夾雜停頓或錯誤的緩慢說話，比快速說話更能可靠指出說謊，所以選 (C)。
why: (A) 文中沒有說無誤的快速說話代表聰明。
(B) 文中說女性更常主動碰觸，不是更具支配力。
(C) 正確：慢速說話較常是說謊的徵象。
(D) 與第 2 段相反，主動碰觸的多是地位較低者。
qs.strat: True 題逐一把選項關鍵詞對回原文段落，注意是否被文意反轉。

qs.s: What is true about fixing your eyes on a person when you first meet him/her?
o: Fixing your eyes on the person will make him/her feel at ease.
It is more polite to fix your eyes on him/her as long as you can.
Most people feel uneasy to have eye contact for over a few seconds.
It doesn’t make a difference whether you fix your eyes on him/her or not.
qs.hint: 回到第 1 段，找 a few seconds 附近的句子。
qs.ev: Most of us are comfortable with eye contact lasting a few seconds. But eye contact which persists longer than that can make us nervous.
qs.ex: 第 1 段指出大多數人只對持續幾秒的眼神接觸感到自在，更久就會緊張，所以 (C) 正確。
why: (A) 盯著對方會讓對方不自在，不是自在。
(B) 文中沒說盯越久越有禮貌。
(C) 正確：多數人對超過幾秒的眼神接觸感到不安。
(D) 文中明確指出有差別。
qs.strat: 細節題先定位段落，再確認選項是否與原文意思一致。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT discussed in the passage?
o: Facial expressions.
Physical contact.
Rate of speech.
Eye contact.
qs.hint: NOT 題：逐一確認三段談了哪些主題，找出沒出現的。
qs.ev: Another widely accepted belief is that powerful people in a society—often men—show their dominance over others by touching them in a variety of ways.
qs.ex: 文章談了眼神接觸（第 1 段）、碰觸／身體接觸（第 2 段）和說話速度（第 3 段），完全沒有談到臉部表情，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：臉部表情全文未提。
(B) 第 2 段談碰觸（physical contact）。
(C) 第 3 段談說話速度。
(D) 第 1 段談眼神接觸。
qs.strat: NOT 題把有提到的選項劃掉，剩下的就是答案。

qs.s: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: People have an instinct for interpreting non-verbal communication.
We should not judge the intention of a person by his body language.
A good knowledge of body language is essential for successful communication.
Common beliefs about verbal and non-verbal communication are not always correct.
qs.hint: 主旨題看首句與各段共通點：每段都先講一個 belief 再反駁。
qs.ev: There is a long-held belief that when meeting someone, the more eye contact we have with the person, the better.
qs.ex: 三段都是先提出一個普遍信念，再指出實際情況不同，所以主旨是關於語言與非語言溝通的常見看法不一定正確，選 (D)。
why: (A) 文中沒有談本能。
(B) 文章沒有叫人不要以肢體語言判斷他人。
(C) 文章沒有強調懂肢體語言對溝通成功必要。
(D) 正確：點出常見看法的錯誤。
qs.strat: 主旨題先看各段共通結構，排除過窄或文中沒提的選項。

zh: 長久以來有一種看法：初次見面時，與對方的眼神接觸越多越好。結果是，人們在初次接觸時（例如求職面試）往往不自覺地緊盯著對方。然而，這種行為很可能讓面試官覺得非常不自在。我們大多數人對持續幾秒鐘的眼神接觸都覺得自在，但如果超過這個時間，就會讓我們緊張。
另一個廣被接受的看法是：社會中有權勢的人（通常是男性）會以各種方式碰觸他人來展現對他人的支配。事實上，研究顯示在幾乎所有情況下，都是地位較低的人主動碰觸；女性主動碰觸的次數也比男性多。
認為說話快與說謊有關，也是一種普遍而持久的看法。我們對說話快的人反應強烈而且帶著懷疑。然而，相反的情況才更令人起疑。因為夾雜停頓或錯誤而變得緩慢的說話方式，比說話快更能可靠地顯示說謊。
summary: 全文以三個「常見看法」逐段破除：眼神、碰觸、語速，每段都是先提迷思、再用事實反駁。主旨是關於語言與非語言溝通的常見看法不一定正確。

title: 大象如何分辨敵友
text: It is easy for us to tell our friends from our enemies. But can other animals do the same? Elephants can! They can use their sense of vision and smell to tell the difference between people who pose a threat and those who do not.

In Kenya, researchers found that elephants react differently to clothing worn by men of the Maasai and Kamba ethnic groups. Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants; Kamba men are mainly farmers and are not a danger to elephants.

In an experiment conducted by animal scientists, elephants were first presented with clean clothing or clothing that had been worn for five days by either a Maasai or a Kamba man. When the elephants detected the smell of clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away from the smell faster and took longer to relax than when they detected the smells of either clothing worn by Kamba men or clothing that had not been worn at all.

Garment color also plays a role, though in a different way. In the same study, when the elephants saw red clothing not worn before, they reacted angrily, as red is typically worn by Maasai men. Rather than running away as they did with the smell, the elephants acted aggressively toward the red clothing.

The researchers believe that the elephants’ emotional reactions are due to their different interpretations of the smells and the sights. Smelling a potential danger means that a threat is nearby and the best thing to do is run away and hide. Seeing a potential threat without its smell means that risk is low. Therefore, instead of showing fear and running away, the elephants express their anger and become aggressive.
pre: 這篇介紹一項大象實驗：牠們靠氣味和視覺辨別威脅。注意氣味與顏色各引發什麼不同反應，以及最後一段的原因解釋。
gist: 大象能用視覺和嗅覺分辨有威脅與無威脅的人。
在肯亞，大象對馬賽族與坎巴族的衣物反應不同，因為馬賽青年會獵殺動物。
實驗中，大象聞到馬賽人穿過的衣物會更快走開、更久才放鬆。
看到未穿過的紅色衣物時，大象反而憤怒、具攻擊性，因為紅色是馬賽人常穿的顏色。
研究者認為差異來自對氣味與視覺的不同解讀：聞到代表危險就在附近，只看到則風險低。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Kamba and Maasai people?
o: Maasai people are a threat to elephants.
Kamba people raise elephants for farming.
Both Kamba and Maasai people are elephant hunters.
Both Kamba and Maasai people traditionally wear red clothing.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，看 Maasai 與 Kamba 各自做什麼。
qs.ev: Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants; Kamba men are mainly farmers and are not a danger to elephants.
qs.ex: 第 2 段說年輕馬賽男性獵殺動物，對大象構成威脅；坎巴人是農夫，不是威脅，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：馬賽人對大象構成威脅。
(B) 坎巴人是農夫，沒有飼養大象。
(C) 坎巴人不是獵人。
(D) 文中只說紅色通常是馬賽人穿的。
qs.strat: 細節題對照原文，留意被偷換的人物或動作。

qs.s: How did the elephants react to smell in the study?
o: They attacked a man with the smell of new clothing.
They needed time to relax when smelling something unfamiliar.
They became anxious when they smelled Kamba-scented clothing.
They were frightened and ran away when they smelled their enemies.
qs.hint: 找第 3 段氣味實驗的結果，以及最後一段的解釋。
qs.ev: When the elephants detected the smell of clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away from the smell faster and took longer to relax than when they detected the smells of either clothing worn by Kamba men or clothing that had not been worn at all.
qs.ex: 大象聞到馬賽人的氣味會快速走開、較晚放鬆，最後一段更說聞到危險就逃跑，所以牠們是被敵人氣味嚇到逃走，選 (D)。
why: (A) 攻擊的是看到的紅色衣物，不是聞到新衣物的氣味。
(B) 放鬆較久是因為馬賽人氣味，不是陌生氣味。
(C) 對坎巴氣味沒有焦慮反應。
(D) 正確：聞到威脅氣味就害怕逃跑。
qs.strat: 注意題目限定 smell，勿與顏色（視覺）反應混淆。

qs.s: What is the main idea of this passage?
o: Elephants use sight and smell to detect danger.
Elephants attack people who wear red clothing.
Scientists are now able to control elephants’ emotions.
Some Kenyan tribes understand elephants’ emotions very well.
qs.hint: 主旨題看首段末句與全文：重點是用兩種感官偵測危險。
qs.ev: They can use their sense of vision and smell to tell the difference between people who pose a threat and those who do not.
qs.ex: 首段點出大象用視覺與嗅覺辨別有威脅的人，其後各段以實驗說明，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：大象用視覺與嗅覺偵測危險。
(B) 只是細節，且並非攻擊所有穿紅衣的人。
(C) 文中沒說科學家能控制大象情緒。
(D) 文中沒討論部落對大象情緒的了解。
qs.strat: 主旨題選能涵蓋全文的選項，排除過窄或未提及者。

qs.s: What can be inferred about the elephant’s behavior from this passage?
o: Elephants learn from their experiences.
Elephants have sharper sense of smell than sight.
Elephants are more intelligent than other animals.
Elephants tend to attack rather than escape when in danger.
qs.hint: 推論題要找實驗中大象反應差異的原因：牠們依過去經驗連結氣味與顏色。
qs.ev: In the same study, when the elephants saw red clothing not worn before, they reacted angrily, as red is typically worn by Maasai men.
qs.ex: 大象對從沒穿過的紅衣也生氣，是因為紅色與馬賽人連在一起，顯示牠們從經驗中學到這種連結，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：大象能從經驗學習。
(B) 文中沒有比較嗅覺與視覺誰更敏銳。
(C) 文中沒有說大象比其他動物聰明。
(D) 對氣味是逃跑，並非傾向攻擊。
qs.strat: 推論題答案要有文中證據支撐，避免過度延伸。

zh: 我們很容易分辨朋友與敵人，但其他動物也能做到嗎？大象可以！牠們能用視覺和嗅覺分辨會構成威脅的人與不會的人。
在肯亞，研究人員發現大象對馬賽族與坎巴族男性所穿的衣物反應不同。年輕的馬賽男性會用矛獵殺動物，因此對大象構成威脅；坎巴男性主要是農夫，對大象沒有危險。
在動物科學家進行的一項實驗中，先讓大象接觸乾淨的衣物，或是馬賽或坎巴男性穿過五天的衣物。當大象聞到馬賽男性穿過的衣物氣味時，比起聞到坎巴男性穿過的衣物或完全沒穿過的衣物，牠們離開那氣味的速度更快，也需要更久才放鬆下來。
衣服的顏色也扮演一個角色，只是方式不同。在同一項研究中，當大象看到沒穿過的紅色衣物時，牠們憤怒地反應，因為紅色通常是馬賽男性穿的顏色。牠們不是像對氣味那樣逃跑，而是對紅色衣物表現出攻擊性。
研究人員相信，大象的情緒反應源自對氣味與視覺的不同解讀。聞到潛在的危險代表威脅就在附近，最好的做法是逃跑躲藏。看到潛在威脅卻沒有氣味，則表示風險低。因此，大象不是表現恐懼和逃跑，而是表達憤怒並變得具攻擊性。
summary: 文章先提出大象能辨敵友，再用肯亞實驗說明氣味引發逃避、紅色引發攻擊，最後解釋兩種反應源於對危險程度的不同判斷。

title: 受傷球員的新方向
text: It was something she had dreamed of since she was five. Finally, after years of training and intensive workouts, Deborah Duffey was going to compete in her first high school basketball game. The goals of becoming an outstanding player and playing college ball were never far from Deborah’s mind.

The game was against Mills High School. With 1:42 minutes left in the game, Deborah’s team led by one point. A player of Mills had possession of the ball, and Deborah ran to guard against her. As Deborah shuffled sideways to block the player, her knee went out and she collapsed on the court in burning pain. Just like that, Deborah’s season was over.

After suffering the bad injury, Deborah found that, for the first time in her life, she was in a situation beyond her control. Game after game, she could do nothing but sit on the sidelines watching others play the game that she loved so much.

Injuries limited Deborah’s time on the court as she hurt her knees three more times in the next five years. She had to spend countless hours in a physical therapy clinic to receive treatment. Her frequent visits there gave her a passion and respect for the profession. And Deborah began to see a new light in her life.

Currently a senior in college, Deborah focuses on pursuing a degree in physical therapy. After she graduates, Deborah plans to use her knowledge to educate people how to best take care of their bodies and cope with the feelings of hopelessness that she remembers so well.
pre: 這是一篇人物故事，按時間順序敘述一位籃球員受傷後的轉變。讀的時候注意她的心情變化與最後的人生新目標。
gist: 黛博拉從五歲起夢想打籃球，終於要打第一場高中比賽。
比賽中她的膝蓋受傷倒地，球季就此結束。
她第一次面對無法掌控的處境，只能在場邊看別人打球。
之後五年又傷了三次膝蓋，因常去物理治療診所而對這個行業產生熱情與敬意。
她現在主修物理治療，打算教人照顧身體並面對絕望感。

qs.s: What is the best title for this passage?
o: A Painful Mistake
A Great Adventure
A Lifelong Punishment
A New Direction in Life
qs.hint: 標題要概括全文，看結尾的 new light 與最後一段的規劃。
qs.ev: And Deborah began to see a new light in her life.
qs.ex: 故事從受傷轉到她在物理治療中找到新目標，所以最佳標題是「人生的新方向」(D)。
why: (A) 受傷是意外，不是錯誤。
(B) 全文不是冒險故事。
(C) 傷並非一生的懲罰。
(D) 正確：呼應 new light 與未來規劃。
qs.strat: 標題題選能涵蓋全文轉折的選項，排除過窄或誇大者。

qs.s: How did Deborah feel when she first hurt her knee?
o: Excited.
Confused.
Ashamed.
Disappointed.
qs.hint: 找第 2、3 段，受傷時與之後的心情描述。
qs.ev: Game after game, she could do nothing but sit on the sidelines watching others play the game that she loved so much.
qs.ex: 她夢想多年的比賽卻在第一場就受傷，只能在場邊看別人打球，這顯示她感到失望，選 (D)。
why: (A) 不是興奮。
(B) 文中沒有困惑的描述。
(C) 沒有羞愧的線索。
(D) 正確：夢想受挫的失望。
qs.strat: 情緒題從情境與行為推論心情，不要只看單字。

qs.s: What is true about Deborah Duffey?
o: She didn’t play on the court after the initial injury.
She injured her knee when she was trying to block her opponent.
She knew that she couldn’t be a basketball player when she was a child.
She refused to seek professional assistance to help her recover from her injuries.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，找受傷發生的情境。
qs.ev: As Deborah shuffled sideways to block the player, her knee went out and she collapsed on the court in burning pain.
qs.ex: 第 2 段說她在側滑步阻擋對手時膝蓋受傷，所以選 (B)。
why: (A) 她之後仍坐在場邊，但文中未說完全沒上過場。
(B) 正確：防守對手時受傷。
(C) 她五歲就夢想打球，不是知道自己不能。
(D) 她接受了物理治療。
qs.strat: True 題把每個選項回原文核對，找最確切的一項。

qs.s: What was the new light that Deborah saw in her life?
o: To help people take care of their bodies.
To become a teacher of Physical Education.
To become an outstanding basketball player.
To receive treatment in a physical therapy office.
qs.hint: 找 new light 後面或最後一段的具體計畫。
qs.ev: After she graduates, Deborah plans to use her knowledge to educate people how to best take care of their bodies and cope with the feelings of hopelessness that she remembers so well.
qs.ex: 新曙光指她要運用物理治療的知識，教導人們照顧身體，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：幫助人們照顧身體。
(B) 文中沒說要當體育老師。
(C) 這是她原本的夢想。
(D) 接受治療是過程，不是新目標。
qs.strat: 指涉題找前後文對應的具體內容。

zh: 這是她從五歲起就夢想的事。經過多年的訓練與密集鍛鍊，黛博拉．達菲終於要參加她的第一場高中籃球比賽了。成為傑出球員並打大學籃球的目標，從來沒有離開過黛博拉的心。
比賽對手是米爾斯高中。比賽剩下一分四十二秒時，黛博拉的球隊領先一分。米爾斯的一名球員持球，黛博拉跑去防守她。當黛博拉側滑步想阻擋那名球員時，她的膝蓋一軟，在球場上倒下，劇痛難耐。就這樣，黛博拉的球季結束了。
遭遇嚴重傷害後，黛博拉發現自己生平第一次處於無法掌控的處境。一場又一場比賽，她只能坐在場邊，看著別人打她如此熱愛的比賽。
傷病限制了黛博拉在球場上的時間，因為接下來五年她又傷了三次膝蓋。她必須花無數時間在物理治療診所接受治療。頻繁造訪那裡讓她對這個職業產生熱情與敬意，黛博拉也開始在生命中看到新的曙光。
黛博拉目前是大學四年級生，專注於攻讀物理治療學位。畢業後，她打算運用所學教導人們如何好好照顧身體，並面對她記憶猶新的絕望感。
summary: 全文依時間順序，從夢想打球、膝蓋受傷、長期復健，到發現物理治療這個新人生方向，說明挫折也能帶來轉變。

title: 紅杉的長壽祕密
text: Redwood trees are the tallest plants on the earth, reaching heights of up to 100 meters. They are also known for their longevity, typically 500 to 1000 years, but sometimes more than 2000 years. A hundred million years ago, in the age of dinosaurs, redwoods were common in the forests of a much more moist and tropical North America. As the climate became drier and colder, they retreated to a narrow strip along the Pacific coast of Northern California.

The trunk of redwood trees is very stout and usually forms a single straight column. It is covered with a beautiful soft, spongy bark. This bark can be pretty thick, well over two feet in the more mature trees. It gives the older trees a certain kind of protection from insects, but the main benefit is that it keeps the center of the tree intact from moderate forest fires because of its thickness. This fire resistant quality explains why the giant redwood grows to live that long. While most other types of trees are destroyed by forest fires, the giant redwood actually prospers because of them. Moderate fires will clear the ground of competing plant life, and the rising heat dries and opens the ripe cones of the redwood, releasing many thousands of seeds onto the ground below.

New trees are often produced from sprouts, little baby trees, which form at the base of the trunk. These sprouts grow slowly, nourished by the root system of the “mother” tree. When the main tree dies, the sprouts are then free to grow as full trees, forming a “fairy ring” of trees around the initial tree. These trees, in turn, may give rise to more sprouts, and the cycle continues.
pre: 這篇介紹紅杉的生長特性。留意它為什麼能活很久，以及它如何繁殖新樹。
gist: 紅杉是最高的植物、壽命很長，曾廣布北美，後來退到加州北部海岸。
厚樹皮保護樹木免於蟲害與中度森林大火，火反而使紅杉受益，因此長壽。
新樹常由主樹基部的嫩芽長成，主樹死後形成「仙女環」並循環繁殖。

qs.s: Why were redwood trees more prominent in the forests of North America millions of years ago?
o: The trees were taller and stronger.
The soil was softer for seeds to sprout.
The climate was warmer and more humid.
The temperature was lower along the Pacific coast.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段，看一億年前的氣候描述。
qs.ev: A hundred million years ago, in the age of dinosaurs, redwoods were common in the forests of a much more moist and tropical North America.
qs.ex: 當時北美更潮濕、更熱帶，紅杉才很常見，所以選氣候較溫暖濕潤的 (C)。
why: (A) 文中沒比較樹的高度與強壯。
(B) 沒提土壤。
(C) 正確：氣候較暖、較濕。
(D) 後來氣候才變冷，沿海是退縮的地方。
qs.strat: 原因題找 why 對應的因果敘述。

qs.s: What does a “fairy ring” in the last paragraph refer to?
o: Circled tree trunks.
Connected root systems.
Insect holes around an old tree.
Young trees surrounding a mature tree.
qs.hint: 回最後一段，看 fairy ring 前面的句子。
qs.ev: When the main tree dies, the sprouts are then free to grow as full trees, forming a “fairy ring” of trees around the initial tree.
qs.ex: 主樹死後，嫩芽長成完整的樹，圍繞著最初那棵，形成仙女環，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 不是圍成圈的樹幹。
(B) 不是根系相連。
(C) 與蟲洞無關。
(D) 正確：年輕樹圍繞成熟樹。
qs.strat: 指涉題從引號詞彙前後句找定義。

qs.s: Which of the following is a function of the tree bark as mentioned in the passage?
o: It allows redwood trees to bear seeds.
It prevents redwood trees from attack by insects.
It helps redwood trees absorb moisture in the air.
It makes redwood trees more beautiful and appealing.
qs.hint: 找第 2 段 bark 的功能，注意 insects 與 fires。
qs.ev: It gives the older trees a certain kind of protection from insects, but the main benefit is that it keeps the center of the tree intact from moderate forest fires because of its thickness.
qs.ex: 文中說樹皮提供防蟲保護，所以選 (B)；其餘功能文中沒提。
why: (A) 結籽是靠火烘開毬果，不是樹皮。
(B) 正確：防止蟲害。
(C) 文中沒說吸收水氣。
(D) 美觀只是描述，不是功能。
qs.strat: 功能題要找文中明確說的作用，不選自行延伸的。

qs.s: Why do redwood trees grow to live that long according to the passage?
o: They have heavy and straight tree trunks.
They are properly watered and nourished.
They are more resistant to fire damage than other trees.
They produce many young trees to sustain their life cycle.
qs.hint: 找 live that long 這句。
qs.ev: This fire resistant quality explains why the giant redwood grows to live that long.
qs.ex: 文中直接說抗火的特質解釋了它們為何長壽，所以選 (C)。
why: (A) 粗壯筆直不是原因。
(B) 沒提澆水與養分為長壽原因。
(C) 正確：比其他樹更能抗火。
(D) 繁殖新樹不是長壽原因。
qs.strat: 原因題抓文中指示詞 This ... explains why。

zh: 紅杉是地球上最高的植物，高度可達一百公尺。它們也以長壽聞名，壽命通常是五百到一千年，有時超過兩千年。一億年前的恐龍時代，紅杉常見於氣候濕潤許多的熱帶北美森林。隨著氣候變得更乾更冷，它們退縮到北加州太平洋沿岸的一條狹長地帶。

紅杉的樹幹非常粗壯，通常形成單一筆直的柱狀。樹幹覆蓋著美麗、柔軟又有彈性的樹皮。這種樹皮可以很厚，在較成熟的樹上遠超過兩英尺。它讓較老的樹有某種程度的防蟲保護，但主要的好處是，因為夠厚，能使樹心不受中度森林大火的傷害。這種抗火特性解釋了巨大紅杉為何能活這麼久。大多數其他樹種會被森林大火摧毀，巨大紅杉卻反而因大火而繁盛。中度的火會清除地面上競爭的植物，而上升的熱氣會烘乾並打開紅杉成熟的毬果，將數千顆種子釋放到下方的地面上。
新樹常由嫩芽，也就是長在樹幹基部的小樹苗長成。這些嫩芽生長緩慢，由「母」樹的根系提供養分。當主樹死亡，嫩芽就能自由長成完整的樹，在最初那棵樹周圍形成一圈「仙女環」。這些樹接著又可能長出更多嫩芽，循環就這樣持續下去。
summary: 文章先介紹紅杉高大長壽的特性與分布變遷，再說明厚樹皮使其耐火長壽，最後描述嫩芽長成仙女環的繁殖方式。

title: 蘇格蘭裙介紹
text: The kilt is a skirt traditionally worn by Scottish men. It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side. The overlapping layers in front are called “aprons.” Usually, the kilt covers the body from the waist down to just above the knees. A properly made kilt should not be so loose that the wearer can easily twist the kilt around the body, nor should it be so tight that it causes bulging of the fabric where it is buckled. Underwear may be worn as one prefers.

One of the most distinctive features of the kilt is the pattern of squares, or sett, it exhibits. The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years. Then in the Victorian era (19th century), weaving companies began to systematically record and formalize the system of setts for commercial purposes. Today there are also setts for States and Provinces, schools and universities, and general patterns that anybody can wear.

The kilt can be worn with accessories. On the front apron, there is often a kilt pin, topped with a small decorative family symbol. A small knife can be worn with the kilt too. It typically comes in a very wide variety, from fairly plain to quite elaborate silver- and jewel-ornamented designs. The kilt can also be worn with a sporran, which is the Gaelic word for pouch or purse.
pre: 這篇介紹蘇格蘭傳統服飾 kilt。讀時分三塊整理：怎麼穿、格紋、配件。
gist: 蘇格蘭裙是蘇格蘭男性的傳統裙裝，圍繞腰部穿著，鬆緊要適中。
格紋是特色，起初與家族相關，維多利亞時期織造商將其系統化，今日也有地區、學校等格紋。
蘇格蘭裙可搭配別針、小刀與腰包等配件。

qs.s: What’s the proper way of wearing the kilt?
o: It should be worn with underwear underneath it.
It should loosely fit on the body to be turned around.
It should be long enough to cover the wearer’s knees.
It should be wrapped across the front of the body two times.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段，找 wrapped 的描述。
qs.ev: It is a tailored garment that is wrapped around the wearer’s body at the waist starting from one side, around the front and back and across the front again to the opposite side.
qs.ex: 裙子從一側繞前、後、再橫過前面到另一側，也就是前面包兩次，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 內衣是隨個人喜好。
(B) 不該鬆到能轉動。
(C) 只蓋到膝蓋上方，不是蓋住膝蓋。
(D) 正確：前面包兩次。
qs.strat: 細節題注意文中數量與位置描述。

qs.s: Which of the following is a correct description about setts?
o: They were once symbols for different Scottish families.
They were established by the government for business purposes.
They represented different States and Provinces in the 19th century.
They used to come in one general pattern for all individuals and institutions.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，看 sett 與家族的關係。
qs.ev: The association of particular patterns with individual families can be traced back hundreds of years.
qs.ex: 格紋與家族的關聯可追溯數百年，所以曾是不同蘇格蘭家族的象徵，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：曾是家族象徵。
(B) 是織造公司為商業目的記錄，不是政府。
(C) 州與省的格紋是今日才有。
(D) 並非一種通用圖案。
qs.strat: 留意時間詞（once, today）與主體是否被偷換。

qs.s: Which of the following items is NOT typically worn with the kilt for decoration?
o: A pin.
A purse.
A ruby apron.
A silver knife.
qs.hint: NOT 題：圍片 aprons 是裙子本身的一部分，不是配件。
qs.ev: The overlapping layers in front are called “aprons.”
qs.ex: 別針、腰包、銀刀都是裝飾配件，而 apron 是裙子前面重疊的布層，不是配件，所以選 (C)。
why: (A) 別針是配件。
(B) sporran 就是皮袋。
(C) 正確：apron 是裙子的一部分，且沒有 ruby。
(D) 銀飾小刀是配件。
qs.strat: NOT 題把有明確提到的剔除。

qs.s: What is the purpose of this passage?
o: To introduce a Scottish garment.
To advertise a weaving pattern.
To persuade men to wear kilts.
To compare a skirt with a kilt.
qs.hint: 看首句與全文功能：介紹一種服飾。
qs.ev: The kilt is a skirt traditionally worn by Scottish men.
qs.ex: 全文說明蘇格蘭裙的穿法、格紋與配件，目的是介紹一種蘇格蘭服飾，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：介紹蘇格蘭服飾。
(B) 沒有在推銷格紋。
(C) 沒有說服男性穿裙。
(D) 沒有比較裙子與蘇格蘭裙。
qs.strat: 寫作目的題看全文功能：介紹、說服、比較或廣告。

zh: 蘇格蘭裙是蘇格蘭男性傳統上穿的裙子。它是一件量身剪裁的衣服，從一側開始圍繞穿戴者腰部，經過前面、後面，再橫過前面到另一側。前面重疊的層次稱為「圍片」。通常裙子從腰部往下蓋到膝蓋上方一點。做得合適的蘇格蘭裙不應鬆到穿著者可以輕易將裙子在身上轉動，也不應緊到讓扣住的地方布料鼓起。內衣可依個人喜好穿著。
蘇格蘭裙最獨特的特色之一是它所呈現的方格圖案，即「sett」。特定圖案與個別家族的關聯可以追溯到數百年前。後來在維多利亞時代（十九世紀），織造公司開始為了商業目的有系統地記錄並將格紋制度正式化。今日也有州與省、學校與大學的格紋，以及任何人都可以穿的通用圖案。
蘇格蘭裙可以搭配配件穿戴。前面的圍片上常有一枚別針，頂端有小小的裝飾性家族符號。也可以佩戴一把小刀，它的款式通常極為多樣，從相當樸素到鑲有銀和珠寶的華麗設計都有。蘇格蘭裙也可以搭配 sporran，這是蓋爾語「小袋或錢包」的意思。
summary: 文章以介紹為目的，依序說明蘇格蘭裙的穿法、格紋的歷史與用途，以及常見配件。

title: 輪椅上的爵士歌手
text: Wesla Whitfield, a famous jazz singer, has a unique style and life story, so I decided to see one of her performances and interview her for my column.

I went to a nightclub in New York and watched the stage lights go up. After the band played an introduction, Wesla Whitfield wheeled herself onstage in a wheelchair. As she sang, Whitfield’s voice was so powerful and soulful that everyone in the room forgot the wheelchair was even there.

At 57, Whitfield is small and pretty, witty and humble, persistent and philosophical. Raised in California, Whitfield began performing in public at age 18, when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor. After studying classical music in college, she moved to San Francisco and went on to sing with the San Francisco Opera Chorus.

Walking home from rehearsal at age 29, she was caught in the midst of a random shooting that left her paralyzed from the waist down. I asked how she dealt with the realization that she’d never walk again, and she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it. After a year of depression she tried to kill herself. She was then admitted to a hospital for treatment, where she was able to recover.

Whitfield said she came to understand that the only thing she had lost in this misfortunate event was the ability to walk. She still possessed her most valuable asset—her mind. Pointing to her head, she said, “Everything important is in here. The only real disability in life is losing your mind.” When I asked if she was angry about what she had lost, she admitted to being frustrated occasionally, “especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance. But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.”
pre: 這是一篇專欄作者訪問爵士歌手的文章，以第一人稱寫成。注意她的經歷與最後一段她對失去的看法。
gist: 作者因歌手惠特菲爾德獨特的風格與人生，決定去看她演出並訪問。
她坐輪椅上台，歌聲強而有力，使人忘了輪椅。
57 歲的她早年唱歌打工、學古典音樂，並加入舊金山歌劇合唱團。
29 歲遭隨機槍擊而下半身癱瘓，一度憂鬱到自殺，後來住院康復。
她明白自己只失去行走能力，最珍貴的是心智；感到挫折時就專注於自己能做的事。

qs.s: In which of the following places has Wesla Whitfield worked?
o: A college.
A hospital.
A pizza parlor.
A news agency.
qs.hint: 找文中提到的工作地點。
qs.ev: Raised in California, Whitfield began performing in public at age 18, when she took a job as a singing waitress at a pizza parlor.
qs.ex: 她十八歲時在披薩店當唱歌服務生，所以選 (C)；醫院是治療地點，不是工作。
why: (A) 她在大學是學習，不是工作。
(B) 醫院是接受治療。
(C) 正確：披薩店工作。
(D) 作者才是專欄作家。
qs.strat: 注意題目問 worked，要區分工作與學習、治療。

qs.s: What does “when that happens” mean in the last paragraph?
o: When Wesla is losing her mind.
When Wesla is singing on the stage.
When Wesla is going out in her wheelchair.
When Wesla is watching other people dancing.
qs.hint: 回最後一段，找 when that happens 前面的情境。
qs.ev: especially when everybody’s dancing, because I love to dance.
qs.ex: that 指前面說的「大家都在跳舞」的時候，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 失去心智是她說的殘疾。
(B) 唱歌不會讓她挫折。
(C) 沒有提出門。
(D) 正確：看別人跳舞時。
qs.strat: 指涉題向前找最近的完整情境。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about Wesla Whitfield’s physical disability?
o: It was caused by a traffic accident.
It made her sad and depressed at first.
It seriously affected her singing career.
It happened when she was a college student.
qs.hint: 回第 4 段，看癱瘓的原因與當時反應。
qs.ev: I asked how she dealt with the realization that she’d never walk again, and she confessed that initially she didn’t want to face it. After a year of depression she tried to kill herself.
qs.ex: 癱瘓使她起初陷入憂鬱，所以選 (B)；原因是槍擊，不是車禍。
why: (A) 是隨機槍擊，不是車禍。
(B) 正確：起初悲傷憂鬱。
(C) 文中說她仍持續唱歌，沒有嚴重影響。
(D) 發生時她 29 歲，已大學畢業。
qs.strat: True 題逐項檢查，注意原因與時間點。

qs.s: What advice would Wesla most likely give other disabled people?
o: Ignore what you have lost and make the best use of what you have.
Be modest and hard-working to earn respect from other people.
Acquire a skill so that you can still be successful and famous.
Try to sing whenever you feel upset and depressed.
qs.hint: 推論她的建議：從最後一段她的態度反推。
qs.ev: But when that happens I just remove myself so I can focus instead on what I can do.
qs.ex: 她強調重要的在心智，並專注於自己還能做的事，所以建議是忽略失去的、善用擁有的，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：忽略失去、善用擁有。
(B) 文中沒有談尊重。
(C) 並非強調成功出名。
(D) 沒有說唱歌就能消愁。
qs.strat: 推論題從人物態度與話語歸納立場。

zh: 衛絲拉．惠特菲爾德是一位有名的爵士歌手，她有獨特的風格與人生故事，所以我決定去看她的一場演出，並為我的專欄訪問她。
我到了紐約的一家夜總會，看著舞台燈光亮起。樂團演奏完前奏後，惠特菲爾德坐著輪椅自己推上台。她唱歌時，聲音強而有力、深具靈魂，讓房間裡每個人都忘了輪椅的存在。
57 歲的惠特菲爾德嬌小而漂亮，機智又謙虛，堅持又富哲思。她在加州長大，十八歲時開始公開表演，當時在披薩店當唱歌的服務生。在大學學過古典音樂後，她搬到舊金山，繼續加入舊金山歌劇合唱團演唱。
二十九歲那年，她排練後走路回家時，捲入一場隨機的槍擊，導致她腰部以下癱瘓。我問她如何面對再也無法走路的事實，她坦承起初她不願面對。經過一年的憂鬱之後，她試圖自殺。她隨後被送進醫院治療，在那裡得以康復。
惠特菲爾德說，她逐漸明白，在這個不幸的事件中，她唯一失去的是行走的能力。她仍擁有最珍貴的資產，也就是她的心智。她指著頭說：「重要的一切都在這裡。人生唯一真正的殘疾是失去心智。」當我問她是否對失去的東西感到憤怒時，她承認偶爾會感到挫折，「尤其是大家都在跳舞的時候，因為我愛跳舞。但那種時候我就讓自己離開，這樣我就能專心在我能做的事上。」
summary: 文章透過一次訪問介紹歌手惠特菲爾德的經歷：從歌唱生涯、遭槍擊癱瘓到走出低潮，並以她面對失去的態度作結。

title: 叉子的歷史
text: Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks. Forks at that time were fairly large with two tines that aided in the carving of meat in the kitchen. The tines prevented meat from twisting or moving during carving and allowed food to slide off more easily than it would with a knife.

By the 7th century A.D., royal courts of the Middle East began to use forks at the table for dining. From the 10th through the 13th centuries, forks were fairly common among the wealthy in Byzantium. In the 11th century, a Byzantine wife brought forks to Italy; however, they were not widely adopted there until the 16th century. Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France. The French were also slow to accept forks, for using them was thought to be awkward.

In 1608, forks were brought to England by Thomas Coryate, who saw them during his travels in Italy. The English first ridiculed forks as being unnecessary. “Why should a person need a fork when God had given him hands?” they asked. Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status. They were prized possessions made of expensive materials intended to impress guests. By the mid 1600s, eating with forks was considered fashionable among the wealthy British.

Early table forks were modeled after kitchen forks, but small pieces of food often fell through the two tines or slipped off easily. In late 17th century France, larger forks with four curved tines were developed. The additional tines made diners less likely to drop food, and the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating. By the early 19th century, four-tined forks had also been developed in Germany and England and slowly began to spread to America.
pre: 這篇依時間順序說明叉子的傳播，請留意年代與地名，並圈出各地接受叉子的原因。
gist: 叉子起源於古希臘，是兩齒的大型廚房用具。
七世紀中東宮廷開始用叉進食，後來傳到義大利、法國，但都推廣緩慢。
1608 年傳到英國，起初被嘲笑，後來成為富人身分象徵。
十七世紀晚期法國發展出四齒彎曲叉子，之後傳到德國、英國與美國。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The different designs of forks.
The spread of fork-aided cooking.
The history of using forks for dining.
The development of fork-related table manners.
qs.hint: 主旨題看首句與各段時間線：整篇講叉子如何演變與傳播。
qs.ev: Forks trace their origins back to the ancient Greeks.
qs.ex: 全文依年代說明叉子的起源、傳播與設計演變，主題是用叉子進食的歷史，選 (C)。
why: (A) 設計只是部分內容。
(B) 重點是餐桌用叉，不是烹飪。
(C) 正確：用叉子用餐的歷史。
(D) 沒有談餐桌禮儀。
qs.strat: 主旨題找貫穿全文的線索，這裡是時間順序。

qs.s: By which route did the use of forks spread?
o: Middle East → Greece → England → Italy → France
Greece → Middle East → Italy → France → England
Greece → Middle East → France → Italy → Germany
Middle East → France → England → Italy → Germany
qs.hint: 依序追蹤地名：希臘、中東、義大利、法國、英國。
qs.ev: Then in 1533, forks were brought from Italy to France. The French were also slow to accept forks, for using them was thought to be awkward.
qs.ex: 路線是希臘、中東、義大利、法國，接著 1608 年義大利到英國（第 3 段），選項中只有 (B) 順序最符合。
why: (A) 順序錯誤。
(B) 正確：希臘、中東、義大利、法國、英國。
(C) 義大利應在法國之前。
(D) 起點應是希臘。
qs.strat: 路線題把地名按段落先後排序。

qs.s: How did forks become popular in England?
o: Wealthy British were impressed by the design of forks.
Wealthy British thought it awkward to use their hands to eat.
Wealthy British gave special forks to the nobles as luxurious gifts.
Wealthy British considered dining with forks a sign of social status.
qs.hint: 回第 3 段，找英國富人接受叉子的原因。
qs.ev: Slowly, however, forks came to be adopted by the wealthy as a symbol of their social status.
qs.ex: 英國富人把叉子視為社會地位的象徵，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 不是因為設計。
(B) 他們起初嘲笑叉子。
(C) 沒提送禮給貴族。
(D) 正確：叉子是地位象徵。
qs.strat: 原因題找 as a symbol of 之類的因果語。

qs.s: Why were forks made into a curved shape?
o: They could be used to scoop food as well.
They looked more fashionable in this way.
They were designed in this way for export to the US.
They ensured the meat would not twist while being cut.
qs.hint: 回最後一段，找 curved 的原因。
qs.ev: In late 17th century France, larger forks with four curved tines were developed. The additional tines made diners less likely to drop food, and the curved tines served as a scoop so people did not have to constantly switch to a spoon while eating.
qs.ex: 彎曲的叉齒可以像勺子一樣舀取食物，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：也能舀食物。
(B) 文中沒說是為了時髦。
(C) 沒有為了出口美國。
(D) 防止肉扭動是古希臘叉子的功能。
qs.strat: 留意題目問的是哪個時期的叉子。

zh: 叉子的起源可追溯到古希臘人。當時的叉子相當大，有兩根叉齒，用來協助在廚房切肉。叉齒能防止肉在切割時扭動或移動，也使食物比使用刀子時更容易滑下來。
