到了西元七世紀，中東的皇室宮廷開始在餐桌上使用叉子進食。從十世紀到十三世紀，叉子在拜占庭的富人之間相當常見。十一世紀時，一位拜占庭的妻子把叉子帶到義大利，然而直到十六世紀才在那裡被廣泛採用。接著在 1533 年，叉子從義大利被帶到法國。法國人也很慢才接受叉子，因為使用它被認為很笨拙。
1608 年，湯瑪斯．柯里亞特把叉子帶到英國，他是在義大利旅行時看到叉子的。英國人起初嘲笑叉子沒有必要。他們問：「上帝既然給了人手，人為什麼還需要叉子？」然而慢慢地，叉子被富人接納，成為社會地位的象徵。它們是珍貴的物品，以昂貴材料製成，意在讓賓客印象深刻。到了十七世紀中期，使用叉子吃飯在英國富人之間被視為時髦。
早期的餐叉仿照廚房叉子，但小塊食物常從兩根叉齒間掉落，或輕易滑落。十七世紀晚期的法國發展出較大、有四根彎曲叉齒的叉子。多出來的叉齒使用餐者較不易掉落食物，彎曲的叉齒又像勺子一樣，人們不必在進食時一直換用湯匙。到了十九世紀初，德國和英國也發展出四齒叉子，並慢慢傳到美國。
summary: 全文依時間與地點說明叉子從古希臘廚房到各國餐桌的傳播過程，並解釋英國的接受與四齒設計的由來。

title: 動物攝影小技巧
text: Animals are a favorite subject of many photographers. Cats, dogs, and other pets top the list, followed by zoo animals. However, because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.

One way to get an appealing portrait of a cat or dog is to hold a biscuit or treat above the camera. The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera, but the treat won’t appear in the picture because it’s out of the camera’s range. When you show the picture to your friends afterwards, they’ll be impressed by your pet’s loving expression.

If you are using fast film, you can take some good, quick shots of a pet by simply snapping a picture right after calling its name. You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique. Depending on your pet’s mood, the picture will capture an interested, curious expression or possibly a look of annoyance, especially if you’ve awakened it from a nap.

Taking pictures of zoo animals requires a little more patience. After all, you can’t wake up a lion! You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot. When photographing zoo animals, don’t get too close to the cages, and never tap on the glass or throw things between the bars of a cage. Concentrate on shooting some good pictures, and always respect the animals you are photographing.
pre: 這是一篇攝影教學文章。讀的時候找出每種情況（寵物、動物園）各給什麼建議與原因。
gist: 動物是熱門攝影題材，但因難以聽令表演，有些攝影師拒拍寵物。
用餅乾在相機上方引誘，可拍到寵物渴望的可愛表情。
用快速底片，在叫名字後立即拍，可捕捉好奇或惱怒的不同表情。
拍動物園動物需要更多耐心等待，且要保持距離、尊重動物。

qs.s: Why do some professional photographers NOT like to take pictures of pets?
o: Pets may not follow orders.
Pets don’t want to be bothered.
Pets may not like photographers.
Pets seldom change their expressions.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段，找 refuse 前面的 because。
qs.ev: because it’s hard to get them to sit still and “perform on command,” some professional photographers refuse to photograph pets.
qs.ex: 因為寵物難以聽令靜坐表演，所以選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：寵物不一定聽命令。
(B) 沒提寵物不想被打擾。
(C) 沒提寵物討厭攝影師。
(D) 反而表情會變化。
qs.strat: 原因題找 because 後面的原因。

qs.s: What is the use of a biscuit in taking pictures of a pet?
o: To capture a cute look.
To create a special atmosphere.
To arouse the appetite of the pet.
To keep the pet from looking at the camera.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，看餅乾放在哪裡、為什麼。
qs.ev: The animal’s longing look toward the food will be captured by the camera, but the treat won’t appear in the picture because it’s out of the camera’s range.
qs.ex: 餅乾用來引出寵物渴望的神情並被拍下，所以是為了拍到可愛的表情，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：捕捉可愛表情。
(B) 沒提氣氛。
(C) 目的不是引起食慾，而是拍表情。
(D) 是讓寵物看向上方的食物，不是不看鏡頭。
qs.strat: 用途題看目的，不要選手段本身。

qs.s: What is the advantage of calling your pet’s name when taking a shot of it?
o: To help your pet look its best.
To make sure that your pet sits still.
To keep your pet awake for a while.
To catch a different expression of your pet.
qs.hint: 回第 3 段，找叫名字的效果。
qs.ev: You’ll get a different expression from your pet using this technique.
qs.ex: 叫名字後立刻拍，可以拍到寵物不同的表情，選 (D)。
why: (A) 沒說讓牠看起來最好。
(B) 沒有說會坐著不動。
(C) 沒有說讓牠保持清醒。
(D) 正確：拍到不同表情。
qs.strat: 優點題找 advantage 對應的句子。

qs.s: In what way is photographing zoo animals different from photographing pets?
o: You need to have fast film.
You need special equipment.
You need to stay close to the animals.
You need more time to watch and wait.
qs.hint: 回最後一段，找與寵物比較的差別。
qs.ev: You may have to wait for a while until the animal does something interesting or moves into a position for you to get a good shot.
qs.ex: 動物園動物需要更多耐心，要觀察等待，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 快速底片是拍寵物時提到的。
(B) 沒提特殊器材。
(C) 文中叫人不要太靠近。
(D) 正確：需要更多時間觀察與等待。
qs.strat: 比較題找 requires more 之類的差異。

zh: 動物是許多攝影師最喜愛的題材。貓、狗與其他寵物名列第一，其次是動物園裡的動物。然而，因為很難讓牠們靜坐不動並「聽令表演」，有些專業攝影師拒絕拍攝寵物。
要拍出貓或狗的迷人肖像，有一個方法是把餅乾或點心舉在相機上方。動物望向食物的渴望神情會被相機捕捉到，但點心因為在相機拍攝範圍之外，不會出現在照片中。之後你把照片拿給朋友看時，他們會對你的寵物那充滿愛意的表情印象深刻。
如果你用的是高速底片，只要在呼喚寵物名字後立刻按下快門，就可以快速拍到一些好照片。用這個技巧你會得到寵物不同的表情。依寵物的心情，照片會捕捉到感興趣、好奇的表情，或可能是惱怒的神情，尤其是你把牠從午睡中叫醒時。
拍攝動物園的動物需要更多耐心。畢竟你不能叫醒一隻獅子！你可能得等上一陣子，直到動物做出有趣的事或移動到適合拍攝的位置。拍攝動物園動物時，不要太靠近籠子，也絕不要敲玻璃或從柵欄間丟東西進去。專注於拍出好照片，並始終尊重你所拍攝的動物。
summary: 文章先說明拍寵物的難處，再依序給出引誘、叫名字等技巧，最後提醒拍動物園動物要有耐心並尊重動物。

title: 瑞士刀的由來
text: The Swiss army knife is a popular device that is recognized all over the world. In Switzerland, there is a saying that every good Swiss citizen has one in his or her pocket. But the knife had humble beginnings.

In the late nineteenth century, the Swiss army issued its soldiers a gun that required a special screwdriver to dismantle and clean it. At the same time, canned food was becoming common in the army. Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.

It was a lifesaver for Swiss knife makers, who were struggling to compete with cheaper German imports. In 1884, Carl Elsener, head of the Swiss knife manufacturer Victorinox, seized that opportunity with both hands, and designed a soldier’s knife that the army loved. It was a simple knife with one big blade, a can opener, and a screwdriver.

A few years after the soldier’s knife was issued, the “Schweizer Offizier Messer,” or Swiss Officer’s Knife, came on the market. Interestingly, the Officer’s Knife was never given to those serving in the army. The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves. But its special multi-functional design later launched the knife as a global brand. After the Second World War, a great number of American soldiers were stationed in Europe. And as they could buy the Swiss army knife at shops on military bases, they bought huge quantities of them. However, it seems that “Schweizer Offizier Messer” was too difficult for them to say, so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
pre: 這篇說明瑞士刀如何誕生並得名。依時間順序抓重點：軍方需求、製刀商的機會、軍官刀、美軍命名。
gist: 瑞士刀聞名全球，但起源平凡。
十九世紀晚期，瑞士軍方需要螺絲起子與開罐器，決定發給士兵標準刀具。
這對受德國便宜進口品打擊的瑞士刀商是救星，維氏設計出軍方喜愛的士兵刀。
軍官刀因有開瓶器不被軍方採購，後來因多功能設計成為全球品牌，並被美軍簡稱為瑞士軍刀。

qs.s: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To explain the origin of the Swiss army knife.
To introduce the functions of the Swiss army knife.
To emphasize the importance of the Swiss army knife.
To tell a story about the designer of the Swiss army knife.
qs.hint: 看首段末句 humble beginnings 與後文都在說來歷。
qs.ev: But the knife had humble beginnings.
qs.ex: 全文說明瑞士軍刀的起源與名稱由來，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：解釋瑞士軍刀的由來。
(B) 沒有逐項介紹功能。
(C) 沒有強調重要性。
(D) 設計者只是故事一部分。
qs.strat: 目的題看全文大部分篇幅在做什麼。

qs.s: What does “It” in the third paragraph refer to?
o: The Swiss army needed a knife for every soldier.
Every good Swiss citizen had a knife in his pocket.
Swiss knives were competing with imported knives.
Canned food was becoming popular in the Swiss army.
qs.hint: It 指前一段提出的事件，往前一段找。
qs.ev: Swiss generals decided to issue each soldier a standard knife to serve both as a screwdriver and a can opener.
qs.ex: It 指前句瑞士軍方決定發給每位士兵標準刀這件事，對製刀商是救星，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：軍方需要每位士兵一把刀。
(B) 是首段的說法。
(C) 這是製刀商的處境。
(D) 罐頭變普遍只是背景。
qs.strat: 指涉題 It 常指前文整個事件。

qs.s: Why didn’t the Swiss army purchase the Swiss Officer’s Knife?
o: The design of the knife was too simple.
The knife was sold out to American soldiers.
The army had no budget to make the purchase.
The new design was not considered necessary for officers to own.
qs.hint: 回第 4 段，看 not essential for survival。
qs.ev: The Swiss military purchasers considered the new model with a corkscrew for opening wine not “essential for survival,” so officers had to buy this new model by themselves.
qs.ex: 軍方認為新設計對軍官並非必需，所以沒購買，選 (D)。
why: (A) 設計並不簡單。
(B) 不是賣光。
(C) 沒提預算。
(D) 正確：不被認為是必需。
qs.strat: 原因題找 not ... so 的因果。

qs.s: Who gave the name “the Swiss army knife” to the knife discussed in the passage?
o: Carl Elsener.
Swiss generals.
American soldiers.
German businessmen.
qs.hint: 回最後，找誰發明 Swiss army knife 這個名字。
qs.ev: so they just called it the Swiss army knife, and that is the name it is now known by all over the world.
qs.ex: 美國士兵覺得德文太難念，就直接叫它瑞士軍刀，選 (C)。
why: (A) 埃爾森納是設計者。
(B) 將領決定發刀。
(C) 正確：美軍命名。
(D) 德國商人是競爭者。
qs.strat: 人物題找主詞，注意 they 指誰。

zh: 瑞士軍刀是一種風行的工具，全世界都認得。在瑞士有句話說，每位優秀的瑞士公民口袋裡都有一把。但這把刀的起源很平凡。
十九世紀晚期，瑞士軍方發給士兵一種槍，需要特殊螺絲起子才能拆解和清理。同一時期，罐頭食品在軍中變得普遍。瑞士將領們決定發給每位士兵一把標準刀，既當螺絲起子又當開罐器。
這對正努力與較便宜的德國進口品競爭的瑞士刀具製造商是個救星。1884 年，瑞士刀具製造商維氏的負責人卡爾．埃爾森納雙手抓住這個機會，設計出軍方很喜愛的士兵刀。它是一把簡單的刀，有一片大刀刃、一個開罐器和一支螺絲起子。

士兵刀發出數年後，「Schweizer Offizier Messer」，也就是瑞士軍官刀上市了。有趣的是，軍官刀從未發給在軍中服役的人。瑞士軍方採購人員認為這款附有開紅酒用開瓶器的新型號並非「求生所必需」，所以軍官必須自己購買。但它特殊的多功能設計後來讓這把刀成為全球品牌。二次大戰後，大批美國士兵駐紮在歐洲。由於他們可以在軍事基地的商店買到瑞士軍刀，他們買了大量的刀。然而，「Schweizer Offizier Messer」對他們來說似乎太難念，所以他們就直接稱它為瑞士軍刀，這就是它現在舉世皆知的名稱。
summary: 全文依時間說明瑞士軍刀從軍方需求、士兵刀、軍官刀到美軍命名的過程，重點在其起源與得名。

title: 太空垃圾危機
text: Space is where our future is—trips to the Moon, Mars and beyond. Most people would think that aside from comets and stars there is little else out there. But, since our space journey started we have left so much trash there that scientists are now concerned that if we don’t clean it up, we may all be in mortal danger.

The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center. However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.

It is estimated that there are currently over 500,000 pieces of man-made trash orbiting the Earth at speeds of up to 17,500 miles per hour. The junk varies from tiny pieces of paint chipped off rockets to cameras, huge fuel tanks, and even odd items like the million-dollar tool kit that astronaut Heidemarie Stefanyshyn-Piper lost during a spacewalk.

The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft. Moreover, pieces of junk may collide with each other and break into fragments which fall back to the Earth. To avoid this, scientists have devised several ways for clearing the sky. Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles. Future plans include a cooperative effort among many nations to stop littering in space and to clean up the trash already there.
pre: 這篇談太空垃圾的來源、數量、危害與因應。依「問題、原因、影響、解決」的順序整理。
gist: 太空是未來所在，但我們留下的垃圾可能危及所有人。
第一件太空垃圾是 1964 年失聯的衛星，因無後果，科學家愈來愈放心丟棄無用物品。
現有超過五十萬件人造垃圾高速繞行，從油漆碎片到工具箱都有。
問題是會撞毀衛星與太空船，目前以地面站監控，未來計畫國際合作清理。

qs.s: What was the first piece of man-made space trash?
o: A camera.
A tool kit.
A fuel tank.
A broken satellite.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，找 first piece。
qs.ev: The first piece of space junk was created in 1964, when the American satellite Vanguard I stopped operating and lost its connection with the ground center.
qs.ex: 第一件太空垃圾是停止運作的先鋒一號衛星，選 (D)。
why: (A) 相機是後來的例子。
(B) 工具箱是後來的例子。
(C) 燃料槽是後來的例子。
(D) 正確：壞掉的衛星。
qs.strat: First 題找最早的時間點。

qs.s: Why were scientists NOT concerned about space trash in the beginning?
o: It no longer served any useful purpose.
It was millions of miles away from the Earth.
It did not cause any problems.
It was regarded as similar to comets and stars.
qs.hint: 找 NOT concerned 的原因，在第 2 段。
qs.ev: However, since it kept orbiting around the Earth without any consequences, scientists became increasingly comfortable abandoning things that no longer served any useful purpose in space.
qs.ex: 因為垃圾繞行地球而沒造成後果，科學家起初不擔心，選 (C)。
why: (A) 這是丟棄的原因，不是不擔心的原因。
(B) 沒說離地球數百萬英里。
(C) 正確：沒造成問題。
(D) 沒說被視為彗星恆星。
qs.strat: 留意題目的 NOT 與 why，選真正的原因。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about space junk?
o: It is huge, heavy machines.
It never changes position.
It floats slowly around the Earth.
It may cause problems for space shuttles.
qs.hint: 回第 4 段，找問題。
qs.ev: The major problem with the space trash is that it may hit working satellites and damage traveling spacecraft.
qs.ex: 太空垃圾可能撞毀太空船，選 (D)。
why: (A) 垃圾有大有小，並非都是大型機器。
(B) 它持續繞行，位置會變。
(C) 時速高達一萬七千五百英里。
(D) 正確：可能造成太空梭問題。
qs.strat: True 題避免被極端字眼（never, always）誤導。

qs.s: What has been done about the space trash problem?
o: Scientists have cleaned up most of the trash.
Large pieces of space trash are being closely watched.
Many nations have worked together to stop polluting space.
Ground stations are built to help store the trash properly in space.
qs.hint: 回第 4 段，找已做的措施。
qs.ev: Ground stations have been built to monitor larger pieces of space trash to prevent them from crashing into working satellites or space shuttles.
qs.ex: 已建地面站監控較大的垃圾，選 (B)。
why: (A) 並未清理大部分。
(B) 正確：大垃圾受到密切監視。
(C) 多國合作是未來計畫。
(D) 地面站是用來監控，不是儲存。
qs.strat: 注意 have been done 與 future plans 的差別。

zh: 太空是我們未來所在，到月球、火星及更遠地方旅行。大多數人會認為，除了彗星和恆星之外，那裡幾乎沒有別的東西。但自從我們的太空旅程開始，我們在那裡留下了太多垃圾，科學家現在擔心，如果我們不清理，可能會使我們全都陷入致命的危險。
第一件太空垃圾產生於 1964 年，當時美國衛星先鋒一號停止運作，並失去與地面中心的連線。然而，由於它持續繞著地球運行而沒有造成任何後果，科學家愈來愈放心地把太空中不再有用的東西丟棄在那裡。
據估計，目前有超過五十萬件人造垃圾以時速高達一萬七千五百英里的速度繞著地球運行。這些垃圾種類繁多，從火箭上剝落的細小油漆碎片，到相機、巨大的燃料槽，甚至還有像太空人海黛瑪麗．史蒂芬妮辛－派柏在太空漫步時遺失的價值百萬美元的工具箱這類奇特物品。
太空垃圾的主要問題是它可能撞上運作中的衛星，並損壞行進中的太空船。此外，垃圾碎片可能互相碰撞並裂成碎片，墜回地球。為避免這種情形，科學家設計了幾種清理天空的方法。已經建造了地面站來監控較大的太空垃圾，以防止它們撞上運作中的衛星或太空梭。未來的計畫包括多國合作，停止在太空亂丟垃圾，並清理已經在那裡的垃圾。
summary: 文章說明太空垃圾由第一顆失效衛星開始累積，如今數量龐大且危險，目前以地面站監控，未來盼靠國際合作清理。

title: 能量飲料與酒測
text: An alcohol breath test (ABT) is often used by the police to find out whether a person is drunk while driving. In the United States, the legal blood alcohol limit is 0.08% for people aged 21 years or older, while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body. A “positive” test result, a result over the legal limit, allows the police to arrest the driver. However, many people who tested positive on the test have claimed that they only drank a “non-alcoholic” energy drink. Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.

First, the amount of alcohol in 27 different popular energy drinks was measured. All but one had an alcohol level greater than 0.005%. In nine of the 27 drinks, the alcohol level was at least 0.096%. The scientists then investigated the possibility that these small levels of alcohol could be detected by an ABT. They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.

For 11 of the 27 energy drinks, the ABT did detect the presence of alcohol if the test was given within one minute after the drink was taken. However, alcohol could not be detected for any of the drinks if the test was given 15 minutes after the drink was consumed. This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result. The sooner the test is conducted after the consumption of these drinks, the more likely a positive alcohol reading will be obtained.
pre: 這篇報導一項實驗。依「問題、方法、結果、結論」整理，並注意時間點的差異。
gist: 警方用酒測抓酒駕，但有人說只喝了無酒精能量飲料卻測出陽性，密蘇里研究者做實驗查證。
先測 27 種能量飲料含酒精量，再讓受試者喝完後於 1 分鐘與 15 分鐘後酒測。
11 種飲料在 1 分鐘內可測出，15 分鐘後都測不出，可見測驗時間是關鍵。

qs.s: For a person who just turned 20, what is the legal alcohol level allowed while driving in the US?
qs.hint: 找 under 21 的規定，在第 1 段。
qs.ev: while people under 21 are not allowed to drive a car with any level of alcohol in their body.
qs.ex: 剛滿 20 歲屬於 21 歲以下，不得有任何酒精，所以是 0.000%，選 (A)。
why: (A) 正確：不得有任何酒精。
(B) 是飲料中的酒精含量。
(C) 這是 21 歲以上的限制。
(D) 是飲料的酒精含量。
qs.strat: 數字題要先確認對象的條件。

qs.s: What is the purpose of the Missouri experiment?
o: To introduce a new method of calculating blood alcohol levels.
To discover the relation between energy drinks and ABT test results.
To warn about the dangers of drinking energy drinks mixed with alcohol.
To challenge the current legal alcohol limit for drivers in the United States.
qs.hint: 實驗目的在問題後面，看研究者想查什麼。
qs.ev: Can one of these energy drinks really cause someone to test positive on an ABT? Researchers in Missouri set up an experiment to find out.
qs.ex: 實驗要查明能量飲料是否會造成酒測陽性，也就是飲料與酒測結果的關係，選 (B)。
why: (A) 沒介紹新計算方法。
(B) 正確：探討能量飲料與酒測結果的關係。
(C) 沒有混酒。
(D) 沒有挑戰法定限制。
qs.strat: 目的題找 to find out 前面的問題。

qs.s: What were the participants of the experiment asked to do after they finished their energy drink?
o: To line up in the laboratory.
To recall the drink brands.
To take an alcohol breath test.
To check their breath for freshness.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段末句，看受試者的任務。
qs.ev: They asked test subjects to drink a full can or bottle of an energy drink and then gave each subject an ABT one minute and 15 minutes after the drink was finished.
qs.ex: 受試者喝完後要接受酒測，選 (C)。
why: (A) 沒說排隊。
(B) 沒說回想品牌。
(C) 正確：做酒精呼氣測試。
(D) 沒說檢查口氣。
qs.strat: 細節題找 after 之後的動作。

qs.s: What is the most important factor that affects the ABT test result for energy drink consumers?
o: The age of the person who takes the test.
The place where the test is given.
The equipment that the test uses.
The time when the test is taken.
qs.hint: 找結論句 plays a crucial role。
qs.ev: This shows that when the test is taken plays a crucial role in the test result.
qs.ex: 測試時間是影響結果最重要的因素，選 (D)。
why: (A) 沒提年齡影響。
(B) 沒提地點。
(C) 沒提設備。
(D) 正確：測試時間。
qs.strat: 最重要因素題找 crucial 這類強調詞。

zh: 酒精呼氣測試（ABT）常被警方用來判斷駕駛人是否酒醉。在美國，二十一歲以上者的法定血液酒精濃度上限是 0.08%，而二十一歲以下的人則不得在體內有任何酒精的情況下開車。測試結果為「陽性」，也就是超過法定限制，警方就可以逮捕駕駛。然而，許多測出陽性的人聲稱，他們只喝了「無酒精」的能量飲料。這些能量飲料真的會讓人在酒測中呈現陽性嗎？密蘇里的研究人員設計了一項實驗來查明。
首先，測量 27 種受歡迎的能量飲料的酒精含量。除了一種之外，全都超過 0.005%。在 27 種飲料中，有九種的酒精濃度至少為 0.096%。科學家接著調查這些少量的酒精是否能被酒測偵測到。他們請受試者喝完一整罐或一整瓶能量飲料，然後在喝完後一分鐘和十五分鐘各做一次酒測。
27 種能量飲料中，有 11 種在喝下後一分鐘內測試時，酒測確實測得出酒精。然而，若在飲用後十五分鐘才測，則所有飲料都測不出酒精。這顯示測試進行的時間對測試結果有關鍵影響。喝下這些飲料後越快測試，越有可能得到陽性的酒精讀數。
summary: 文章以問題開頭，說明密蘇里實驗的方法與結果，結論是能量飲料可能在短時間內使酒測呈陽性，測試時間是關鍵因素。

title: 印度額間紅點
text: The majority of Indian women wear a red dot between their eyebrows. While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion. The dot goes by different names in different Hindi dialects, and “bindi” is the one that is most commonly known. Traditionally, the dot carries no gender restriction: Men as well as women wear it. However, the tradition of men wearing it has faded in recent times, so nowadays we see a lot more women than men wearing one.

The position of the bindi is standard: center of the forehead, close to the eyebrows. It represents a third, or inner eye. Hindu tradition holds that all people have three eyes: The two outer ones are used for seeing the outside world, and the third one is there to focus inward toward God. As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.

Red is the traditional color of the dot. It is said that in ancient times a man would place a drop of blood between his wife’s eyes to seal their marriage. According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple. Today, people go with different colors depending upon their preferences. Women often wear dots that match the color of their clothes. Decorative or sticker bindis come in all sizes, colors and variations, and can be worn by young and old, married and unmarried people alike. Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.
pre: 這篇介紹印度人額頭上的 bindi。留意它原本的宗教意義，以及今日的變化。
gist: 多數印度女性額間戴紅點，主要與印度教有關，傳統上男女皆可，如今男性較少。
點的位置固定，象徵第三隻眼，使信徒時時把神放在心上。
紅色起源於婚姻象徵與好運，如今顏色多樣、人人可戴，更像時尚。

qs.s: Why did people in India start wearing a red dot on their forehead?
o: To indicate their social rank.
To show their religious belief.
To display their financial status.
To highlight their family background.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段，看 primarily related to。
qs.ev: While it is generally taken as an indicator of their marital status, the practice is primarily related to the Hindu religion.
qs.ex: 這個習俗主要與印度教有關，所以是為了表達宗教信仰，選 (B)。
why: (A) 不是社會階級。
(B) 正確：表達宗教信仰。
(C) 不是財務狀況。
(D) 不是家世背景。
qs.strat: 原因題注意 generally 與 primarily 的轉折。

qs.s: What is the significance of the third eye in Hindu tradition?
o: To stay in harmony with nature.
To observe the outside world more clearly.
To pay respect to God.
To see things with a subjective view.
qs.hint: 回第 2 段，找第三隻眼的作用。
qs.ev: As such, the dot signifies piety and serves as a constant reminder to keep God in the front of a believer’s thoughts.
qs.ex: 第三隻眼象徵虔誠，提醒信徒把神放在心上，也就是向神致敬，選 (C)。
why: (A) 沒提與自然和諧。
(B) 外在世界是兩隻外眼的功能。
(C) 正確：向神表達敬意。
(D) 沒提主觀看法。
qs.strat: 意義題找 signifies 這類字眼。

qs.s: Why was red chosen as the original color of the bindi?
o: The red dot represented the blood of God.
Red stood for a wife’s love for her husband.
The word “bindi” means “red” in some Hindi dialects.
Red was supposed to bring blessings to a married couple.
qs.hint: 回第 3 段，找紅色的緣由。
qs.ev: According to Hindu beliefs, the color red is believed to bring good fortune to the married couple.
qs.ex: 紅色被認為為夫妻帶來好運，也就是祝福，選 (D)。
why: (A) 沒說是神的血。
(B) 是丈夫的血，不代表愛。
(C) 沒說 bindi 意為紅色。
(D) 正確：帶來祝福。
qs.strat: 原因題找 believed to 的內容。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about the practice of wearing a bindi today?
o: Bindis are worn anywhere on the face now.
Bindis are now used as a decorative item.
Most Indian women do not like to wear bindis anymore.
Wearing a bindi has become more popular among Indian men.
qs.hint: 回最後一段，看今日的情況。
qs.ev: Wearing a bindi has become more of a fashion statement than a religious custom.
qs.ex: 今日更像時尚表現，也就是裝飾品，選 (B)。
why: (A) 位置仍是額頭中央。
(B) 正確：被當作裝飾品。
(C) 沒說大多數女性不喜歡。
(D) 男性戴的傳統已消退。
qs.strat: 時間題注意 today 與 traditionally 的對比。

zh: 大多數印度女性在眉間戴一個紅點。雖然一般認為它是婚姻狀態的標誌，但這個習俗主要與印度教有關。這個點在不同印地語方言中有不同名稱，而「bindi」是最廣為人知的一個。傳統上這個點沒有性別限制：男性和女性都戴。然而，男性戴它的傳統近來已逐漸消退，所以如今我們看到戴的女性比男性多得多。
bindi 的位置是固定的：額頭正中央、靠近眉毛處。它代表第三隻眼，也就是內在之眼。印度教傳統認為所有人都有三隻眼睛：兩隻外面的眼睛用來看外在世界，而第三隻用來向內專注於神。因此，這個點象徵虔誠，並且是一個持續的提醒，讓信徒隨時把神放在心中最前面。
紅色是這個點的傳統顏色。據說在古代，男人會在妻子的雙眼之間點上一滴血來為婚姻蓋印。根據印度教信仰，紅色被認為會為已婚夫妻帶來好運。今日，人們依個人喜好選擇不同顏色。女性常戴與衣服顏色相配的點。裝飾性或貼紙式的 bindi 有各種大小、顏色與變化，年輕人與老年人、已婚與未婚者都可以戴。戴 bindi 已經更像是一種時尚表現，而不是宗教習俗。
summary: 文章說明 bindi 起初與宗教和婚姻有關，象徵第三隻眼與好運，如今顏色、款式多樣，成為人人可用的時尚裝飾。

title: 童妮・摩里森的寫作人生
text: American writer Toni Morrison was born in 1931 in Ohio. She was raised in an African American family filled with songs and stories of Southern myths, which later shaped her prose. Her happy family life led to her excellent performance in school, despite the atmosphere of racial discrimination in the society. After graduating from college, Morrison started to work as a teacher and got married in 1958. Several years later, her marriage began to fail. For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group, in which each member was required to bring a story or poem for discussion. She wrote a story based on the life of a girl she knew in childhood who had prayed to God for blue eyes. The story was well received by the group, but then she put it away, thinking she was done with it.

In 1964, Morrison got divorced and devoted herself to writing. One day, she dusted off the story she had written for the writers’ group and decided to make it into a novel. She drew on her memories from childhood and expanded upon them using her imagination so that the characters developed a life of their own. The Bluest Eye was eventually published in 1970. From 1970 to 1992, Morrison published five more novels.

In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory. In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture. The novels and other works won her several prizes.
In 1993, Morrison received the Nobel Prize in Literature. She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.
pre: 這是一篇依時間順序介紹作家生平的文章，讀的時候留意年份、重大事件（婚姻、出版、得獎）和她作品的主題。
gist: 摩里森生於1931年，成長於充滿歌謠與故事的家庭，婚姻失敗後加入寫作團體並寫出一篇故事。
1964年離婚後她專心寫作，把舊故事擴寫成小說《最藍的眼睛》，1970年出版。
她的小說呈現非裔美國人的過去、掙扎與文化記憶，並贏得多項獎項。
1993年她獲得諾貝爾文學獎，是第八位女性得主，也是第一位非裔美籍女性得主。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The life of black people in the U.S.
The life of an African American writer.
The history of African American culture.
The history of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
qs.hint: 看第一句介紹的人物，再看全文是依什麼順序在寫（出生、婚姻、寫作、得獎）。
qs.ev: American writer Toni Morrison was born in 1931 in Ohio.
qs.ex: 全文從摩里森出生、成長、婚姻、寫作到獲得諾貝爾獎，依時間介紹同一個人的一生，所以主旨是一位非裔美國作家的生平。
why: (A) 只談黑人的生活，但文章焦點是單一作家
(B) 正確：全文介紹作家摩里森的一生
(C) 文化歷史只是她作品的背景，不是全文主軸
(D) 諾貝爾獎只在最後一句出現
qs.strat: 主旨題先看首段與全文脈絡，排除只涵蓋局部細節或範圍過大的選項。

qs.s: Why did Morrison join the writers’ group?
o: She wanted to publish The Bluest Eye.
She wanted to fight racial discrimination.
She wanted to be a professional writer.
She wanted to get away from her unhappy marriage.
qs.hint: 回到第1段，找 joined the writers’ group 前面那句交代的原因。
qs.ev: Several years later, her marriage began to fail. For a temporary escape, she joined a small writers’ group, in which each member was required to bring a story or poem for discussion.
qs.ex: 文中說她的婚姻開始破裂，為了「暫時逃避」才加入寫作團體，所以是想擺脫不快樂的婚姻。
why: (A) 《最藍的眼睛》是日後才出版的作品
(B) 文中沒說她加入是為了對抗種族歧視
(C) 她加入時只是想暫時逃避，還沒打算當職業作家
(D) 正確：想逃離不幸福的婚姻
qs.strat: 原因題找 why 對應的 for / because 等線索句，再對照選項換句話說。

qs.s: According to the passage, what is one of the themes in Morrison’s works?
o: A search for African American values.
Divorced black women in American society.
Songs and stories of African Americans in Ohio.
History of African Americans from the 1970s through the 1990s.
qs.hint: 看第3段 In her novels 之後，作者怎麼說她作品的內容與例子。
qs.ev: In her novels, Morrison brings in different elements of the African American past, their struggles, problems and cultural memory. In Song of Solomon, for example, Morrison tells the story of an African American man and his search for identity in his culture.
qs.ex: 第3段說她的小說呈現非裔美國人的過去與文化記憶，並以尋找文化認同為例，因此主題之一是尋找非裔美國人的價值（認同）。
why: (A) 正確：尋找非裔美國人的文化認同與價值
(B) 文中沒有寫離婚的黑人女性這個主題
(C) 歌謠與故事是她的成長背景，不是作品主題，也未限定俄亥俄
(D) 1970到1992是出版時間，不是主題
qs.strat: 主題題要找作者描述作品內容的段落，避開只是時間或背景的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about Toni Morrison?
o: She has been writing a lot since her adolescent years.
She suffered from severe racial discrimination in her family.
What she wrote in her novels are true stories of African Americans.
No African American woman ever received a Nobel Prize in Literature before her.
qs.hint: 找最後一段提到諾貝爾獎的句子，注意 first 這個字。
qs.ev: She is the eighth woman and the first African American woman to win the honor.
qs.ex: 文末說她是第一位獲得諾貝爾文學獎的非裔美籍女性，所以在她之前沒有非裔女性得過此獎。
why: (A) 文章說她成年後才開始寫作，不是青少年時期
(B) 種族歧視是社會氛圍，不是來自家庭
(C) 小說是以記憶加想像寫成，不全是真實故事
(D) 正確：在她之前沒有非裔女性獲得諾貝爾文學獎
qs.strat: 判斷是非題時逐項對照原文，注意 first、never、all 這類絕對字眼。

zh: 美國作家童妮・摩里森於1931年出生在俄亥俄州。她成長於一個充滿南方神話歌謠與故事的非裔美國人家庭，這些後來影響了她的文筆。儘管社會瀰漫著種族歧視的氣氛，快樂的家庭生活讓她在學校表現優異。大學畢業後，摩里森開始當老師，並在1958年結婚。數年後，她的婚姻開始破裂。為了暫時逃避，她加入了一個小型寫作團體，團體中每位成員都必須帶一篇故事或詩來討論。她寫了一個故事，取材於她童年認識的一個女孩，那女孩曾向上帝祈求擁有藍色的眼睛。這個故事很受團體讚賞，但她隨後把它收了起來，以為自己已經寫完了。
1964年，摩里森離婚並全心投入寫作。有一天，她把當初為寫作團體寫的故事拿出來拍掉灰塵，決定把它寫成一部小說。她汲取童年的記憶，再用想像力加以擴充，讓角色自己發展出生命。《最藍的眼睛》終於在1970年出版。從1970年到1992年，摩里森又出版了五部小說。
在她的小說中，摩里森帶入非裔美國人過去的各種元素，包括他們的奮鬥、問題與文化記憶。例如在《所羅門之歌》中，摩里森講述一位非裔美國男子在自己的文化中尋找認同的故事。這些小說與其他作品為她贏得了許多獎項。
1993年，摩里森獲得諾貝爾文學獎。她是第八位獲得此項殊榮的女性，也是第一位獲得的非裔美籍女性。
summary: 全文依時間順序介紹摩里森：成長背景、婚姻破裂後加入寫作團體、離婚後把故事擴寫成小說、作品主題，最後以獲得諾貝爾獎作結。讀傳記類文章時，抓年份與關鍵事件就能掌握脈絡。

title: 艾曼紐三兄弟的成功之道
text: Below is an excerpt from an interview with Zeke Emanuel, a health-policy expert, on his famous brothers.

Interviewer: You’re the older brother of Rahm, the mayor of Chicago, and Ari, an extremely successful talent agent. And you’re a bioethicist and one of the architects of Obamacare. Isn’t writing a book about how great your family is a bit odd?

Zeke: I don’t write a book about how great my family is. There are lots of idiocies and foolishness—a lot to make fun of in the book. I wrote Brothers Emanuel because I had begun jotting stories for my kids. And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.
I: To what do you attribute the Emanuel brothers’ success?

Z: I would put success in quotes. We strive. First, I think we got this striving from our mother to make the world a better place. A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do. And maybe the third important thing is my father’s admonition that offense is the best defense. We don’t give up.
I: Do you still not have a TV?
Z: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
I: But you have four cell phones.
Z: I’m down to two, thankfully.
I: Your brothers are a national source of fascination. Where do you think they’ll be in five years?

Z: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self. The one thing I can guarantee is none of us will have taken a cruise, none of us will be sitting on a beach with a pina colada.
pre: 這是一段訪談，以「問（I）」與「答（Z）」交替進行。讀的時候分清誰在說話，並留意受訪者話中的幽默與言外之意。
gist: 這是對衛生政策專家季克・艾曼紐談他兄弟的訪談節錄。
訪談者問：寫一本誇耀家人的書不奇怪嗎？
他說書中有許多可笑之處，起因是替孩子記下的故事，大家也好奇母親到底讓他們吃了什麼。
訪談者問三兄弟成功的原因。
他說成功要打上引號，三點：母親的奮鬥精神、不停留在上次勝利、父親的進攻信念。
訪談者問他是否還是沒有電視。
他說自己不用電視、汽車、臉書與推特。
訪談者說他有四支手機。
他回答已減為兩支。
訪談者問五年後兄弟們會在哪裡。
他預測三人大致不變，而且絕不會悠閒度假。

qs.s: What does Zeke Emanuel have in mind when saying “What did Mom put in the cereal?”
o: The secret to bringing up successful kids.
The recipe for a breakfast food.
The difference among the brothers.
The questions from his kids.
qs.hint: 看這句話前後：他說大家一直問他什麼問題，後面接著提到哪三個人。
qs.ev: And then we began getting a lot of questions: What did Mom put in the cereal? Three successful brothers, all different areas.
qs.ex: 「媽媽在麥片裡放了什麼」是玩笑話，緊接著提到三個兄弟都成功，其實是在問母親怎麼養出成功的孩子的祕訣。
why: (A) 正確：養出成功孩子的祕訣
(B) 不是真的在問早餐食譜，而是玩笑
(C) 三兄弟領域不同，但問題問的不是差異
(D) 這些問題是外界問的，不是他的孩子
qs.strat: 引述俏皮話的題目，要從前後文推它真正想表達的意思，不要只看字面。

qs.s: What does Zeke Emanuel think of the modern conveniences mentioned in the interview?
o: Better late than never.
Practice makes perfect.
One can live without many of them.
They are great inventions.
qs.hint: 看他回答 TV、car、Facebook 的那幾句，想想他的生活態度。
qs.ev: I don’t own a TV. I don’t own a car. I don’t Facebook. I don’t tweet.
qs.ex: 他沒有電視、汽車，也不用社群網站，卻依然成功，顯示許多現代便利設施其實可以不要。
why: (A) 「遲做總比不做好」與內容無關
(B) 「熟能生巧」與內容無關
(C) 正確：許多便利設施沒有也能生活
(D) 他並未稱讚這些發明，反而都不用
qs.strat: 態度題看說話者的實際作為與用詞，再選最貼近的結論。

qs.s: According to Zeke Emanuel, which of the following is a reason for the brothers’ success?
o: They defend themselves by attacking others.
They learn a lot from great people’s quotes.
They are committed to glorifying their parents.
They keep moving forward even after a big success.
qs.hint: 回到他回答成功原因的那一段，找 important thing 後面列出的幾點。
qs.ev: A second important thing is you never rest on the last victory. There’s always more to do.
qs.ex: 他說第二個重要的事是絕不滿足於上次的勝利，總是還有更多事要做，也就是成功之後仍持續前進。
why: (A) 他提到的是『攻擊是最好的防守』，不是攻擊別人來自保
(B) 文中沒提向名人名言學習
(C) 文中沒說要榮耀父母
(D) 正確：即使大成功之後仍不停向前
qs.strat: 列舉型細節題先找 first、second、third 這類序列字，再逐項比對。

qs.s: Which of the following best summarizes Zeke Emanuel’s response to the last question?
o: The brothers look forward to a family trip on a cruise.
Nothing much will change in the near future for them.
Higher positions and more power will be their goals.
None of the brothers will go to the beach.
qs.hint: 看最後一個問題的回答，他怎麼預測三兄弟五年後的狀況。
qs.ev: Ari will be a superagent running the same company. Rahm would still be mayor of Chicago. I will probably continue to be my academic self.
qs.ex: 他預測三人五年後仍在原來的位置，沒有太大改變，並說不會去度假，因此最能概括的是近期內沒有多大變化。
why: (A) 他只是說不會去郵輪旅行，不是期待
(B) 正確：近期內不會有太大改變
(C) 他並未提到追求更高職位與權力
(D) 坐在海灘上只是舉例說他們不會悠閒度假，並非整段回答的重點
qs.strat: 歸納回答的題目要抓整段話的共同點，避開只抓一個細節的選項。

zh: 以下是對衛生政策專家季克・艾曼紐談他赫赫有名的兄弟們的訪談節錄。
訪談者：你是芝加哥市長拉姆的哥哥，也是極為成功的藝人經紀人阿里的哥哥。而你是生物倫理學家，也是歐巴馬健保的設計者之一。寫一本書談自己的家人多麼了不起，不是有點奇怪嗎？
季克：我寫的不是一本說我家人多了不起的書。書裡有很多愚蠢和荒唐的事，很多可以拿來開玩笑。我寫《艾曼紐兄弟》，是因為我開始替我的孩子們草草記下一些故事。後來大家開始問我們很多問題：媽媽在麥片裡放了什麼？三個成功的兄弟，領域各不相同。
訪談者：你認為艾曼紐兄弟成功的原因是什麼？
季克：我會把『成功』加上引號。我們是在奮鬥。第一，我認為這種奮鬥精神來自母親，要讓世界變得更好。第二個重要的事是，絕不躺在上一次的勝利上。永遠還有更多事要做。也許第三個重要的事是父親的告誡：攻擊就是最好的防守。我們不放棄。
訪談者：你還是沒有電視嗎？
季克：我沒有電視，沒有車，不用臉書，也不發推特。
訪談者：但你有四支手機。
季克：謝天謝地，我已經減到兩支了。
訪談者：你的兄弟們是全國矚目的焦點。你認為五年後他們會在哪裡？
季克：阿里會是個超級經紀人，經營同一家公司。拉姆仍會是芝加哥市長。我大概還是繼續當我的學者。我唯一能保證的是，我們沒有一個人會去搭郵輪，沒有一個人會坐在海灘上喝鳳梨可樂達。
summary: 這篇訪談中，受訪者說明三兄弟的成功來自母親的奮鬥精神、不斷前進的態度與父親的進攻信念，生活簡樸、不追求享樂。讀訪談時要分辨問答者，並理解幽默回答背後的真意。

title: 大規模開放線上課程 MOOC
text: MOOC, a massive open online course, aims at providing large-scale interactive participation and open access via the web. In addition to traditional course materials such as videos, readings, and problem sets, MOOCs provide interactive user forums that help build a community for the students, professors, and teaching assistants.

MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up. This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways. Since the courses can be taken by hundreds of thousands of students at the same time, the number of universities might decrease dramatically. Professor Thrun has even envisioned a future in which there will only need to be 10 universities in the world. Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.

There is a lot of excitement and fear surrounding MOOCs. While some say free online courses are a great way to increase the enrollment of minority students, others have said they will leave many students behind. Some critics have said that MOOCs promote an unrealistic one-size-fits-all model of higher education and that there is no replacement for true dialogues between professors and their students. After all, a brain is not a computer. We are not blank hard drives waiting to be filled with data. People learn from people they love and remember the things that arouse emotion. Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
pre: 這篇先介紹 MOOC 是什麼，再談它的影響，最後談支持與批評的聲音。讀的時候留意正反兩面的轉折字（While, Some critics）。
gist: MOOC 是大規模開放的線上課程，提供互動討論區讓師生形成社群。
MOOC 自2011年興起，正在改變高等教育，而且免費，對缺錢的學生是好消息。
MOOC 引發興奮也引發擔憂，批評者認為它缺乏真正的人際互動與情感連結。

qs.s: What does the word “cash-strapped” in the second paragraph mean?
o: Making a lot of money.
Being short of money.
Being careful with money.
Spending little money.
qs.hint: 回到第2段，看 free 之後那句 good news for 誰，推測 cash-strapped 的意思。
qs.ev: Perhaps the most striking thing about MOOCs, many of which are being taught by professors at prestigious universities, is that they’re free. This is certainly good news for cash-strapped students.
qs.ex: MOOC 免費，對這類學生是好消息，可知他們缺錢，cash-strapped 就是缺乏金錢。
why: (A) 賺很多錢的人不需要免費課程
(B) 正確：缺錢的
(C) 小心花錢不等於缺錢
(D) 花很少錢不符合免費才是好消息的語氣
qs.strat: 字義題用前後文線索（免費就是好消息）推測詞義。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of MOOCs?
o: It is free to take the courses.
Many courses are offered by famous universities.
Most courses address artificial intelligence.
Many students can take the course at the same time.
qs.hint: 找第2段中關於 Thrun 的課程內容，比對選項 C 是否是普遍特色。
qs.ev: MOOCs first made waves in the fall of 2011, when Professor Sebastian Thrun from Stanford University opened his graduate-level artificial intelligence course up to any student anywhere, and 160,000 students in more than 190 countries signed up.
qs.ex: 人工智慧只是第一個 MOOC 的例子，文中並未說多數課程都是人工智慧，因此不是 MOOC 的特色。
why: (A) 免費是文中指出的特色
(B) 許多課由名校教授開設，文中有提到
(C) 正確：人工智慧只是例子，不是多數課程的主題
(D) 同時可由數十萬人修課，文中有提到
qs.strat: NOT 題要逐項找原文證據，找不到的就是答案。

qs.s: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
o: The impact of MOOCs.
The goal of MOOCs.
The size of MOOC classes.
The cost of MOOC courses.
qs.hint: 看第2段第二句，它總結了這段的方向（改變高等教育）。
qs.ev: This new breed of online classes is shaking up the higher education world in many ways.
qs.ex: 第2段談 MOOC 興起後對大學、學生人數與學費的影響，所以主要是在談 MOOC 帶來的衝擊。
why: (A) 正確：MOOC 的衝擊
(B) 目標在第1段介紹
(C) 班級規模只是細節之一
(D) 費用只是細節之一
qs.strat: 段落主旨題找主題句，排除只講細節的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following is a problem of MOOCs mentioned in the passage?
o: The disappearance of traditional course materials.
The limited number of courses offered around the world.
The overreliance on professors from prestigious universities.
The lack of social interaction among students and professors.
qs.hint: 最後一段列出批評者的擔憂，找 worry 或 critics 的句子。
qs.ev: Some critics worry that online students will miss out on the social aspects of college.
qs.ex: 批評者擔心線上學生會錯過大學的社交面向，也提到缺乏師生真正的對話，所以問題是缺乏人際互動。
why: (A) 傳統教材並未消失，反而第1段說仍提供
(B) 文中沒提課程數量有限
(C) 名校教授是優點，不是問題
(D) 正確：師生之間缺乏社交互動
qs.strat: 問題題找批評、擔憂、缺點等字眼的位置。

zh: MOOC（大規模開放線上課程）的目標，是透過網路提供大規模的互動參與與開放使用。除了影片、閱讀材料和習題集等傳統課程資料之外，MOOC 還提供互動式的使用者論壇，幫助學生、教授和助教建立起一個社群。

MOOC 在2011年秋天首度引起轟動，當時史丹佛大學的塞巴斯蒂安・特龍教授把他的研究所等級人工智慧課程開放給世界各地的任何學生，結果來自190多個國家的16萬名學生報名。這種新型態的線上課程，正在以許多方式撼動高等教育界。由於課程可以同時讓數十萬名學生修習，大學的數量可能會大幅減少。特龍教授甚至設想過一個世界上只需要10所大學的未來。MOOC 最驚人的地方也許是，許多課程由名校教授授課，卻是免費的。這對缺錢的學生來說無疑是好消息。
圍繞著 MOOC 有許多興奮，也有許多恐懼。有人說免費線上課程是增加少數族群學生入學的好方法，也有人說它會讓許多學生被拋在後頭。一些批評者說，MOOC 推廣的是不切實際、一體適用的高等教育模式，而且沒有東西能取代教授與學生之間真正的對話。畢竟，大腦不是電腦。我們不是等著被填入資料的空白硬碟。人們向所愛的人學習，記得會引起情緒的事物。一些批評者擔心，線上學生會錯過大學生活的社交面向。
summary: 文章先定義 MOOC，再說明它免費、規模大，正在改變高等教育，最後提出批評：缺少真實的人際互動與情感。掌握先介紹、再影響、後爭議的結構，就能抓住重點。

title: 車輛通訊與無人駕駛
text: Today the car seems to make periodic leaps in progress. A variety of driver assistance technologies are appearing on new cars. A developing technology called Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication, or V2V, is being tested by automotive manufacturers as a way to help reduce the number of accidents. V2V works by using wireless signals to send information back and forth between cars about their location, speed and direction, so that they keep safe distances from each other. Another new technology being tested is Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communication, or V2I. V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues. V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes. Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.

More and more new cars can reverse-park, read traffic signs, maintain a safe distance in steady traffic and brake automatically to avoid crashes. Moreover, a number of firms are creating cars that drive themselves to a chosen destination without a human at the controls. It is predicted that driverless cars will be ready for sale within five years. If and when cars go completely driverless, the benefits will be enormous. Google, which already uses prototypes of such cars to ferry its staff along Californian freeways, once put a blind man in a prototype and filmed him being driven off to buy takeaway hamburgers. If this works, huge numbers of elderly and disabled people can regain their personal mobility. The young will not have to pay crippling motor insurance, because their reckless hands and feet will no longer touch the wheel or the accelerator. People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.
pre: 這篇介紹未來汽車的新技術與好處。讀的時候分清 V2V、V2I 兩種技術各自做什麼，並留意第二段列出的好處。
gist: V2V 與 V2I 兩種車輛通訊技術正在測試，有望減少約八成的車禍。
越來越多新車有自動功能，無人駕駛車將帶來行動不便者、年輕人與通勤者的許多好處。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about V2V?
o: V2V communication has been very well developed.
Through V2V, drivers can chat with each other on the road.
V2V is designed to decrease crashes by keeping safe distances.
Through V2V, a car can warn cyclists nearby of its approach.
qs.hint: 找第1段 V2V works by 開頭的句子，看它的目的。
qs.ev: V2V works by using wireless signals to send information back and forth between cars about their location, speed and direction, so that they keep safe distances from each other.
qs.ex: V2V 讓車子互傳位置、速度與方向，好讓彼此保持安全距離，目的是減少車禍。
why: (A) V2V 仍在測試中，並未發展完善
(B) 不是讓駕駛聊天，而是傳送行車資訊
(C) 正確：用保持安全距離來減少車禍
(D) 文中沒有提到警告自行車騎士
qs.strat: 是非題逐項對照原文，注意 being tested 這類時態線索。

qs.s: What does “infrastructure” in Vehicle-to-Infrastructure refer to?
o: Traffic facilities and information systems.
The basic structure of roads and bridges.
Knowledge and regulations about safe driving.
The traffic department of the government.
qs.hint: 回到 V2I 的說明，看它跟哪些東西溝通。
qs.ev: V2I would allow vehicles to communicate with road signs or traffic signals and provide information to the vehicle about safety issues. V2I could also request traffic information from a traffic management system and access the best possible routes.
qs.ex: V2I 讓車與路標、號誌、交通管理系統溝通，所以 infrastructure 指交通設施與資訊系統。
why: (A) 正確：交通設施與資訊系統
(B) 不只是道路橋梁的基本結構
(C) 不是安全駕駛的知識法規
(D) 不是政府的交通部門
qs.strat: 詞義或指涉題用定義句或舉例推出範圍。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT a potential benefit of driverless cars?
o: The elderly will become more mobile.
“Drivers” can sleep in cars all the way to work.
People can race cars to their heart’s content.
A blind man can get into a car and travel safely.
qs.hint: 回到第2段列出好處的地方，找沒提到的一項。
qs.ev: People who commute by car will gain hours each day to work, rest, or read a newspaper.
qs.ex: 文中好處包括老人與盲人能行動、通勤者可休息，但完全沒提飆車競速的好處。
why: (A) 老年人更能行動，文中有提到
(B) 通勤時可休息，文中有提到
(C) 正確：文中沒提到可以盡情賽車
(D) 盲人安全出行，文中有提到
qs.strat: NOT 題逐項在原文找證據，找不到者為答案。

qs.s: What can be inferred from the passage?
o: Cars will refuse to start if the driver is drunk.
The future may be a vehicle-accident-free era.
Everyone, including children, can afford a car.
The production of driverless cars is still far away.
qs.hint: 看第1段末句降低車禍的比例，再想像技術成熟後的狀況。
qs.ev: Both V2V and V2I have the potential to reduce around 80 percent of vehicle crashes on the road.
qs.ex: 兩種技術可減少八成車禍，再加上無人駕駛不會有魯莽駕駛，可推論未來可能是幾乎沒有車禍的時代。
why: (A) 文中沒提酒駕就不能發動車子
(B) 正確：未來可能是沒有車禍的時代
(C) 年輕人省下保險費，不代表人人買得起車
(D) 文中預測五年內就會上市，不是還很遙遠
qs.strat: 推論題以原文事實為基礎，選最合理、不過度延伸的選項。

zh: 今天，汽車似乎週期性地出現躍進。各種駕駛輔助技術正出現在新車上。一種稱為車對車通訊（V2V）的發展中技術，正由汽車製造商測試，作為減少意外數量的方法。V2V 的運作方式是利用無線訊號，在車輛之間來回傳送有關位置、速度和方向的資訊，讓它們彼此保持安全距離。另一種正在測試的新技術是車對基礎設施通訊（V2I）。V2I 能讓車輛與路標或交通號誌溝通，並向車輛提供有關安全問題的資訊。V2I 也能向交通管理系統索取交通資訊，並取得最佳路線。V2V 和 V2I 都有潛力減少道路上約八成的車禍。

越來越多新車能夠倒車入庫、讀取交通標誌、在穩定車流中保持安全距離，並自動煞車以避免撞擊。此外，一些公司正在製造能自行開到選定目的地、不需人類操控的車。據預測，無人駕駛車將在五年內上市銷售。如果汽車完全變成無人駕駛，好處將非常巨大。Google 已經使用這種原型車在加州高速公路接送員工，還曾讓一位盲人坐進原型車，並拍下他被載去買外帶漢堡的畫面。若能成功，大量的老年人與身障者將重獲個人行動能力。年輕人將不必支付負擔沉重的汽車保險，因為他們魯莽的手腳不會再碰到方向盤或油門。開車通勤的人每天將多出好幾個小時，可以工作、休息或看報紙。
summary: 文章先介紹 V2V、V2I 兩種車輛通訊技術能大幅減少車禍，再說明無人駕駛車將帶給行動不便者、年輕人與通勤者許多好處。結構是先技術、後好處。

title: 太武國小古調傳唱隊
text: In 2009, the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers were invited to perform in Belgium, France, Germany, and Luxemburg. In 2011, they were voted as one of the world’s top five performance groups by audiences of Japan Broadcasting Corporation’s Amazing Voice program.

Recalling the group’s first tour in Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers, admitted that he felt very nervous. He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound. Surprisingly, the audience listened with full focus and high spirits. Camake said, “They told me afterward that through our performance, they had a vision of our country, our village, without having to visit it. This experience greatly boosted our confidence.”

According to Camake Valaule, singing traditional ballads has helped students and their parents to re-understand their culture. “It used to be that the only ones who could sing these songs were tribal elders aged between 50 and 60. Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’ Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.”

Winning international fame, however, was neither the original intention nor the main reason why Camake founded the group in 2006. The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture. Referring to the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School and Taiwu Village following Typhoon Morakot in August 2009, Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along. As long as the children are willing to sing, I will always be there for them, singing with them and leading them to experience the meaning of the ballads.”
pre: 這是一篇介紹原住民孩子合唱團的報導，透過創辦人的話說明傳唱歌謠的意義。留意他說過的話（引號內）反映的想法。
gist: 太武國小古調傳唱隊曾赴歐洲演出，也獲選為世界前五大表演團體。
創辦人擔心觀眾會睡著，但觀眾專注聆聽，也讓團員更有信心。
傳唱歌謠幫助學生與家長重新認識自己的文化。
創辦團隊的目的是傳承文化，颱風後遷校讓他體會到文化比房子更能帶走。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers?
o: The group was first established in 2009.
The group was founded by a PE teacher.
The singers usually sing popular folk songs.
The singers learn to sing from their parents.
qs.hint: 找第2段介紹 Camake Valaule 身分的那句話。
qs.ev: Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers
qs.ex: 文中說 Camake 是體育老師，也是合唱團的創辦人，所以團體由體育老師創辦。
why: (A) 團體成立於2006年，2009年是歐洲巡演
(B) 正確：由體育老師創辦
(C) 他們唱的是傳統歌謠，不是流行民歌
(D) 是孩子教父母，不是向父母學唱
qs.strat: 是非題逐項對照原文，注意年份與人物身分。

qs.s: On his first trip to Europe, why did Camake think the audience might fall asleep?
o: The average age of the audience was between fifty and sixty.
Most of the performance was not accompanied by any instrument.
Nobody could understand the language and the meaning of the songs.
The audience could not visualize the theme sung by the school children.
qs.hint: 看第2段 worried 後面的原因（since 引導）。
qs.ev: He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound.
qs.ex: 他怕觀眾睡著，因為大部分演出是無伴奏，也就是沒有樂器伴奏。
why: (A) 與觀眾年紀無關，50到60歲是部落耆老
(B) 正確：大部分演出沒有樂器伴奏
(C) 文中沒說聽不懂語言
(D) 文中沒說觀眾無法想像主題
qs.strat: 原因題找 since / because 後面的內容。

qs.s: What does “the pieces of a blurred memory” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
o: The children’s ignorance of their own culture.
The fading memories about old tribal people.
The broken pieces of knowledge taught at school.
The parents’ vague understanding of their own tradition.
qs.hint: 看第3段，這句話之前說孩子們教父母唱歌，之後想想什麼東西模糊了。
qs.ev: According to Camake Valaule, singing traditional ballads has helped students and their parents to re-understand their culture.
qs.ex: 孩子教父母唱歌，幫助父母重新認識文化，所以模糊的記憶碎片指父母對傳統文化的模糊理解。
why: (A) 不是孩子無知，而是父母記憶模糊
(B) 不是在說老人逐漸被遺忘
(C) 與學校知識無關
(D) 正確：父母對自身傳統的模糊理解
qs.strat: 比喻性片語要回到前後文找出具體所指。

qs.s: What did Camake realize after the incident of Typhoon Morakot?
o: The significance of the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School.
The need to respect nature to avoid being destroyed by it.
The importance of passing on the traditional culture.
The consequence of building houses in the forest.
qs.hint: 看最後一段，Camake 談颱風後遷校說了什麼。
qs.ev: We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along.
qs.ex: 遷移時帶不走森林與房子，卻能帶走文化，使他體會到傳承傳統文化的重要。
why: (A) 遷校是事件，不是他領悟的重點
(B) 文中沒說要尊重自然
(C) 正確：傳承傳統文化的重要
(D) 文中沒提在森林蓋房子的後果
qs.strat: 領悟題找引述中的結論句，通常是 but 之後。

zh: 2009年，太武國小古調傳唱隊受邀到比利時、法國、德國和盧森堡演出。2011年，他們被日本放送協會《驚奇聲音》節目的觀眾票選為世界五大表演團體之一。
回想團隊首次的歐洲巡演，體育老師也是太武國小古調傳唱隊創辦人的卡瑪克・瓦勞勒坦承自己非常緊張。他擔心觀眾會睡著，因為75分鐘的演出大多是無伴奏合唱，也就是沒有樂器聲的歌唱。令人驚訝的是，觀眾聽得全神貫注、情緒高昂。卡瑪克說：「他們事後告訴我，透過我們的表演，他們不用去拜訪，就對我們的國家、我們的村落有了一個景象。這個經驗大大提升了我們的信心。」
據卡瑪克・瓦勞勒說，傳唱傳統歌謠幫助學生和他們的父母重新認識自己的文化。「過去，會唱這些歌的只有50到60歲的部落耆老。現在有了孩子們來演唱，父母開始問：『為什麼我們不會唱這些歌？』現在很多時候是孩子在教父母唱歌，把模糊記憶的碎片拼回來。」
然而，贏得國際名聲既不是卡瑪克2006年成立這個團體的初衷，也不是主要原因。最重要的是讓孩子們明白為什麼唱這些歌，並保存和傳承他們的文化。談到2009年8月莫拉克颱風後太武國小與太武村的遷移，卡瑪克說：「我們無法把森林或山上的房子帶走，但我們能把文化帶著走。只要孩子們願意唱，我就會一直陪著他們，一起唱，帶領他們體會歌謠的意義。」
summary: 報導先說團體的國際成就，再談創辦人從緊張到受到鼓勵，接著說明歌謠幫助家長與孩子重新認識文化，最後強調團體的真正目的是傳承文化。

title: 過度醫療的代價
text: When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.

Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.

After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.
pre: 這篇先提出「過多的醫療未必更好」的觀點，再用鮑爾太太的案例說明。留意案例裡的醫生做了哪些過度的事。
gist: 作者指出許多人以為醫療越多越好，但過度治療可能造成傷害。
鮑爾太太得了罕見疾病，醫生不斷要求回診、檢查與轉診，花費龐大。
夫妻起疑後換了新醫生，不再例行檢查，病情反而穩定。

qs.s: What is the main idea of this passage?
o: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.
qs.hint: 看第1段的轉折（But what they do not realize），那是作者想強調的重點。
qs.ev: But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm.
qs.ex: 作者指出過度治療可能有害，並以案例說明，所以主旨是過多的醫療未必對病人有益。
why: (A) 文中並未說治療不會有副作用
(B) 病人以為越多越好只是現象，不是主旨
(C) 正確：過多的醫療未必對病人有益
(D) 文中批評醫生要求不必要的回診
qs.strat: 主旨題抓轉折句與全文的共同結論。

qs.s: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?
o: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.
qs.hint: 回到第2段，找檢查結果為陰性之後醫生做了什麼。
qs.ev: Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold.
qs.ex: 即使檢查結果陰性，醫生還是開更多檢查，所以問題是檢查正常卻仍被要求更多測試。
why: (A) 她感冒時住院，但文中沒說住三週
(B) 文中沒提沒有保險
(C) 正確：結果正常仍被開立更多檢查
(D) 文中是連輕微不適也一再轉介，並非因她不斷抱怨
qs.strat: 細節題小心選項中的細節（三週、沒保險）是否真的出現。

qs.s: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
o: Physicians.
Other patients.
Mr. and Mrs. Power.
The online support groups.
qs.hint: 看引號中這句話，想想誰可能越界（crossed the line）。
qs.ev: It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said.
qs.ex: 鮑爾先生說很難判斷何時他們越界，指的是醫生何時進行過度的治療，所以 they 指醫師。
why: (A) 正確：醫師
(B) 其他病人是提供意見者，不是越界者
(C) 他自己夫妻不會越界
(D) 線上互助團體只是諮詢對象
qs.strat: 代名詞題從句意找出做出動作的人，而非最近出現的名詞。

qs.s: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?
o: More tests than necessary are too much.
Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.
qs.hint: 看第1段與全文，作者對檢查的整體看法。
qs.ev: Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.
qs.ex: 作者認為檢查有時會導致更多檢查與不需要的治療，因此態度是超過需要的檢查太多了。
why: (A) 正確：超過必要的檢查太多
(B) 文中並未說檢查對預防至關重要
(C) 文中沒說診斷需要大量測試
(D) 文中沒說醫生很少判讀錯誤
qs.strat: 態度題看作者的描述用詞（harm, left alone）找出傾向。

zh: 談到醫療照護，許多病人與醫生都相信「越多越好」。但他們沒有意識到，過度治療（過多的掃描、過多的血液檢驗、過多的處置）可能造成傷害。有時候，一項檢查會把你引上一條越來越多檢查的路，其中有些可能是侵入性的，或是對本該置之不理的狀況進行治療。
例如，泰倫斯・鮑爾抱怨，在他太太得知罹患韋格納氏肉芽腫（一種罕見的免疫系統疾病）後，他們發現很難拒絕她的醫生所建議的檢查。醫生堅持每三週回診，即使她覺得很好。他常常開血液檢驗與X光，並且為了即使輕微的不適一再轉介她去看專科醫生。即使檢查結果是陰性，仍會開更多檢查，她感冒時還被當作預防措施而住院。她在六個月期間多達25次看診。這對夫妻每年花約三萬美元在她的照護上。
經過數年身體上的痛苦與幾乎因醫療費用而破產之後，這對夫妻在與線上互助團體的其他病人諮詢後，開始質疑這種治療。鮑爾先生說：「很難判斷他們什麼時候越線。你以為她得到全世界最好的照顧，但一段時間後你開始想：目標是什麼？」鮑爾先生接著與他自己的家庭醫師談，醫師建議他找一位新的專科醫生來負責鮑爾太太的照護。在新醫生的照顧下，例行檢查停止了，鮑爾太太的病情也穩定下來。現在她一年只看醫生四、五次。
summary: 作者先提出過度醫療可能有害的觀點，再用鮑爾太太的案例說明過多檢查帶來的身心與經濟負擔，最後以換醫生後病情穩定作對照。結構是觀點加案例。

title: 攝影大師布列松
text: Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908–2004) is one of the most original and influential figures in the history of photography. His humane, spontaneous photographs helped establish photojournalism as an art form.

Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor. Educated in Paris, Cartier-Bresson developed an early love for literature and the arts. As a teenager, Cartier-Bresson rebelled against his parents’ formal ways of education. In his early adulthood, he even drifted toward communism. But it was art that remained at the center of his life.

Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar. And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography. He then wandered around the world with his camera, using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.

Not long after World War II, Cartier-Bresson traveled east, spending considerable time in India, where he met and photographed Gandhi shortly before his assassination in 1948. Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.

Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography remained much the same throughout his life. He made clear his dislike of images that had been improved by artificial light, darkroom effects, and even cropping. The naturalist in Cartier-Bresson believed that all editing should be done when the photo is taken. In 1952, his first book, The Decisive Moment, a rich collection of his work spanning two decades, was published. “There is nothing in this world that does not have a decisive moment,” he said.
In 1968, he began to turn away from photography and returned to his passion for drawing and painting.
pre: 這是一篇依時間順序介紹攝影家生平的文章。留意他的家庭背景、轉折（非洲之行）、重要作品與攝影理念。
gist: 布列松是史上最具原創性與影響力的攝影家之一，開創新聞攝影的藝術性。
他出身富裕卻節儉的家庭，從小愛好文學與藝術，青少年時反抗正規教育。
1931年非洲之行激起他對攝影的興趣，從此帶著相機漫遊世界。
二戰後他在印度拍攝甘地並記錄其死後影響，成為《生活》雜誌的名作。
他一生堅持不靠人工光線、暗房或裁切，主張在拍照時就完成編輯，並出版《決定性瞬間》。
1968年起，他轉而回到繪畫。

qs.s: Which of the following best describes Cartier-Bresson’s family background?
o: His family was rich but was very economical.
His father went to Paris to open a textile factory.
His wealthy family went bankrupt and became poor.
His parents were very liberal in their ways of education.
qs.hint: 看第2段開頭，家庭財富與父母的生活方式。
qs.ev: Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.
qs.ex: 他家富有，卻因父母節儉常讓人覺得像貧窮，所以是富有但很節儉。
why: (A) 正確：富有但很節儉
(B) 文中沒說父親到巴黎開廠
(C) 家境沒有破產
(D) 他反抗父母正式的教育方式，並非自由開放
qs.strat: 選項常有半對半錯，須逐字對照原文每個細節。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s career in photography?
o: He devoted himself to photography all his life.
He developed a passion for photography when he traveled to Africa.
He quit photography right after the publication of The Decisive Moment.
During World War II, he documented the everyday life of the Indian people.
qs.hint: 找第3段 Africa 那句，看非洲帶給他什麼。
qs.ev: Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar. And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography.
qs.ex: 他去非洲打獵，非洲激起他對攝影的興趣，所以是旅行非洲時產生攝影熱情。
why: (A) 1968年起他轉向繪畫，並非一生攝影
(B) 正確：到非洲旅行時發展出攝影熱情
(C) 他出版《決定性瞬間》在1952年，之後仍拍到1968年
(D) 他是二戰後才去印度，不是戰爭期間
qs.strat: 年代題要對照時間線，排除年份不符的選項。

qs.s: What significance did Cartier-Bresson have to Gandhi of India?
o: He witnessed Gandhi’s assassination in 1948.
He was the first photographer to take Gandhi’s photo.
He used photos to document the effect of Gandhi’s death on India.
His photos told the world who was guilty of assassinating Gandhi.
qs.hint: 看第4段關於甘地的敘述，重點在他的作品做了什麼。
qs.ev: Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.
qs.ex: 他的作品記錄了甘地死後對印度的立即影響，所以是用照片記錄甘地之死對國家的影響。
why: (A) 他在甘地死前不久拍攝，不是目睹暗殺
(B) 文中沒說他是第一位拍甘地的人
(C) 正確：用照片記錄甘地之死的影響
(D) 文中沒提照片揭露凶手
qs.strat: 意義題看文中對事件貢獻的具體描述。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography?
o: He never waited for a decisive moment to shoot photos.
He preferred to edit his images carefully in his darkroom.
Most of his photos described things that happen every day.
He experimented with different ways and settled on being a naturalist.
qs.hint: 看第3段他如何拍照，對照選項 C 的說法。
qs.ev: He then wandered around the world with his camera, using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.
qs.ex: 他用手持相機捕捉日常生活的瞬間，所以他的照片多半描述每天發生的事。
why: (A) 他相信每件事都有決定性瞬間，會等待時機
(B) 他不喜歡暗房修圖
(C) 正確：多半描述日常生活的事
(D) 文中說他的方法一生大致不變，沒有試驗不同方法
qs.strat: 是非題先找主題句，再核對選項是否與文意一致。

zh: 亨利・卡蒂埃-布列松（1908-2004）是攝影史上最具原創性與影響力的人物之一。他富有人情味又即興的照片，協助確立了新聞攝影作為一種藝術形式。
布列松的家境富裕（他父親靠紡織製造業賺了一大筆財富），但布列松後來開玩笑說，由於父母節儉，常讓人覺得家裡很窮。他在巴黎受教育，從小就愛上文學與藝術。青少年時，布列松反抗父母正規的教育方式。成年早期，他甚至一度傾向共產主義。但藝術始終是他生活的核心。
布列松1931年前往非洲打獵羚羊與野豬。非洲又激起了他的另一個興趣：攝影。之後他帶著相機漫遊世界，用手持相機捕捉日常生活中稍縱即逝的影像。
二戰後不久，布列松往東旅行，在印度待了相當長的時間，並在甘地遇刺前不久與他相遇並替他拍照，那是在1948年。布列松後來記錄甘地之死及其對國家的立即影響，成為《生活》雜誌最受推崇的攝影專題之一。
布列松對攝影的態度一生大致不變。他明確表示不喜歡經過人工光線、暗房效果，甚至裁切而「改良」的影像。他內心的自然主義者認為，所有編輯都應該在拍照時完成。1952年，他的第一本書《決定性瞬間》出版，是橫跨二十年作品的豐富集錦。他說：「這個世界上沒有什麼東西是沒有決定性瞬間的。」
1968年，他開始遠離攝影，回到他對繪畫與素描的熱情。
summary: 文章依時間順序介紹布列松：家庭背景、非洲之行引發攝影興趣、拍攝甘地的名作、堅持自然不修圖的理念，最後轉向繪畫。掌握時間線就能答對細節題。

title: 久坐病與健康
text: You’ve most likely heard the news by now: A car-commuting, desk-bound, TV-watching lifestyle can be harmful to our health. All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases that experts have named this modern-day health epidemic the “sitting disease.”

Sitting for too long slows down the body’s metabolism and the way enzymes break down our fat reserves, raising both blood sugar levels and blood pressure. Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down. And those small amounts of activity add up—30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise. But without that activity, blood sugar levels and blood pressure keep creeping up, steadily damaging the inside of the arteries and increasing the risk of diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and other serious diseases. In essence, fundamental changes in biology occur if you sit for too long.

But wait, you’re a runner. You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right? Well, not so fast. Recent studies show that people spend an average of 64 hours a week sitting, whether or not they exercise 150 minutes a week as recommended by World Health Organization (WHO). Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise. Overall, most people simply aren’t exercising or moving around enough to counteract all the harm that can result from sitting nine hours or more a day.
Scared straight out of your chair? Good. The remedy is as simple as standing up and taking activity breaks.
pre: 這篇談久坐對健康的傷害，並指出運動並不能完全抵消。注意作者使用的問句與口語語氣，以及最後給的解決辦法。
gist: 現代生活方式導致久坐，被稱為「久坐病」，增加多種致命疾病的風險。
久坐會讓代謝變慢、血糖與血壓上升，經常少量活動即可降下來。
即使固定運動，人們仍久坐過久，運動者在運動日也較不活躍，不足以抵消傷害。
解決辦法很簡單：站起來，經常休息活動。

qs.s: What is the purpose of this passage?
o: To point out the challenges of the modern lifestyle.
To discuss how a modern epidemic may spread quickly.
To explore the effects of regular exercise to our body.
To explain the threat to our health from long hours of sitting.
qs.hint: 看第1段，作者先說什麼生活方式有害，並給了什麼名稱。
qs.ev: All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases
qs.ex: 全文討論久坐不動帶來的健康威脅，並說明為何運動也不夠，所以目的是說明長時間久坐對健康的威脅。
why: (A) 不是在討論現代生活挑戰的全貌
(B) 不是在談流行病如何擴散
(C) 運動的影響不是重點
(D) 正確：說明久坐對健康的威脅
qs.strat: 寫作目的題看首段主題與結尾的結論。

qs.s: What does the word “sedentary” in the third paragraph most likely mean?
o: Modern.
Risky.
Inactive.
Epidemic.
qs.hint: 看第3段開頭，這裡的對比是『你有運動，所以不用擔心什麼』。
qs.ev: You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right?
qs.ex: 這句話承接前文的久坐危害，因此 sedentary 指不活動的、久坐的。
why: (A) Modern 不符合前文意思
(B) Risky 是結果而非字義
(C) 正確：不活動的
(D) Epidemic 是指流行病
qs.strat: 字義題找與前文呼應的詞，例如 sitting、rooted in the chair。

qs.s: What is the best way to bring down high blood sugar level and blood pressure?
o: Exercising for 150 minutes or more every week.
Getting rid of the habit of car commuting and TV watching.
Interrupting sitting time with light activity as often as possible.
Standing or moving around for at least two or three minutes every day.
qs.hint: 看第2段中間，作者如何降低血糖與血壓。
qs.ev: Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down.
qs.ex: 文中說一天中少量規律活動就足以降低上升的數值，所以最好方式是盡量以輕度活動打斷久坐。
why: (A) 每週運動150分鐘不夠抵銷久坐
(B) 文中沒說要戒掉通勤和看電視
(C) 正確：用輕度活動打斷久坐
(D) 兩三分鐘是舉例，不是每天最低標準
qs.strat: 找 best way 這類題，要找原文直接給的方法。

qs.s: Which of the following may be inferred about those who do serious exercise?
o: They often live longer than those who don’t exercise.
They tend to stand or move around less on days they work out.
They generally spend less time sitting than those who are inactive.
They usually do not meet the standard of exercise recommended by WHO.
qs.hint: 看第3段，運動者在運動日的活動量。
qs.ev: Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise.
qs.ex: 研究發現規律運動者在運動日其他時間活動量約少三成，可推論他們在運動日較少站立走動。
why: (A) 文中沒說他們比較長壽
(B) 正確：運動日其他時間較少站立走動
(C) 文中說人們不論有無運動都坐很久
(D) 文中沒說他們不達標
qs.strat: 推論題要根據原文數據，不要擴張成原文沒說的結論。

zh: 你很可能已經聽過這個消息：開車通勤、被綁在書桌前、看電視的生活方式可能對我們的健康有害。我們坐在椅子上生根的所有時間，都與許多致命疾病的風險增加有關，以至於專家把這種現代的健康流行病稱為「久坐病」。

坐太久會減慢身體的新陳代謝以及酵素分解脂肪儲備的速度，使血糖和血壓都升高。一整天裡少量規律的活動，即使只是站起來走動，就足以讓升高的數值降回來。而且這些少量活動會累積：以兩、三分鐘為單位進行共30分鐘的輕度活動，可以和半小時一整段運動一樣有效。但沒有這些活動，血糖和血壓會持續攀升，穩定地傷害動脈內側，並增加糖尿病、心臟病、中風和其他嚴重疾病的風險。基本上，如果你坐太久，身體的生理就會發生根本的改變。
但等一下，你是跑者。你不必擔心久坐生活方式的危害，因為你規律運動，對吧？嗯，先別急。最新研究顯示，不論是否達到世界衛生組織建議的每週150分鐘運動，人們平均每週坐64小時。此外，規律運動者在他們運動的日子裡活動量被發現少約30%。整體而言，大多數人根本沒有足夠的運動或走動，來抵消每天坐九小時以上可能造成的所有傷害。
被嚇得從椅子上站起來了嗎？很好。解決辦法就像站起來、做活動休息一樣簡單。
summary: 文章先說明久坐的健康危害及原理，再指出規律運動也無法完全抵消，最後以站起來活動作為簡單的解決方式。結構是問題、原因、迷思、解方。

title: 日本的血型迷思
text: In Japan, a person’s blood type is popularly believed to decide his/her temperament and personality. Type-A people are generally considered sensitive perfectionists and good team players, but over-anxious. Type Os are curious and generous but stubborn. Type ABs are artistic but mysterious and unpredictable, and type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish. Though lacking scientific evidence, this belief is widely seen in books, magazines, and television shows.

The blood-type belief has been used in unusual ways. The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player. Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines, and even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type. In 1990, Mitsubishi Electronics was reported to have announced the formation of a team composed entirely of AB workers, thanks to “their ability to make plans.”

The belief even affects politics. One former prime minister considered it important enough to reveal in his official profile that he was a type A, while his opposition rival was type B. In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised. In his resignation speech, he blamed his failings on the fact that he was blood type B.

The blood-type craze, considered simply harmless fun by some Japanese, may manifest itself as prejudice and discrimination. In fact, this seems so common that the Japanese now have a term for it: bura-hara, meaning blood-type harassment. There are reports of discrimination leading to children being bullied, ending of happy relationships, and loss of job opportunities due to blood type.
pre: 這篇談日本人相信血型決定個性的現象，從日常、職場到政治，最後談帶來的歧視。留意作者是在陳述事實（如 reportedly），還是表達自己的好惡。
gist: 日本人普遍相信血型決定個性，雖缺乏科學證據，仍廣泛流傳。
血型信仰被用在運動訓練、幼稚園教學和公司人事安排。
它甚至影響政治，有部長因個性失言而把原因怪到B型。
血型風潮可能造成偏見與歧視，甚至有專門名詞，造成霸凌與失業。

qs.s: What is the speaker’s attitude toward the blood-type belief in Japan?
o: Negative.
Defensive.
Objective.
Encouraging.
qs.hint: 注意作者多用 is reported to、reportedly 等轉述字眼，看他是在陳述事實還是表達好惡。
qs.ev: Some kindergartens have adopted teaching methods along blood group lines, and even major companies reportedly make decisions about assignments based on an employee’s blood type.
qs.ex: 作者多用 is reported to、reportedly 等轉述方式陳述各種現象，提到缺乏科學證據與可能造成的歧視時也只是說明事實，沒有直接表達褒貶，所以態度是客觀的。
why: (A) 雖提到偏見與歧視，但只是陳述現象，沒有直接批評
(B) 作者沒有為它辯護
(C) 正確：客觀的
(D) 作者不是鼓勵
qs.strat: 態度題看作者用字：多用 reportedly、is reported to 等轉述字眼、不加個人褒貶時，態度通常是客觀的。

qs.s: According to the examples mentioned in the passage, which blood type can we infer is the LEAST favored in Japan?
o: Type A.
Type B.
Type O.
Type AB.
qs.hint: 看第1段對 B 型的描述，再看第3段部長的辭職。
qs.ev: and type Bs are cheerful but eccentric, individualistic, and selfish.
qs.ex: B型被描述為古怪、自私，而松本部長因失態而把責任歸咎於自己是B型，可推論B型最不受歡迎。
why: (A) A型被描述為好的團隊成員
(B) 正確：B型最不受歡迎
(C) O型有好奇與慷慨的特質
(D) AB型被認為有計劃能力
qs.strat: 比較題逐一看各類型被怎麼描述，找負面最多的。

qs.s: Why did Prime Minister Ryu Matsumoto resign from office?
o: He revealed his rival’s blood type.
He was seen behaving rudely on TV.
He blamed his failings on local officials.
He was discriminated against because of blood type.
qs.hint: 找第3段 Ryu Matsumoto 辭職的原因，注意 when 後面。
qs.ev: In 2011, a minister, Ryu Matsumoto, was forced to resign after only a week in office, when a bad-tempered encounter with local officials was televised.
qs.ex: 他因與地方官員的壞脾氣衝突被電視播出，而被迫辭職，也就是被看到在電視上舉止無禮。
why: (A) 他洩漏的是自己的血型，不是對手的
(B) 正確：被看到在電視上行為無禮
(C) 他是把失敗歸咎血型，不是歸咎官員
(D) 他沒有被歧視，只是自己怪血型
qs.strat: 原因題分清是真正的原因，還是他自己找的藉口。

qs.s: Which field is NOT mentioned in the passage as being affected by blood-type beliefs?
o: Education.
Sports.
Business.
Medicine.
qs.hint: 逐項在第2段找運動、教育、商業對應的例子。
qs.ev: The women’s softball team that won gold for Japan at the Beijing Olympics is reported to have used blood-type theories to customize training for each player.
qs.ex: 第2段提到壘球隊（運動）、幼稚園（教育）、公司（商業），但沒有提到醫療。
why: (A) 教育有提到幼稚園
(B) 運動有提到壘球隊
(C) 商業有提到公司的人事
(D) 正確：醫療文中沒提
qs.strat: NOT 題逐項在原文找證據，找不到的就是答案。

zh: 在日本，人們普遍相信一個人的血型決定他或她的氣質與個性。A型的人通常被認為是敏感的完美主義者與優秀的團隊成員，但過於焦慮。O型的人好奇又慷慨，但固執。AB型的人有藝術天分，但神祕又難以預測；B型的人開朗，但古怪、個人主義而且自私。雖然缺乏科學證據，這種信念在書籍、雜誌和電視節目中隨處可見。
血型信念被用在一些不尋常的方式上。據報導，在北京奧運為日本奪金的女子壘球隊，使用血型理論為每位球員量身訂做訓練。一些幼稚園採用依血型分組的教學方式，據說連大公司也依員工的血型來決定工作分派。1990年，據報導三菱電機宣布成立一支完全由AB型員工組成的團隊，原因是「他們擅長規劃」。
這種信念甚至影響政治。一位前首相認為這很重要，在他的官方簡介中透露自己是A型，而他的反對黨對手是B型。2011年，一位部長松本龍在就任僅一週後被迫辭職，因為他與地方官員一次脾氣暴躁的衝突被電視播出。在辭職演說中，他把自己的缺失歸咎於自己是B型。
血型熱潮，雖被一些日本人視為無害的趣味，卻可能表現為偏見與歧視。事實上，這種情況似乎非常普遍，以至於日本人現在有一個詞彙來形容：bura-hara，意思是血型騷擾。有報導指出，因血型而導致孩子被霸凌、幸福的關係結束，以及失去工作機會。
summary: 文章先介紹血型個性說，再列出它在運動、教育、職場與政治的應用，最後指出它造成偏見與歧視。結構是現象、例子、後果，作者以轉述事實的方式客觀陳述。

title: 小發明家的折疊凳
text: Like many other five-year-olds, Jeanie Low of Houston, Texas, would use a stool to help her reach the bathroom sink. However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family. After learning of an invention contest held by her school that year, Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.

Jeanie decided to make a stool attached to the bathroom cabinet door under the sink. She cut a plank of wood into two pieces, each about two feet wide and one foot long. Using metal hinges, Jeanie attached one piece of the wood to the front of the cabinet door, and the second piece to the first. The first piece was set just high enough so that when it swung out horizontally from the cabinet door, the second piece would swing down from the first, just touching the ground, and so serving as a support for the first piece of the wood. This created a convenient, sturdy platform for any person too short to reach the sink. When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets. Jeanie called her invention the “Kiddie Stool.”

Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool won first place in her school’s contest. Two years later, it was awarded first prize again at Houston’s first annual Invention Fair. As a result, Jeanie was invited to make a number of public appearances with her Kiddie Stool, and was featured on local TV as well as in newspapers. Many people found the story of the Kiddie Stool inspiring because it showed that with imagination, anyone can be an inventor.
pre: 這是一個小女孩發明東西的故事。讀的時候留意她遇到什麼問題、怎麼解決、結果如何。
gist: 五歲的潔妮因家中塑膠凳不穩又佔空間，決定為學校發明比賽發明新凳子。
她把木板用鉸鏈裝在櫃門上，做成可摺疊的堅固踏凳，不用時用磁鐵固定。
這項發明在比賽中獲獎，使她受邀公開露面，也激勵許多人。

qs.s: Why did Jeanie Low invent the Kiddie Stool, according to the passage?
o: Many other five-year-olds had problems reaching the bathroom sink.
She did not think that plastic stools were tall enough for her.
The stool in her bathroom was not firm and often got in the way.
She was invited to enter an invention contest held by her school.
qs.hint: 看第1段，找 However 之後她家裡凳子的問題。
qs.ev: However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family.
qs.ex: 家裡的塑膠凳不穩又佔空間，所以她想做一個固定在浴室又能收起來的凳子。
why: (A) 文中沒說很多五歲小孩都有這個問題
(B) 文中沒說塑膠凳不夠高
(C) 正確：凳子不穩又常擋路
(D) 比賽是契機，不是發明的原因
qs.strat: 原因題找 However 後面的問題說明。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about how the Kiddie Stool works?
o: The Kiddie Stool will swing out only when the cabinet door opens.
It uses hinges and magnets to keep the wooden pieces in place.
It swings from left to right to be attached to the cabinet door.
The platform is supported by two pieces of metal.
qs.hint: 看第2段最後幾句，不用時怎麼固定。
qs.ev: When not in use, the hinges allowed the two pieces of wood to fold back up tightly against the cabinet, where they were held in place by magnets.
qs.ex: 文中說用鉸鏈讓兩片木板折回，並用磁鐵固定，所以使用了鉸鏈與磁鐵。
why: (A) 櫃門打開時才擺動，文中沒這樣說
(B) 正確：用鉸鏈與磁鐵固定木板
(C) 它不是左右擺動，而是向下
(D) 支撐的是木板，不是金屬片
qs.strat: 機制題要對照原文描述的零件與動作。

qs.s: What are the characteristics of Jeanie’s Kiddie Stool?
o: Permanent and foldable.
Fragile and eye-catching.
Conventional and touching.
Convenient and recyclable.
qs.hint: 回到第1段，看她希望凳子有哪些特色。
qs.ev: Jeanie resolved to enter the contest by creating a stool that would be a permanent fixture in the bathroom, and yet could be kept out of the way when not in use.
qs.ex: 她要凳子能固定在浴室，又能收起來不擋路，也就是固定且可摺疊。
why: (A) 正確：固定且可摺疊
(B) 並非脆弱
(C) 不是傳統的，而是創新
(D) 沒有提到可回收
qs.strat: 特色題用文中的描述句直接比對形容詞。

qs.s: Which of the following sayings best captures the spirit of Jeanie Low’s story?
o: Failure is the mother of success.
There’s nothing new under the sun.
Necessity is the mother of invention.
Genius is 1% inspiration and 99% perspiration.
qs.hint: 想想她的發明是因什麼需要而產生。
qs.ev: However, the plastic step-stool she had at home was unstable and cluttered up the small bathroom shared by her whole family.
qs.ex: 她因為家裡凳子不方便才創造新凳子，符合『需要為發明之母』的精神。
why: (A) 失敗為成功之母，文中沒有失敗
(B) 日光之下無新事，與創新相反
(C) 正確：需要為發明之母
(D) 天才是百分之一的靈感加百分之九十九的努力，文中未強調努力
qs.strat: 諺語題先找故事的核心因果，再對應諺語。

zh: 和許多其他五歲小孩一樣，德州休士頓的潔妮・羅需要用凳子來幫助她搆到浴室的洗手台。然而，她家裡的塑膠踏凳不穩，還把她全家共用的小浴室弄得雜亂。在得知學校那年舉辦發明比賽後，潔妮決心參賽，做一個可以永久放在浴室，卻在不用時能收到不礙事地方的凳子。
潔妮決定做一個接在洗手台下櫃門上的凳子。她把一塊木板切成兩片，每片約兩英尺寬、一英尺長。她用金屬鉸鏈把其中一片裝在櫃門前面，第二片接在第一片上。第一片的高度剛好讓它從櫃門水平擺出時，第二片會從第一片向下擺，剛好碰到地面，作為第一片木板的支撐。這為任何太矮搆不到洗手台的人創造了方便又堅固的平台。不用時，鉸鏈能讓兩片木板緊貼著櫃子折起來，並用磁鐵固定。潔妮把她的發明稱為「兒童凳」。
潔妮的兒童凳在她學校的比賽中拿下第一名。兩年後，它又在休士頓首屆年度發明展中再次榮獲首獎。因此，潔妮受邀帶著她的兒童凳多次公開露面，也上了當地電視和報紙。許多人覺得兒童凳的故事鼓舞人心，因為它顯示只要有想像力，任何人都能成為發明家。
summary: 故事先交代問題（凳子不穩又佔空間），再描述解決方法（摺疊木凳），最後是獲獎與帶來的啟發。主旨是需要促成發明，想像力人人皆有。

title: 中東兒童失學危機
text: Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The report states that 40% of all children across the region are currently not receiving an education, which is a result of two consequences of violence: structural damage to schools and the displacement of populations, also called “forced migration.” Both issues result from the tide of violence that has crossed the region in recent years. The report examines nine countries where a state of war has become the norm. Across these countries, violence has made 8,500 schools unusable. In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.

The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011. With the crisis now in its fifth year, basic public services, including education, inside Syria have been stretched to breaking point. Within the country, the quality and availability of education depends on whether a particular region is suffering violence.

The report concludes with an earnest request to international policymakers to distribute financial and other resources to ease the regional crisis. With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance. The forces that are crushing individual lives and futures are also destroying the prospects for an entire region.
pre: 這是一篇依據聯合國報告寫成的報導，談衝突造成的教育問題。留意數字、原因（兩個後果）以及最後的呼籲。
gist: 聯合國兒童基金會報告指出中東衝突使超過一千三百萬兒童無法上學。
原因是學校受損與人口被迫遷徙，八千五百所學校不能使用，有的被當成避難所。
報告特別關注敘利亞，內戰使九百萬人流離失所，教育服務吃緊。
報告懇請國際決策者提供資源，因為整個世代的教育前途懸而未決。

qs.s: What is this article mainly about?
o: Why people are moving away from their own countries.
Why there are civil wars and violence in the Middle East.
Why many schools have become shelters for displaced families.
Why many children in the Middle East are not attending school.
qs.hint: 看第1段首句，它點出全文的核心議題。
qs.ev: Ongoing conflicts across the Middle East have prevented more than 13 million children from attending school, according to a report published by UNICEF, the United Nations Children’s Fund.
qs.ex: 全文圍繞衝突導致一千三百萬兒童無法上學，以及原因與影響，所以主旨是為何中東許多兒童沒上學。
why: (A) 遷徙只是原因之一
(B) 內戰成因不是重點
(C) 避難所只是例子
(D) 正確：為何中東許多兒童沒上學
qs.strat: 主旨題看首句與全文共同圍繞的主題。

qs.s: Why is “Iraq” mentioned in the second paragraph?
o: To convince people that temporary housing can be easily found.
To prove that classrooms there are big enough to host many families.
To give an example of why schools are not usable for children’s learning.
To show how structural damages of school can affect the quality of education.
qs.hint: 看這句話前面是什麼（8,500 schools unusable），伊拉克是用來舉什麼例。
qs.ev: In certain cases, communities have relied on school buildings to function as shelters for the displaced, with up to nine families living in a single classroom in former schools across Iraq.
qs.ex: 伊拉克的例子說明學校被當成避難所，使學校無法讓孩子上課，所以是學校無法用於學習的例子。
why: (A) 不是要說明臨時住所容易找
(B) 不是說教室夠大
(C) 正確：說明學校為何不能供孩子學習使用
(D) 例子不是談結構損毀影響品質，而是被占用
qs.strat: 舉例目的題，找例子所支持的上一句論點。

qs.s: What does the phrase “in the balance” in the last paragraph most likely mean?
o: Being well taken care of.
In an uncertain situation.
Under control by the authority.
Moving in the wrong direction.
qs.hint: 看這句話整體：一千三百萬孩子被趕出教室，一個世代的教育前途如何。
qs.ev: With more than 13 million children already driven from classrooms by conflict, it is no exaggeration to say that the educational prospects of a generation of children are in the balance.
qs.ex: in the balance 指前途未定、處於不確定的狀態，與前文孩子被趕出教室的危機相呼應。
why: (A) 被好好照顧不符合危機語氣
(B) 正確：處於不確定的狀況
(C) 不是受政府控制
(D) 不是朝錯誤方向移動，而是未定
qs.strat: 慣用語題用上下文語氣判斷詞義。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
o: The war in Syria has been going on since 2011.
More than nine thousand schools have been destroyed by wars.
Thirteen million people have been forced to leave their homes in the Middle East.
Forty percent of all children in the world are not attending schools due to ongoing conflict.
qs.hint: 看第3段 Syria 的敘述，找年份。
qs.ev: The report pays particularly close attention to Syria, where a bloody civil war has displaced at least nine million people since the war began in 2011.
qs.ex: 敘利亞的戰爭自2011年開始，並持續至今，所以選項A正確。
why: (A) 正確：敘利亞戰爭自2011年持續
(B) 八千五百所學校是無法使用，不是被摧毀，且不到九千
(C) 一千三百萬是兒童失學人數，不是流離失所人數
(D) 百分之四十是中東地區兒童，不是全世界
qs.strat: 數字題小心主體與範圍（地區或全世界）。

zh: 聯合國兒童基金會（UNICEF）發表的一份報告指出，整個中東持續的衝突使超過一千三百萬名兒童無法上學。
報告指出，該地區有40%的兒童目前沒有接受教育，這是暴力的兩個後果造成的：學校結構受損，以及人口流離失所（也稱為「被迫遷徙」）。這兩個問題都來自近年橫掃該地區的暴力浪潮。報告檢視了九個戰爭狀態已成常態的國家。在這些國家，暴力使8,500所學校無法使用。在某些情況下，社區依賴學校建築作為流離失所者的避難所，在伊拉克各地的前學校中，多達九個家庭住在同一間教室。
報告特別關注敘利亞，那裡血腥的內戰自2011年開始以來，已使至少九百萬人流離失所。隨著這場危機進入第五年，敘利亞境內包括教育在內的基本公共服務已被拉到瀕臨崩潰。在該國境內，教育的品質與可得性取決於特定地區是否正遭受暴力。
報告最後懇切請求國際決策者分配財務與其他資源以緩解區域危機。在已有超過一千三百萬名兒童因衝突被趕出教室的情況下，說一整個世代孩子的教育前途懸而未決並不誇張。那些壓垮個人生命與未來的力量，也正在摧毀整個地區的前景。
summary: 報導先說明中東衝突使一千三百萬孩子失學，接著解釋兩個原因（學校受損與人口遷徙）、以敘利亞為重點案例，最後呼籲國際協助。

title: 海蛇如何喝水
text: Many marine animals, including penguins and marine iguanas, have evolved ways to get rid of excess salt by using special salt-expelling glands around their tongue. However, the sea snake’s salt glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater. This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink. If seawater is not an option, how does this animal survive in the ocean?

An international team of researchers focused on a population of yellow-bellied sea snakes living near Costa Rica, where rain often does not fall for up to seven months out of the year. Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water. When it rains, a thin layer of fresh water forms on top of the ocean, providing the snakes with a fleeting opportunity to lap up that precious resource. But during the dry season when there is no rain, snakes presumably have nothing to drink. Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.

The researchers collected more than 500 yellow-bellied sea snakes and weighed them. They found that during the dry season about half of the snakes accepted fresh water offered to them, while nearly none did during the wet season. A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more. Finally, as predicted, snakes captured during the dry season contained significantly less body water than those scooped up in the rainy season. Thus, it seems the snake is able to endure certain degrees of dehydration in between rains. Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.
pre: 這篇說明一項科學研究：提出問題、研究方法、發現與結論。讀的時候依照這個順序找資訊。
gist: 許多海洋動物能排鹽，但海蛇的鹽腺處理不了海水，牠們如何取得淡水成為疑問。
研究團隊針對哥斯大黎加附近的黃腹海蛇，想測試牠們在海上是否會脫水。
研究發現旱季蛇較願意喝淡水、體內水分較少，顯示牠們能忍受兩次降雨間的脫水，脫水可能與族群減少有關。

qs.s: What is the purpose of the study described in this passage?
o: To test if sea snakes lose body water at sea.
