To see whether sea snakes drink water offered to them.
To find out if sea snakes are greatly reduced in population.
To prove that sea snakes drink only water coming from rivers.
qs.hint: 看第2段最後一句，Thus 後面說明研究團隊的興趣。
qs.ev: Thus, the team became interested in testing whether sea snakes became dehydrated at sea.
qs.ex: 研究團隊想測試海蛇在海上是否會脫水，這就是研究目的。
why: (A) 正確：測試海蛇在海上是否失去體內水分
(B) 給蛇水喝只是研究方法
(C) 族群減少是最後的推論
(D) 文中說雨水才是淡水來源，不是河水
qs.strat: 研究目的題找 interested in、aim 等字，通常在方法之前。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about sea snakes?
o: Their salt glands can remove the salt in the seawater.
They can drink seawater when it mixes with rainwater.
The ocean is like a desert to them since they don’t drink seawater.
They usually live near the coastal area where there is more fresh water.
qs.hint: 看第2段 rain 與 fresh water 的關係。
qs.ev: Because yellow-bellied sea snakes usually spend all of their time far from land, rain is the animals’ only source of fresh water.
qs.ex: 牠們不能喝海水，遠離陸地，只能靠雨水取得淡水，所以海洋對牠們來說像沙漠。
why: (A) 牠們的鹽腺無法處理海水中的鹽
(B) 海水混雨水不是文中說法
(C) 正確：海洋像沙漠，因為牠們不能喝海水
(D) 牠們常遠離陸地，不是住在沿岸
qs.strat: 是非題找關鍵字（only source），再判斷比喻是否合理。

qs.s: Which of the following is one of the findings of the study?
o: If a sea snake was dried and weak, it drank more fresh water.
If captured in the wet season, sea snakes drank a lot of fresh water.
Most of the sea snakes had lost a lot of body water when captured.
Dehydration is not a problem among sea snakes since they live at sea.
qs.hint: 看第3段研究發現，找蛇的身體狀況與喝水的關係。
qs.ev: A snake’s likelihood to drink also correlated with its body condition, with more withered snakes being more likely to drink, and to drink more.
qs.ex: 越乾癟的蛇越可能喝，也喝得越多，所以乾又虛弱的蛇喝更多淡水。
why: (A) 正確：乾癟虛弱的蛇喝更多淡水
(B) 雨季時幾乎沒有蛇接受淡水
(C) 旱季捕獲的蛇才較少體內水分，並非大多數蛇
(D) 脫水是個問題，並非沒事
qs.strat: 發現題在方法之後，找 found、correlated 等字。

qs.s: What can be inferred from the study?
o: Sea snakes can easily survive long years of drought.
Evolution will very likely enable sea snakes to drink seawater.
Sea snakes will be the last creature affected by global warming.
The sea snakes’ population distribution is closely related to rainfall.
qs.hint: 看最後一句，科學家如何連結脫水與族群。
qs.ev: Scientists believe that dehydration at sea may explain the declining populations of sea snakes in some parts of the world.
qs.ex: 科學家認為海上脫水可能與族群減少有關，因此可推論海蛇的分布與降雨密切相關。
why: (A) 牠們只能忍受一定程度的脫水，不是能長年撐過乾旱
(B) 文中沒提海蛇會演化出喝海水
(C) 文中沒提全球暖化
(D) 正確：族群分布與降雨密切相關
qs.strat: 推論題用研究結論往前延伸一步，不要超出原文。

zh: 許多海洋動物，包括企鵝和海鬣蜥，已演化出排除多餘鹽分的方法，使用舌頭周圍特殊的排鹽腺。然而，海蛇的鹽腺無法處理牠們若真喝海水時進入身體的大量鹽分。這在取得足夠飲水方面造成了嚴重問題。如果海水不是選項，這種動物如何在海洋中生存？
一個國際研究團隊把焦點放在哥斯大黎加附近的一群黃腹海蛇上，那裡的雨經常長達一年中七個月都不下。由於黃腹海蛇通常整天遠離陸地，雨水是牠們唯一的淡水來源。下雨時，海洋表面會形成一層薄薄的淡水，讓蛇有短暫機會舔食這項珍貴資源。但在沒有下雨的乾季，蛇大概沒有東西可喝。因此，研究團隊對測試海蛇是否在海上脫水產生了興趣。
研究人員捕捉了500多條黃腹海蛇並替牠們秤重。他們發現，在乾季約有一半的蛇接受了提供的淡水，而雨季時幾乎沒有蛇接受。蛇是否可能喝水也與牠的身體狀況有關，越乾癟的蛇越可能喝，也喝得越多。最後，如同預測，乾季捕獲的蛇體內水分明顯少於雨季撈起的蛇。因此，蛇似乎能在兩次降雨之間忍受一定程度的脫水。科學家認為，海上脫水可能解釋世界部分地區海蛇族群的減少。
summary: 文章先提出問題：海蛇不能喝海水怎麼辦，再描述研究方法與發現（乾季蛇更渴、體內水分更少），最後推論脫水可能影響族群。結構是問題、研究、發現、結論。

title: 狗狗的智商測驗 Dognition
genre: 說明文・科普／產品介紹
text: Is your dog an Einstein or a Charmer? For US $60, a recently-founded company called Dognition will help you learn more about your dog’s cognitive traits. It offers an online test telling you about the brain behind the bark.

Dognition’s test measures a dog’s intellect in several aspects—from empathy to memory to reasoning skills. But don’t expect it to measure your pet’s IQ. Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders, says a dog’s intelligence can’t be described with a single number. Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs. The question is what type your dog relies on more.

After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog: For example, how excited does your dog get around other dogs, or children? Do fireworks scare your pup? Then, Dognition guides you through tests that are as fun as playing fetch or hide-and-seek. At the end, you get a report of your dog’s cognitive profile.

Your dog could fall into one of nine categories: Ace, Stargazer, Maverick, Charmer, Socialite, Protodog, Einstein, Expert, or Renaissance Dog. That can give you something to brag about on Dognition’s Facebook page. It also can shed new light on why dogs do the things they do. For example, a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes.
Dognition helps people understand their dogs in ways that they have never been able to do. This new understanding can enrich the relationship between dogs and their owners.
pre: 這是一篇介紹新產品（狗狗智力測驗）的文章。讀的時候注意每一段在做什麼：介紹產品、說明測驗內容、說明流程、介紹分類結果。
gist: Dognition 提供線上測驗，讓你了解愛犬的認知特質。
測驗衡量多方面的能力，但不是單一的智商數字。
測驗流程：先填問卷，再做遊戲式測驗，最後得到報告。
狗狗會被分成九種類型，Charmer 是依賴主人提供資訊的類型。
這項測驗能加深主人與狗的關係。

qs.s: What is the third paragraph mainly about?
o: The theory behind the questionnaire used in the Dognition test.
The procedure for evaluating a dog’s intellect on Dognition.
The products one can get by paying a fee to Dognition.
The characteristics of the activities Dognition offers.
qs.hint: 只看第三段：注意 After…、Then…、At the end 這些表示先後的詞。
qs.ev: After you plunk your money down, Dognition’s website will take you through a questionnaire about your dog
qs.ex: 第三段依序說付費後先填問卷、接著做測驗、最後拿到報告，就是評估狗狗智力的流程（procedure）。
why: (A) 段中只舉問卷例子，沒有談問卷背後的理論。
(B) 對：依序介紹問卷、測驗、報告的步驟。
(C) 付費可得到的『產品』不是本段重點。
(D) 只提到遊戲像 fetch，並非主要在談活動特性。
qs.strat: 段落主旨題：找出這一段表示順序的線索詞，選能概括整段的選項，不要選只涵蓋一個細節的。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
o: Different dogs display strengths in different intelligences.
A dog’s cognitive profile is composed of nine cognitive skills.
The purpose of Dognition’s testing is to control a dog’s behavior.
A dog’s intelligence can be ranked based on the score of a Dognition’s test.
qs.hint: 回到第二段，看 Dr. Hare 怎麼說智力。
qs.ev: Just as humans have a wide range of intelligences, so do dogs.
qs.ex: 第二段說人有多種智力，狗也一樣，所以不同的狗擅長的智力類型不同。
why: (A) 對：與 so do dogs 一致。
(B) 是九種『類型』，不是九種技能。
(C) 目的是了解狗，不是控制行為。
(D) 文中說智力無法用單一數字表示，不能排名。
qs.strat: 是非題：把每個選項拿回原文逐一對照，注意 nine categories 與 nine skills 這類偷換概念。

qs.s: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “venture” in the second paragraph?
o: Creative measurement.
Risky attempt.
Non-profit organization.
New business.
qs.hint: 看 venture 前面的 co-founders（共同創辦人），想想什麼東西有創辦人。
qs.ev: Dr. Hare, one of the venture’s co-founders
qs.ex: 有 co-founders 的是新創公司，所以 venture 指新事業；第一段也說這是 recently-founded company。
why: (A) 與 measure 無關。
(B) venture 也有『冒險』義，但此處有共同創辦人，不是冒險。
(C) 文中收費 US $60，不是非營利組織。
(D) 對：new business。
qs.strat: 字義題：用上下文（這裡是 co-founders）決定詞義，不要只選最常見的字典義。

qs.s: According to the passage, what would a Charmer most likely do?
o: Stay away from people whenever possible.
Imitate how other dogs solve problems.
Rely on its owner to point out where a treat is.
Follow its own senses to get what it wants.
qs.hint: 找第四段 Charmer 的定義。
qs.ev: a Charmer is a dog that trusts you so much that it would prefer to solve problems using information you give it rather than information it can get with its own eyes
qs.ex: Charmer 很信任主人，偏好用主人給的資訊解決問題，所以會倚賴主人指出零食在哪裡。
why: (A) 牠信任人，不會躲人。
(B) 文中沒有提到模仿其他狗。
(C) 對：用主人給的資訊。
(D) 與定義相反，Charmer 不偏好靠自己的眼睛。
qs.strat: 推論題：找到原文定義，再套到具體情境，並留意選項是否說反了。

zh: 你的狗是愛因斯坦還是魅力型呢？只要 60 美元，一家新成立的公司 Dognition 就能幫你更了解愛犬的認知特質。它提供線上測驗，告訴你吠叫背後的大腦是怎樣的。
Dognition 的測驗從同理心、記憶到推理能力等多方面衡量狗的智力。但別期待它測出你寵物的智商。共同創辦人之一 Hare 博士說，狗的智力無法用單一數字描述。就像人類有各式各樣的智力，狗也是。問題在於你的狗比較依賴哪一種。
你付了錢之後，Dognition 的網站會帶你填一份關於愛犬的問卷：例如，你的狗遇到其他狗或小孩時有多興奮？煙火會嚇到你的小狗嗎？接著，Dognition 引導你進行像玩接球或捉迷藏一樣有趣的測驗。最後，你會拿到一份愛犬的認知檔案報告。
你的狗可能落在九種類型之一：王牌、觀星者、特立獨行者、魅力型、社交型、原型犬、愛因斯坦、專家或文藝復興犬。這能讓你在 Dognition 的臉書專頁上炫耀一番，也能讓你對狗為什麼做那些事有新的認識。例如，魅力型的狗非常信任你，所以比起用自己的眼睛取得的資訊，牠更喜歡用你給牠的資訊來解決問題。
Dognition 幫助人們以前所未有的方式了解自己的狗。這種新的了解能豐富狗與主人之間的關係。
summary: 本文介紹 Dognition 狗狗認知測驗：智力是多元的、測驗以問卷加遊戲進行、結果分成九種類型，最後強調能增進人與狗的關係。結構是由產品簡介到內容、流程、結果，再到好處。

title: 巴西武術 Capoeira
text: Capoeira is a martial art that combines elements of fight, acrobatics, drumming, singing, dance, and rituals. It involves a variety of techniques that make use of the hands, feet, legs, arms, and head. Although Capoeira appears dancelike, many of its basic techniques are similar to those in other martial arts.

Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves. It is believed that the martial art was connected with tribal fighting in Africa, in which people fought body to body, without weapons, in order to acquire a bride or desired woman. In the sixteenth century, when the Africans were taken from their homes to Brazil against their will and kept in slavery, Capoeira began to take form among the community of slaves for self-defense. But it soon became a strong weapon in the life-or-death struggle against their oppressors. When the slave owners realized the power of Capoeira, they began to punish those who practiced it. Capoeiristas learned to camouflage the forbidden fights with singing, clapping, and dancing as though it were simply entertainment.

At first, Capoeira was considered illegal in Brazil. However, a man known as Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities that Capoeira has great cultural value and should become an official fighting style. He succeeded in his endeavor and transformed the martial art into Brazil’s national sport. He and Mestre Pastinha were the first to open schools, and the Capoeira tree grew, spreading its branches across the world. Nowadays, it is performed in movies and music clips. Capoeira is also believed to have influenced several dancing styles like breaking and hip-hop.
pre: 這是介紹一項武術的文章。讀的時候留意時間線索（500 years ago、In the sixteenth century、At first、Nowadays），並想想作者對它的評價。
gist: Capoeira 結合多種元素，外表像舞蹈，基本招式卻與其他武術相似。
約五百年前由非洲奴隸創造，為了自衛，並用歌舞掩飾。
起初被視為非法，後來因 Mestre Bimba 的努力成為國家運動並傳向全世界。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The history of Capoeira.
The values of Capoeira.
The contribution of Capoeira.
The techniques of Capoeira.
qs.hint: 第二、三段分別在講什麼時期？把整篇的時間順序串起來。
qs.ev: Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves.
qs.ex: 全文從起源、被禁、到合法並傳播，依時間敘述 Capoeira 的歷史。
why: (A) 對：起源、發展到現況。
(B) 價值只在第三段略提。
(C) 對舞蹈的影響只是結尾一句。
(D) 技巧只在第一段簡單帶過。
qs.strat: 主旨題：檢查選項是否涵蓋全文，只涵蓋一段的是陷阱。

qs.s: Which of the following will probably NOT be found in the performance of Capoeira?
o: Singing with drums.
Sweeping with the legs.
Stabbing with swords.
Striking with the hands.
qs.hint: 回到第一段，看它用到哪些身體部位與元素；再看第二段是否有武器。
qs.ev: in which people fought body to body, without weapons
qs.ex: 第一段列出鼓、歌唱、手腳等，第二段說非洲源頭是不用武器的徒手對打，所以不會有用劍刺的動作。
why: (A) 第一段有 drumming、singing。
(B) 用到腿（legs）。
(C) 對：文中強調沒有武器。
(D) 用到手（hands）。
qs.strat: NOT 題：先逐項在文中找到證據，找不到（或相反）的就是答案。

qs.s: What is the author’s attitude toward Capoeira as a sport?
o: Admiring.
Objective.
Doubtful.
Harsh.
qs.hint: 看作者用詞是在讚美、批評，還是只陳述事實。
qs.ev: Capoeira was created nearly 500 years ago in Brazil by African slaves.
qs.ex: 全文以事實陳述歷史與特色，沒有明顯的褒貶字眼，態度是客觀的。
why: (A) 沒有讚嘆的詞語。
(B) 對：客觀陳述。
(C) 沒有表達懷疑。
(D) 沒有嚴厲批評。
qs.strat: 態度題：先判斷全文是否有情緒字眼，沒有就多半是客觀（objective）。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Capoeira?
o: It was greatly influenced by modern dancing styles.
It was initially created as a type of dance and ritual.
It was mainly performed to protect a bride or desired woman.
It was officially recognized in Brazil through the effort of Mestre Bimba.
qs.hint: 回到第三段，找 Mestre Bimba 做了什麼。
qs.ev: Mestre Bimba devoted a great deal of time and effort to convincing the Brazilian authorities
qs.ex: 第三段說 Mestre Bimba 努力說服當局，讓 Capoeira 成為正式的格鬥風格。
why: (A) 是 Capoeira 影響舞蹈，不是反過來。
(B) 最初是為了自衛，歌舞只是掩飾。
(C) 新娘只是非洲部落打鬥的目的之一，且不是主要用途。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題：用關鍵人名定位原文，再比對因果方向。

zh: Capoeira 是一種結合打鬥、特技、擊鼓、歌唱、舞蹈與儀式元素的武術。它運用手、腳、腿、手臂和頭的各種技巧。雖然 Capoeira 看起來像舞蹈，但許多基本招式與其他武術相似。

Capoeira 是近五百年前由非洲奴隸在巴西創造的。一般認為這種武術與非洲的部落打鬥有關，人們在那裡徒手近身搏鬥，為了贏得新娘或心儀的女子。十六世紀，非洲人違背意願被帶離家鄉到巴西為奴，Capoeira 便在奴隸群體中開始成形，用來自衛。但它很快成為生死掙扎中對抗壓迫者的有力武器。當奴隸主發現 Capoeira 的威力，就開始懲罰練習的人。練習者學會用唱歌、拍手和跳舞來偽裝這些被禁止的打鬥，彷彿只是娛樂。

起初，Capoeira 在巴西被視為非法。然而，一位名為 Mestre Bimba 的人投入大量時間與心力，說服巴西當局相信 Capoeira 具有重大文化價值，應成為正式的格鬥風格。他成功了，並將這門武術轉變為巴西的國家運動。他與 Mestre Pastinha 是最早開設學校的人，Capoeira 這棵樹便成長茁壯，枝枒伸向世界各地。如今，它出現在電影和音樂影片中。人們也相信 Capoeira 影響了霹靂舞和嘻哈等幾種舞蹈風格。
summary: 本文依時間順序介紹 Capoeira：由非洲奴隸為自衛而創，以歌舞掩飾，後由 Mestre Bimba 爭取合法並成為國家運動，影響擴及全世界。作者以客觀口吻陳述。

title: 畫家 Winslow Homer 回顧展
genre: 說明文・人物介紹／展覽簡介
text: Winslow Homer (1836-1910) is regarded by many as the greatest American painter of the nineteenth century. Born and raised in Boston, he began his career at age eighteen in his hometown, working as an apprentice at a printing company. Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.

He then moved to New York City, where he worked as a freelance illustrator with Harper’s Weekly, a popular magazine of the time, and began painting. Homer was assigned to cover the inauguration of President Lincoln and, later, the Civil War. His pictures of the Union troops won international recognition. Homer moved to England and, after a two-year stay, returned to America. He settled permanently in Maine in 1883.

From the late 1850s until his death in 1910, Winslow Homer produced a body of work distinguished by its thoughtful expression and its independence from artistic conventions. A man of multiple talents, Homer excelled equally in the arts of illustration, oil painting, and watercolor. Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life. Others speak to more universal themes such as the primal relationship of humans to nature.

This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art. It shows his extraordinary career from the battlefields, farmland, and coastal villages of America, to the North Sea fishing village of Cullercoats, the rocky coast of Maine, the Adirondacks, and the Caribbean. The exhibition offers viewers an opportunity to experience and appreciate the breadth of his remarkable artistic achievement.
pre: 這篇是畫家生平加展覽介紹。先找出人物的生涯順序，最後一段會透露文章出現的場合。
gist: Homer 出生於波士頓，從印刷公司學徒開始，以插畫出名。
他到紐約當自由插畫家，報導林肯就職與內戰並開始繪畫，後定居緬因州。
他的作品擅長多種形式，描繪美國生活與人和自然的關係。
這個為期兩週的展覽呈現他多樣的藝術成就。

qs.s: Where does this passage most likely appear?
o: On an ad featuring contemporary arts.
On a website of an art gallery.
In a booklet on American-born British artists.
In an encyclopedia on the art of printing.
qs.hint: 看最後一段 This two-week exhibition…，想想誰會這樣寫。
qs.ev: This two-week exhibition highlights a wide and representative range of Homer’s art.
qs.ex: 最後一段在介紹為期兩週的展覽並邀請觀眾欣賞，最可能出現在美術館（畫廊）的網站上。
why: (A) Homer 是十九世紀畫家，非當代藝術。
(B) 對。
(C) Homer 是美國畫家，並非英國藝術家。
(D) 主題是畫家，不是印刷藝術的百科。
qs.strat: 出處題：找最能顯示用途的句子（如 exhibition），再推哪種媒介會刊登。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about Homer’s career?
o: He achieved international fame with his vivid paintings of England.
He is considered the greatest illustrator in the history of American art.
He is better known for his watercolors than his illustrations and oil paintings.
He first established his reputation as an illustrator in his hometown of Boston.
qs.hint: 回到第一段，看他在家鄉開始做什麼、怎麼出名。
qs.ev: Skilled at drawing, he soon made a name for himself making illustrations for novels, sheet music, magazines, and children’s books.
qs.ex: 第一段說他在家鄉波士頓開始職業生涯，並因插畫很快成名。
why: (A) 國際聲譽來自美國軍隊（Union troops）的圖畫。
(B) 文中說他是最偉大的『畫家』，不是插畫家。
(C) 文中說他三種形式同樣擅長。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 細節題：注意修飾語（international、greatest）是否與原文相符。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following best characterizes Homer’s art?
o: His pictures vividly portrayed the life of nineteenth-century Americans.
His art thoughtfully expressed the voices of people suffering from war.
His style faithfully conformed to the artistic traditions of his time.
His paintings constantly reflected his desire to escape from society.
qs.hint: 第三段在總結他的作品特色。
qs.ev: Many of his works—depictions of children at play and in school, farm girls attending to their work, hunters and their prey—have become classic images of nineteenth-century American life.
qs.ex: 第三段說他的許多作品成為十九世紀美國生活的經典影像。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 文中沒有說他表達戰爭受難者的聲音。
(C) 文中說他獨立於藝術傳統之外，相反。
(D) 沒有提到想逃離社會。
qs.strat: 特色題：找作者總評他作品的那一段，排除與原文相反的選項。

qs.s: What does “Others” in the third paragraph refer to?
o: Other artists.
Other themes.
Other works.
Other images.
qs.hint: 看 Others 前面那句 Many of his works，再看後面接 speak to more universal themes。
qs.ev: Many of his works
qs.ex: Others 是承接上一句 Many of his works，意思是『他的其他作品』。
why: (A) 不是在講別的藝術家。
(B) 主題是後面說的 universal themes，不是 Others 所指。
(C) 對：其他作品。
(D) images 是前一句的 classic images，不是指涉對象。
qs.strat: 指涉題：代名詞通常指前一句的名詞，要代回去讀通順。

zh: Winslow Homer（1836-1910）被許多人視為十九世紀最偉大的美國畫家。他在波士頓出生、長大，十八歲時在家鄉開始職業生涯，在一家印刷公司當學徒。他擅長繪畫，很快就以替小說、樂譜、雜誌和兒童書籍畫插圖而成名。
他接著搬到紐約市，擔任當時知名雜誌《哈潑週刊》的自由插畫家，並開始繪畫。Homer 受派報導林肯總統的就職典禮，後來又報導內戰。他描繪北軍部隊的圖畫贏得國際肯定。Homer 搬到英國，停留兩年後回到美國。1883 年他永久定居緬因州。
從 1850 年代末到 1910 年去世，Winslow Homer 創作出一系列作品，特色是思想深刻的表達與不受藝術傳統拘束。Homer 多才多藝，在插畫、油畫與水彩上同樣出色。他的許多作品——描繪玩耍和上學的孩童、忙於工作的農家女孩、獵人與獵物——已成為十九世紀美國生活的經典影像。其他作品則談到更普遍的主題，例如人類與大自然的原始關係。
這場為期兩週的展覽呈現了 Homer 藝術中廣泛而具代表性的作品。展覽展示他非凡的生涯，從美國的戰場、農地和海岸村莊，到北海的漁村卡勒科茨、緬因州的岩岸、阿迪朗達克山區和加勒比海。展覽讓觀眾有機會體驗並欣賞他卓越藝術成就的廣度。
summary: 本文先介紹 Homer 的生平與職涯，再說明他多樣的作品特色，最後以展覽介紹收尾，顯示這是美術館展覽的宣傳文字。

title: 英國的茶文化
text: Tea, the most typical English drink, became established in Britain because of the influence of a foreign princess, Catherine of Braganza, the queen of Charles II. A lover of tea since her childhood in Portugal, she brought tea-drinking to the English royal court and set a trend for the beverage in the seventeenth century. The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes, and tea became a popular drink at the London coffee houses where people met to do business and discuss events of the day. Many employers served a cup of tea to their workers in the middle of the morning, thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.” However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people. It came with a high price tag and tea was taxed as well.

Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,” a ceremony taking place at about four o’clock. Until then, people did not usually eat or drink anything between lunch and dinner. At approximately the same time, the Earl of Sandwich popularized a new way of eating bread—in thin slices, with something (e.g., jam or cucumbers) between them. Before long, a small meal at the end of the afternoon, involving tea and sandwiches, had become part of the British way of life.

As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, its popularity spread right through all corners of the British society. Thus, tea became Britain’s favorite drink. In working-class households, it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor. This meal has become known as “high tea.”
Today, tea can be drunk at any time of the day, and accounts for over two-fifths of all beverages consumed in Britain—with the exception of water.
pre: 這篇談茶如何成為英國人的生活習慣。讀時用鉛筆標出時間（seventeenth century、Around 1800、nineteenth century、Today）。
gist: 十七世紀葡萄牙公主 Catherine 將喝茶帶進英國宮廷，後擴及中產階級，但一般人負擔不起。
1800 年左右 Bedford 公爵夫人開創下午茶，三明治也出現。
十九世紀茶變便宜，成為全民飲料，也有了 high tea。
如今茶占英國飲料消耗的五分之二以上（不含水）。

qs.s: How is this passage organized?
o: By cause and effect.
In the order of importance.
In the sequence of time.
By comparison and contrast.
qs.hint: 看每段開頭的時間詞。
qs.ev: Around 1800, the seventh Duchess of Bedford, Anne Maria, began the popular practice of “afternoon tea,”
qs.ex: 各段依十七世紀、1800 年左右、十九世紀、今天的順序敘述，是時間順序。
why: (A) 並非以因果關係貫穿全文。
(B) 沒有依重要性排序。
(C) 對。
(D) 沒有比較兩樣事物。
qs.strat: 結構題：看各段開頭是否有時間、地點、原因等線索詞。

qs.s: What does the phrase “a lasting British institution” in the first paragraph mean?
o: The most popular British organization.
A long-standing tradition in the UK.
The last tea company in London.
A well-established British business.
qs.hint: lasting 是『持久的』；institution 此處指茶歇這個習慣。
qs.ev: thus inventing a lasting British institution, the “tea break.”
qs.ex: tea break 是雇主讓員工喝茶的習慣，lasting 表示延續下來，所以是長久的英國傳統。
why: (A) institution 不是組織。
(B) 對。
(C) lasting 不是『最後的』。
(D) tea break 不是一門生意。
qs.strat: 片語題：回到同位語（這裡是 the “tea break”）看它到底指什麼。

qs.s: According to the passage, why was tea NOT a common drink of everyday life in the seventeenth century?
o: It was only served at coffee houses in London.
It was taxed as an alcoholic drink.
It was forbidden outside of the business setting.
It was too expensive for most people.
qs.hint: 第一段最後兩句有說原因。
qs.ev: However, drinking tea in social settings outside the workplace was beyond the means of the majority of British people.
qs.ex: 最後說多數人負擔不起，因為價格高且還被課稅，所以太貴。
why: (A) 咖啡館只是流行地點之一。
(B) 沒有說被當作酒類課稅。
(C) 沒有禁止。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 原因題：找 because/however 附近的句子，再用同義詞比對（beyond the means = too expensive）。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following is true?
o: High tea was served later in the day than afternoon tea in the nineteenth century.
British people had tea breaks twice a day in the eighteenth century.
Princess Catherine brought tea to England after visiting Portugal.
The Earl of Sandwich started the afternoon tea ceremony.
qs.hint: 比較第二段 afternoon tea（約四點）與第三段 high tea（工人下班回家的正餐）。
qs.ev: it was served with the main meal of the day, eaten when workers returned home after a day’s labor
qs.ex: high tea 是工人下班後的正餐，晚於約四點的下午茶。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 文中是中午前的一次茶歇，沒有說兩次。
(C) 她是從小在葡萄牙愛茶，不是拜訪後才帶來。
(D) 開創下午茶的是公爵夫人，不是三明治伯爵。
qs.strat: 是非題：逐項回原文，留意人名與事件有沒有被換掉。

zh: 茶是最具英國代表性的飲料，它能在英國確立地位，是因為一位外國公主的影響，即查理二世的王后布拉干薩的凱瑟琳。她從小在葡萄牙就愛喝茶，把喝茶帶進英國皇宮，並在十七世紀掀起這種飲料的風潮。這股風尚很快從貴族圈擴散到中產階級，茶成為倫敦咖啡館裡受歡迎的飲品，人們在那裡碰面談生意、討論時事。許多雇主在上午中段給員工一杯茶，因此發明了一個持久的英國傳統：『茶歇』。然而，在工作場所以外的社交場合喝茶，對大多數英國人來說負擔不起。茶價格高昂，還要課稅。
1800 年左右，第七代貝德福德公爵夫人安妮·瑪麗亞開創了流行的『下午茶』習慣，那是在約四點舉行的儀式。在那之前，人們通常在午餐與晚餐之間不吃不喝。幾乎同一時期，三明治伯爵讓一種新的吃麵包方式流行起來——把麵包切成薄片，中間夾東西（如果醬或小黃瓜）。不久之後，在下午接近尾聲時以茶和三明治組成的小餐，就成了英國生活方式的一部分。
由於茶在十九世紀變得便宜許多，它的受歡迎程度遍及英國社會的每個角落。於是，茶成為英國最愛的飲料。在勞工家庭中，茶是配著一天的主餐一起喝的，這餐在工人辛勞一天回家後食用。這一餐後來被稱為『high tea』。
如今，茶可以在一天的任何時間飲用，占英國所消費飲料的五分之二以上——水除外。
summary: 本文依時間順序說明茶如何成為英國人的最愛：從十七世紀宮廷的流行、十九世紀的下午茶與 high tea，到今日隨時可喝。關鍵轉折是茶價下降使它普及。

title: 白宮的歷史
text: For more than two hundred years, the White House has stood as a symbol of the United States Presidency, the U.S. government, and the American people. In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district “not exceeding ten miles square … on the river Potomac.” As preparations began, a competition was held to find a builder of the “President’s House.” Nine proposals were submitted, and the Irish-born architect James Hoban won the gold medal for his practical and handsome design. Construction began when the first cornerstone was laid in October of 1792. Although President Washington oversaw the construction of the house, he never lived in it. It was not until 1800, when the White House was nearly completed, that its first residents, President John Adams and his wife Abigail, moved in.

American presidents can express their individual style in how they decorate the house and in how they receive the public. Thomas Jefferson held the first inaugural open house in 1805; many of those who attended the swearing-in ceremony at the U.S. Capitol simply followed him home. President Jefferson also opened the house for public tours, and it has remained open, except during wartime, ever since. In addition, Jefferson welcomed visitors to annual receptions on New Year’s Day and on the Fourth of July. Abraham Lincoln did the same, but then the inaugural crowds became far too large for the White House to accommodate comfortably, and this also created a security issue. It was not until Grover Cleveland’s first presidency that some effective crowd control measures were implemented to address the problem caused by this practice.

At various times in history, the White House has been known as the “President’s Palace,” the “President’s House,” and the “Executive Mansion.” President Theodore Roosevelt officially gave the White House its current name in 1901.
pre: 這是一篇按時間順序介紹建築歷史的文章。讀的時候圈出年份與人名，並看每個人對白宮做了什麼。
gist: 白宮的選址、設計競圖、動工與第一批住戶（Adams 夫婦）。
歷任總統的風格與接待民眾的方式，從 Jefferson 的開放參觀到後來的人潮管制。
白宮曾有多個名稱，1901 年由 Theodore Roosevelt 正式定名。

qs.s: What is this passage mainly about?
o: The design of the White House.
The location of the White House.
The importance of the White House.
The history of the White House.
qs.ev: In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district
qs.ex: 全文依年代介紹選址、興建、入住、開放參觀到定名，是白宮的歷史。
why: (A) 設計只是第一段的一小部分。
(B) 選址只是第一段開頭。
(C) 全文沒有在討論重要性。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 主旨題：全文若充滿年份與依序發生的事，通常主旨就是 history。

qs.s: What does “this practice” refer to in the second paragraph?
o: Holding an inaugural open house.
Accommodating the crowds comfortably.
Decorating the White House.
Joining in the swearing-in ceremony.
qs.hint: 回到 practice 之前，看誰先開始做、後來的人怎麼「did the same」。
qs.ev: Thomas Jefferson held the first inaugural open house in 1805; many of those who attended the swearing-in ceremony at the U.S. Capitol simply followed him home.
qs.ex: Jefferson 開創就職後開放白宮的做法，後來人潮過多造成問題，this practice 指的就是舉辦就職開放參觀。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 這是無法做到的結果，不是被實行的做法。
(C) 裝潢與人潮問題無關。
(D) 參加典禮只是人潮來源，不是該做法。
qs.strat: 指涉題：找出造成「問題」的那個做法，再回頭找其最早出現的描述。

qs.s: Who initiated the construction of the White House?
o: John Adams.
James Hoban.
George Washington.
Thomas Jefferson.
qs.hint: 第一段：誰宣布政府所在地、發起競圖？
qs.ev: In 1790, President George Washington declared that the federal government would reside in a district “not exceeding ten miles square … on the river Potomac.”
qs.ex: 是 Washington 宣布政府將設在波多馬克河畔並舉辦競圖，發起興建的人是他。
why: (A) Adams 是第一批居民。
(B) Hoban 是得獎的設計者。
(C) 對。
(D) Jefferson 開創開放參觀。
qs.strat: 細節題：注意 initiate（發起）與 design、live 的差別。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true about the White House?
o: The White House has had several names.
The designer of the White House was an American president.
People were not allowed to visit the White House during wartime.
The White House is located in a district not larger than ten miles square.
qs.hint: 逐項回原文：名字在第三段、設計者在第一段、參觀在第二段。
qs.ev: the Irish-born architect James Hoban won the gold medal for his practical and handsome design
qs.ex: 設計者是愛爾蘭出生的建築師 Hoban，不是總統，所以 B 不符。
why: (A) 第三段列出多個名稱。
(B) 對（為『不正確』的選項）：設計者是建築師。
(C) 第二段說除了戰時一直開放。
(D) 第一段 not exceeding ten miles square。
qs.strat: NOT 題：四個選項中有三個在文中找得到，找不到者為答案。

zh: 兩百多年來，白宮一直是美國總統職位、美國政府和美國人民的象徵。1790 年，喬治·華盛頓總統宣布聯邦政府將設在「波多馬克河畔不超過十英里見方」的區域。籌備開始後，舉辦了一場競賽來尋找「總統府」的建造者。共收到九份提案，出生於愛爾蘭的建築師詹姆斯·霍本以實用又美觀的設計贏得金牌。1792 年 10 月第一塊奠基石安放時，工程正式動工。雖然華盛頓總統監督了興建，但他從未住進去。直到 1800 年，白宮幾乎完工時，第一批住戶約翰·亞當斯總統與妻子艾碧該才搬進去。

美國總統可以透過裝飾白宮的方式以及接待民眾的方式來表現個人風格。湯瑪斯·傑佛遜在 1805 年舉辦了第一次就職開放參觀；許多在國會大廈參加宣誓典禮的人乾脆跟著他回家。傑佛遜總統也開放白宮供民眾導覽，此後除了戰時，白宮一直開放。此外，傑佛遜在每年新年與七月四日的招待會歡迎訪客。林肯也這樣做，但後來就職典禮的人潮變得遠遠超過白宮能舒適容納的程度，這也造成安全問題。直到格羅弗·克里夫蘭第一任總統期間，才實施了一些有效的人群管制措施，來處理這種做法所造成的問題。
歷史上不同時期，白宮曾被稱為「總統宮」、「總統府」和「行政大廈」。1901 年，西奧多·羅斯福總統正式為白宮取了現在的名稱。
summary: 本文依年代介紹白宮：選址與興建、第一批住戶、傑佛遜開放參觀與後來的人潮管理，最後是各種名稱與定名。主軸是歷史發展。

title: 西尼羅病毒與 2012 年疫情
genre: 說明文・科普／社會議題
text: West Nile is a tropical disease that begins in birds, which pass it on to mosquitoes that then go on to infect human beings with a bite. Most people who contract West Nile do not experience any symptoms at all, but, if they do, symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite. About 1 in 5 persons suffers fever, headaches, and body aches, usually lasting a week or so. A far less lucky 1 in 150 experiences high fever, tremors, paralysis, and coma. Some—especially the elderly and those with weak immune systems—die.

That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so scary. The situation was particularly bad in Dallas, Texas, where the West Nile virus killed 10 people and sickened more than 200. The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes, even though residents argued that the pesticide could be more dangerous than the disease.

Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it? Blame the weather. An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive, while the unusually high temperatures in that scorching summer further increased their number by speeding up their life cycle. The economic crisis may have also played a role: Homeowners who were not able to pay their bank loans were forced to abandon their properties, sometimes leaving behind swimming pools that made excellent mosquito breeding grounds.

The severity of tropical diseases is also a matter of whether governments are capable—and willing—to defend their populations against infections. Dallas County was not doing some of the key things to slow the spread of West Nile, such as testing dead birds and setting mosquito traps to test for the presence of the disease. Tropical infections are thus as much related to government inaction as they are to climate.
pre: 這篇先介紹疾病，再追問「為什麼 2012 年的疫情特別嚴重」。注意 Blame the weather、The economic crisis、government inaction 這些原因線索。
gist: 西尼羅病毒由鳥傳給蚊子再傳給人，多數人無症狀，少數嚴重。
2012 年美國疫情，尤其達拉斯，死 10 人，市府空中噴藥。
疫情嚴重的原因：暖冬、酷暑，加上經濟危機造成廢棄泳池。
政府沒有採取檢測死鳥、設蚊子陷阱等關鍵措施，疫情也與政府不作為有關。

qs.s: What is this passage mainly about?
o: West Nile and methods to fight it.
West Nile and governmental efficiency.
West Nile and the conditions its virus thrives in.
West Nile and its relation to tropical diseases.
qs.hint: 看第三、四段在回答什麼問題：為什麼 2012 年疫情這麼嚴重。
qs.ev: Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it?
qs.ex: 全文先介紹病，再說明天氣、經濟、政府作為等使病毒大流行的條件。
why: (A) 抗病方法只是少部分。
(B) 政府是原因之一，不是全文。
(C) 對。
(D) 只是以它為例，不是在談與熱帶病的關係。
qs.strat: 主旨題：全文的設問句常是主旨線索；把各段原因歸納成同一類。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about West Nile?
o: Its symptoms usually appear within two weeks.
It is spread through air and water in tropical areas.
Over 20% of people who contract it will suffer severe symptoms.
It comes from direct human contact with birds infected with the virus.
qs.hint: 第一段有數字：3 to 14 days、1 in 5、1 in 150。
qs.ev: symptoms typically develop between 3 to 14 days after a mosquito bite
qs.ex: 3 到 14 天內出現症狀，也就是兩週內。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 是靠蚊子叮咬傳播。
(C) 嚴重症狀是 150 分之 1，不是 20%。
(D) 是鳥傳給蚊子，再傳給人。
qs.strat: 數字題：自己換算（1 in 5 = 20% 但那是輕症），小心被數字偷換。

qs.s: What did Dallas County do to fight off West Nile?
o: They sprayed pesticide from the air.
They asked citizens to stay away from dead birds.
They encouraged citizens to get vaccinations.
They drained the swimming pools in the county.
qs.hint: 第二段說市府宣布緊急狀態後做了什麼。
qs.ev: The city declared a state of emergency and began aerial spraying of a pesticide to kill the mosquitoes
qs.ex: 市府從空中噴灑殺蟲劑殺蚊。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 文中沒有。
(C) 文中沒有提疫苗。
(D) 廢棄泳池是蚊子的繁殖地，沒說排水。
qs.strat: 細節題：用關鍵字 Dallas 找回第二段，比對動作。

qs.s: Which of the following is a reason why Dallas was hit most seriously in the U.S. in 2012?
o: The increasing population in Texas raised the risk of contracting the disease.
The government did not issue a warning about the disease in time.
The residents worried about the county’s decision and action.
The weather of the previous winter was not as cold as usual.
qs.hint: 找 Blame the weather 之後的說明。
qs.ev: An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive
qs.ex: 前一個冬天非常溫和，讓更多蚊子存活，是疫情嚴重的原因之一。
why: (A) 文中沒有提人口增加。
(B) 文中是沒做檢測與設陷阱，沒說沒發警告。
(C) 居民擔心是對噴藥的反應，不是疫情嚴重的原因。
(D) 對：mild winter。
qs.strat: 原因題：用同義詞對應（not as cold = mild）。

zh: 西尼羅熱是一種熱帶疾病，起源於鳥類，鳥傳給蚊子，蚊子再叮咬人類使人感染。大多數感染西尼羅病毒的人完全沒有症狀，但如果有，症狀通常在被蚊子叮咬後 3 到 14 天出現。約每五人中有一人會發燒、頭痛和身體痠痛，通常持續一週左右。遠為不幸的是每 150 人中有一人會出現高燒、顫抖、麻痺和昏迷。有些人——尤其是老年人和免疫系統較弱的人——會死亡。
這就是 2012 年夏天美國西尼羅病毒大爆發如此可怕的原因。情況在德州達拉斯尤其嚴重，西尼羅病毒在那裡造成 10 人死亡、兩百多人生病。該市宣布進入緊急狀態，並開始空中噴灑殺蟲劑殺蚊，即使居民主張殺蟲劑可能比疾病更危險。
為什麼 2012 年夏天對西尼羅病毒和攜帶它的蚊子如此適合？怪天氣吧。極端溫和的冬天讓比平常更多的蚊子存活，而那個酷熱夏天的異常高溫又加快蚊子的生命週期，使牠們數量更多。經濟危機也可能有影響：無力償還銀行貸款的屋主被迫放棄房產，有時留下游泳池，成為絕佳的蚊子繁殖地。
熱帶疾病的嚴重程度也取決於政府是否有能力——而且願意——保護人民免受感染。達拉斯郡沒有做一些減緩西尼羅病毒傳播的關鍵事項，例如檢驗死鳥、設置蚊子陷阱來檢測疾病是否存在。因此，熱帶感染與政府不作為的關係，就和與氣候的關係一樣大。
summary: 本文先介紹西尼羅病毒的傳播與症狀，再以 2012 年達拉斯疫情為例，說明天氣、經濟危機與政府不作為如何造成疫情嚴重。重點在病毒能大流行的條件。

title: 海水淡化的代價與前景
text: Most parts of Taiwan have access to sufficient supplies of fresh water for drinking. But fresh water can be in short supply in many arid regions of the world such as Saudi Arabia, where there are limited water resources. As the world population continues to grow, shortages of fresh water will occur more often and the need for additional water supplies will become critical. Some may ask, “Since the ocean covers more than 70 percent of the Earth, why not just get drinking water from the ocean?”

To turn seawater into fresh water, we need to remove the salt in seawater, that is, to desalinate seawater. The problem is that the desalination of water requires a lot of energy. Salt dissolves very easily in water, forming strong chemical bonds, and those bonds are difficult to break. The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.

There are environmental costs of desalination as well. Sea life can get sucked into desalination plants, killing small ocean creatures like baby fish and plankton, upsetting the food chain. Also, there is the problem of what to do with the separated salt, which is left over as a very concentrated brine. Pumping this super-salty water back into the ocean can harm local aquatic life. Reducing these impacts is possible, but it adds to the costs.

Despite the economic and environmental hurdles, desalination is becoming increasingly attractive as human beings are using up fresh water from other sources. At present, desalinating seawater is the only viable way to provide water to growing populations in rural areas of the Middle East and North Africa. Therefore, the race is on to find a cheaper, cleaner, and more energy-efficient way of desalinating seawater, and promising new findings are being reported.
pre: 這篇從「為什麼不直接喝海水」切入。讀時分辨：第二段講經濟成本，第三段講環境成本，第四段講前景，並留意作者結尾的語氣。
gist: 許多乾旱地區缺淡水，有人問為何不直接用海水。
海水淡化要移除鹽，耗能多、成本高。
淡化也有環境代價：吸入海洋生物、排放濃鹽水。
儘管如此淡化仍越來越吸引人，並有新發現，前景看好。

qs.s: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “arid” in the first paragraph?
o: Occupied.
Isolated.
Dry.
Remote.
qs.hint: 看 arid regions 後面的 where there are limited water resources。
qs.ev: fresh water can be in short supply in many arid regions of the world such as Saudi Arabia, where there are limited water resources
qs.ex: 前面說淡水短缺，且水資源有限，所以 arid 是乾旱、缺水的意思。
why: (A) 與缺水無關。
(B) 孤立不是重點。
(C) 對。
(D) 遙遠不是重點。
qs.strat: 字義題：用 where 子句或前後句說明的線索來推詞義。

qs.s: What is the second paragraph mainly about?
o: The high cost of desalinating seawater.
The major chemical characteristics of seawater.
The urgent need to turn seawater into fresh water.
The amount of energy produced in the desalination of seawater.
qs.hint: 看第二段最後一句 and this means that…，通常是結論。
qs.ev: The energy and technology to desalinate water are both expensive, and this means that desalinating water can be costly.
qs.ex: 第二段解釋為什麼需要大量能源與技術，結論是淡化成本很高。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 鹽的性質只是說明原因。
(C) 迫切需求在第一段。
(D) 是消耗能源，不是產生。
qs.strat: 段落主旨題：抓段尾結論句，並排除第一段的內容。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?
o: Mixing salt with water is not as easy as removing salt from seawater.
Desalinating seawater may kill some sea creatures and disturb the food chain.
Covering 70% of the Earth, the ocean has always satisfied human needs for water.
The increasing population in Saudi Arabia has resulted in shortages of fresh water.
qs.hint: 第三段談環境代價，找 food chain。
qs.ev: Sea life can get sucked into desalination plants, killing small ocean creatures like baby fish and plankton, upsetting the food chain.
qs.ex: 第三段說海洋生物被吸入淡化廠而死，擾亂食物鏈。
why: (A) 文中說鹽很容易溶於水，且要分離很難，正好相反。
(B) 對。
(C) 文中沒有說海洋一直滿足人類用水需求。
(D) 文中以沙烏地為缺水例子，沒說人口增加所致。
qs.strat: 是非題：逐項回原文，注意與原文相反的敘述。

qs.s: Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward the future of desalination?
o: Amazed.
Doubtful.
Conservative.
Hopeful.
qs.hint: 看最後一段結尾的 promising new findings are being reported。
qs.ev: the race is on to find a cheaper, cleaner, and more energy-efficient way of desalinating seawater, and promising new findings are being reported
qs.ex: 作者說正在找更便宜、環保的方法，並已有有希望的新發現，語氣是樂觀的。
why: (A) 沒有驚嘆。
(B) 作者沒有懷疑。
(C) 沒有保守的態度。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 態度題：看結尾的形容詞（promising）判斷語氣。

zh: 台灣大部分地區都有足夠的飲用淡水。但在世界許多乾旱地區，例如沙烏地阿拉伯，淡水可能供應不足，那裡的水資源有限。隨著世界人口持續增長，淡水短缺將更頻繁地發生，對額外水源的需求將變得迫切。有些人可能會問：「既然海洋覆蓋了地球 70% 以上，為什麼不直接從海洋取得飲用水呢？」
要把海水變成淡水，我們必須去除海水中的鹽，也就是將海水淡化。問題是，水的淡化需要大量能源。鹽很容易溶於水，形成強大的化學鍵，而這些鍵很難打斷。淡化水所需的能源與技術都很昂貴，這表示淡化水的成本可能很高。
淡化也有環境代價。海洋生物可能被吸入淡化廠，殺死像小魚和浮游生物這類小型海洋生物，擾亂食物鏈。此外，還有分離出來的鹽該如何處理的問題，它們留下來成為非常濃的鹽水。把這種超鹹的水抽回海洋可能傷害當地水生生物。減少這些影響是可能的，但會增加成本。
儘管有經濟與環境上的障礙，隨著人類用盡其他來源的淡水，海水淡化變得越來越有吸引力。目前，淡化海水是為中東與北非農村地區成長中人口供水的唯一可行方式。因此，尋找更便宜、更乾淨、更節能的海水淡化方法的競賽正在進行，並且已有有希望的新發現被報導出來。
summary: 本文先提出淡水短缺與「為何不喝海水」的問題，再依序說明淡化的經濟成本與環境成本，最後指出它仍愈來愈重要，並對新技術抱持樂觀。

title: 搖籃曲的功能
text: Four millennia ago, an ancient Babylonian wrote down what is possibly the first lullaby. It is a rather threatening lullaby, in which the baby is scolded for disturbing the house god with its crying and warned of terrifying consequences. It may have got the baby to sleep, but its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her. This lullaby may sound more scary than sleep-inducing, yet it is true that many lullabies—including those sung today—have dark undertones.

Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant; but it is the caretaker’s voice and the rhythm and melody of the music that babies respond to, not the content of the song. Then, what is the function of the content? According to studies, some lullabies provide advice, like the Babylonian lullaby, and quite a few others offer the space to sing the unsung, say the unsayable. Lyrics to those lullabies can indeed be interpreted as a reflection of the caregiver’s emotions.

Researchers believe that a large part of the function of lullabies is to help a mother vocalize her worries and concerns. The mother’s fear of loss especially makes sense since the infant/toddler years of life are fragile ones. Since there is a special physical bond between mother and child during this period, mothers feel they can sing to their child about their own fears and anxieties. Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother. In addition, the songs are seemingly trying to work some magic—as if, by singing, the mother is saying, “Sadness has already touched this house; no need to come by again.”
pre: 文章從一首嚇人的古老搖籃曲開始，再問「歌詞到底有什麼功能」。讀時抓出作者的問句與研究者的答案。
gist: 最早的搖籃曲可能是巴比倫的，內容嚇人，許多搖籃曲有陰暗的意涵。
嬰兒對聲音與旋律有反應，而歌詞可給建議並反映照顧者的情緒。
歌詞幫媽媽說出擔憂，讓搖籃曲成為媽媽的療法，也像驅邪。

qs.s: Which of the following titles best describes the main idea of this passage?
o: The Origin of Lullabies
The Functions of Lullabies
Threatening Lullabies
Sleep-Inducing Lullabies
qs.hint: 看第二段中間的設問句，以及第三段結論。
qs.ev: Then, what is the function of the content?
qs.ex: 全文從嚇人的歌詞出發，討論歌詞和搖籃曲對嬰兒與母親的功能。
why: (A) 只有開頭提到最早的搖籃曲。
(B) 對。
(C) 只是開頭的例子。
(D) 文中說嬰兒對旋律有反應，但不是全文主題。
qs.strat: 標題題：標題要涵蓋全文，不能只是開頭的例子。

qs.s: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word “undertones” in the first paragraph?
o: Consequences.
Vocals.
Whispers.
Messages.
qs.hint: 看前面對巴比倫搖籃曲的描述，它有什麼「隱含的訊息」。
qs.ev: its message is far from comforting: If he/she does not stop crying, the demon will eat him/her
qs.ex: dark undertones 是搖籃曲暗藏的陰暗訊息，最接近 messages。
why: (A) consequences 是文中的恐嚇內容，不是 undertones 的意思。
(B) vocals 是歌聲。
(C) whispers 是低語，字面混淆。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 字義題：拆開字面（under + tone），再看句意是『隱含的意味』。

qs.s: What does the author use to support the idea that lullabies can have a soothing effect?
o: Research reports.
Examples found in history.
Stories of caretakers.
The author’s personal experiences.
qs.hint: 第二段第一句：這個說法是怎麼來的？
qs.ev: Research has shown that lullabies, when used correctly, can soothe and possibly even help to heal an infant
qs.ex: 作者以 Research has shown 引出研究結果作為支持。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 歷史例子是巴比倫搖籃曲，但用來說明內容嚇人，不是安撫效果。
(C) 沒有照顧者的故事。
(D) 沒有個人經驗。
qs.strat: 支持證據題：找 research / studies / for example 等引出證據的字。

qs.s: According to this passage, which of the following statements is true?
o: Scary lullabies better help babies fall asleep.
Mothers prefer to sing lullabies with a joyful melody.
Lullabies comfort not only the baby but also the mother.
Babies react to both the music and the lyrics of lullabies.
qs.hint: 第三段結論：Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother。
qs.ev: Lullabies, therefore, serve as therapy for the mother.
qs.ex: 搖籃曲安撫嬰兒，也對母親有療癒作用。
why: (A) 沒說嚇人的搖籃曲更好睡。
(B) 沒有提到偏好歡樂旋律。
(C) 對。
(D) 嬰兒回應的是聲音和旋律，不是歌詞內容。
qs.strat: 是非題：留意 not A but B 這類句型，選項常把它改掉。

zh: 四千年前，一位古巴比倫人寫下了可能是第一首搖籃曲。這是一首相當具威脅性的搖籃曲，其中嬰兒因哭鬧打擾了家神而被責罵，並被警告將有可怕的後果。它或許能讓嬰兒入睡，但傳達的訊息一點也不令人安慰：如果他或她不停止哭泣，惡魔就會吃掉他或她。這首搖籃曲聽起來可能比催眠更嚇人，但確實有許多搖籃曲——包括今日所唱的——帶有陰暗的意涵。
研究顯示，搖籃曲只要使用得當，可以安撫甚至可能幫助療癒嬰兒；但嬰兒回應的是照顧者的聲音以及音樂的節奏與旋律，而不是歌曲的內容。那麼，內容的功能是什麼？根據研究，有些搖籃曲提供建議，像巴比倫的搖籃曲；還有不少搖籃曲提供了一個空間，讓人唱出未唱出的、說出無法說出口的。這些搖籃曲的歌詞確實可以解讀為照顧者情緒的反映。
研究者認為，搖籃曲有很大一部分功能是幫助母親說出她的憂慮與擔心。母親對失去的恐懼特別說得通，因為嬰幼兒時期是脆弱的時期。由於這段期間母子之間有特殊的身體連結，母親覺得可以對孩子唱出自己的恐懼與焦慮。因此，搖籃曲對母親而言是一種療法。此外，這些歌似乎也在試著施展某種魔法——彷彿母親藉由歌唱在說：『悲傷已經觸碰過這個家；不需要再來了。』
summary: 本文由嚇人的古巴比倫搖籃曲談起，說明嬰兒對聲音與旋律有反應，而歌詞則反映並釋放照顧者（尤其是母親）的情緒，因此搖籃曲同時安撫嬰兒與母親。

title: 神仙魚與變性
text: Angelfish, often found in the warm seas and coral reefs, are among the most brightly colored fish of the ocean. Brilliant colors and stripes form amazing patterns on their body. These patterns actually help the fish to hide from danger among roots and plants. At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale. Often, the young ones are differently colored than the adults. Some scientists believe that the color difference between the young and the old indicates their different social positions.

Another interesting fact about angelfish is that they have an occupation in the fish world. Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies. This is not their food, though. Their diet consists mainly of sponge and algae.

One particular kind of angelfish, the blackspot angelfish, has a special capability that allows it to change gender from female to male. However, the change is not made at random; it happens for a specific reason. Angelfish live in groups, and each group has one male fish, which is blue in color, and four female fish, which are yellow. The male angelfish is the strongest and largest member of the group. He is the one who protects and looks after the females. When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.” This is when the largest female in the group begins to change in appearance. She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue. Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes. She begins behaving like a male. Two weeks later, black stripes appear on her body, indicating the gender change is complete. She is now completely male!
pre: 這是介紹一種魚的科普文。第三段有一連串變化，讀時用箭頭標出變化的先後順序（size、color、behavior、stripes）。
gist: 神仙魚色彩鮮豔，花紋可以幫助躲避危險，幼魚與成魚顏色不同。
多數神仙魚是清潔工，替其他魚清除壞死組織，主食是海綿與藻類。
黑斑神仙魚在雄魚死後，最大的雌魚會依序變大、變色、改變行為、長出黑條紋而變性。

qs.s: What is the job of an angelfish in the sea?
o: Being a cleaner for other fish.
Being a bodyguard for other fish.
Being a gardener for roots and plants.
Being a caretaker for sponge and algae.
qs.hint: 第二段第一句提到 occupation（職業）。
qs.ev: Most of them act as cleaners for other fish and pick dead tissue from their bodies.
qs.ex: 第二段說多數神仙魚是其他魚的清潔工，替牠們清除壞死組織。
why: (A) 對。
(B) security guard 是群體裡雄魚的角色，不是對其他魚。
(C) 沒有提到照顧植物。
(D) 海綿和藻類是牠的食物。
qs.strat: 細節題：用題幹的同義詞（job = occupation）回原文定位。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about the color of angelfish?
o: Female angelfish are blue in color.
The colors of the fish become less bright at night.
Male angelfish do not have black stripes on them.
The adult fish and the young ones have the same colors.
qs.hint: 第一段說了夜晚與幼魚顏色，第三段說雌雄顏色。
qs.ev: At night, when these fish become inactive, their colors may become pale.
qs.ex: 夜裡魚不活動時，顏色可能變淡，也就是變得沒那麼鮮豔。
why: (A) 雌魚是黃色，雄魚才是藍色。
(B) 對。
(C) 變性完成後雄魚會有黑條紋。
(D) 文中說幼魚與成魚顏色不同。
qs.strat: 是非題：逐項回原文，留意顏色與性別是否被調換。

qs.s: According to the passage, what triggers the gender change in the blackspot angelfish?
o: Dangers to the group.
Changes in the fish’s diet.
The birth of young angelfish.
The death of the male fish in a group.
qs.hint: 第三段：the change 發生在什麼時候。
qs.ev: When the male dies, the group needs a new “security guard.”
qs.ex: 當群體中的雄魚死亡，群體需要新的守護者，最大的雌魚便開始變性。
why: (A) 沒有說是因危險。
(B) 沒有提到飲食變化。
(C) 沒有提到幼魚出生。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 原因題：找 for a specific reason 之後的說明。

qs.s: Which of the following describes the order of changes in the features of a blackspot angelfish during gender change?
o: Size → behavior → color → stripes.
Color → size → behavior → stripes.
Size → color → behavior → stripes.
Color → behavior → size → stripes.
qs.hint: 照第三段後半依序找 begins to grow larger、after a week、Slowly、Two weeks later。
qs.ev: She begins to grow larger in size, and after a week, she starts changing color, from yellow to blue. Slowly, her behavior toward the other fish also changes.
qs.ex: 先變大，一週後變色，然後行為慢慢改變，兩週後才出現黑條紋，順序是大小、顏色、行為、條紋。
why: (A) 行為與顏色順序顛倒。
(B) 一開始是變大，不是顏色。
(C) 對。
(D) 順序全部不符。
qs.strat: 順序題：圈出時間詞與連接詞，依序寫成箭頭。

zh: 神仙魚常見於溫暖的海域與珊瑚礁，是海洋中顏色最鮮豔的魚類之一。鮮豔的色彩與條紋在牠們身上形成驚人的圖案。這些圖案其實能幫助魚在植物根部與水草之間躲避危險。夜裡，這些魚不活動時，牠們的顏色可能變淡。幼魚的顏色往往與成魚不同。一些科學家認為，幼魚與老魚的顏色差異顯示牠們不同的社會地位。
關於神仙魚另一個有趣的事實是，牠們在魚的世界裡有一份職業。大多數神仙魚擔任其他魚的清潔工，啄取牠們身上的壞死組織。不過這並不是牠們的食物。牠們的飲食主要是海綿與藻類。

有一種特別的神仙魚，黑斑神仙魚，具有能從雌性轉變成雄性的特殊能力。然而，這種轉變並非隨機，而是有特定原因。神仙魚群居，每個群體有一隻雄魚（藍色）和四隻雌魚（黃色）。雄魚是群體中最強壯、最大的成員，負責保護並照顧雌魚。當雄魚死亡，群體就需要一位新的「保全人員」。這時群體中最大的雌魚開始改變外觀。她開始變大，一週後，她開始變色，由黃色變成藍色。慢慢地，她對其他魚的行為也改變了。她開始表現得像雄魚。兩週後，黑色條紋出現在她身上，表示性別轉變完成。她現在完全是雄魚了！
summary: 本文介紹神仙魚的顏色、清潔工角色，並詳述黑斑神仙魚在雄魚死亡後，最大的雌魚如何依序變大、變色、改變行為、長出條紋而變性。

title: 北美圖騰柱
text: Totem poles in North America are poles or posts carved with symbols or figures by Aboriginal peoples of the Northwest Coast. Carved from large, straight trees and painted vibrant colors, the totem poles are not just unique works of art. The coastal peoples have long passed on knowledge from generation to generation through oral traditions, and totem poles were the traditional way of telling the story of an individual family or clan.

The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved. Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe. Inside the homes of high-ranking chiefs is where house poles were found. The family’s history was carefully carved into each pole. Placed along the rear or front walls of a house, house poles also helped to support the main beam of the roof.

Memorial poles stood in front of a house. They were erected in memory of a deceased chief or a high-ranking clan member. The poles depicted the person’s accomplishments or family history. Mortuary poles were also raised to honor the dead, but they differed from memorial poles, having a burial box placed at the top of the pole. Inside the burial box were the remains of the deceased.

While many of these poles can still be found in various locations on the west coast of North America, there is one pole that can now only be found in a museum—the shame pole. Traditionally, shame poles were carved for a chief to embarrass and ridicule another who had done something wrong. Once the wrong was made right, the pole was taken down.

Totem poles are important expressions of specific Aboriginal cultures. Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces, the art of totem pole carving has survived. Aboriginal carvers continue to carve totems as symbols of their cultural pride and clan kinship.
pre: 這篇介紹圖騰柱的種類。第二到第四段在「分類」介紹，讀時把每一種柱子的位置與用途列成小表。
gist: 圖騰柱是西北海岸原住民雕刻的柱子，用來傳述家族或氏族的故事。
迎賓柱立在海灘，屋柱在酋長家中並支撐屋樑。
紀念柱立在屋前；墓柱頂端有放遺骸的盒子。
恥辱柱用來羞辱做錯事的人，事情解決後就拆除。
圖騰柱是文化的重要表現，雖受殖民威脅仍延續，象徵文化自豪。

qs.s: Which of the following is the best title for this passage?
o: Totem Poles, the Legends of Aboriginal Peoples
Totem Poles: Their Functions
Totem Poles, Symbols of Historical Resistance
Totem Poles: Their Designs
qs.hint: 看第二到第四段，每種柱子在哪裡、做什麼用。
qs.ev: Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe.
qs.ex: 全文介紹各種圖騰柱的用途（迎賓、支撐屋樑、紀念、喪葬、羞辱），所以標題是功能。
why: (A) 文中沒有講傳說。
(B) 對。
(C) 抵抗殖民只在最後一段提到一句。
(D) 沒有介紹圖案設計。
qs.strat: 標題題：選能涵蓋中間各段的選項，排除只對應首尾的。

qs.s: How is the information about totem poles organized in Paragraphs 2 to 4?
o: In order of importance.
In order of time.
By cause and effect.
By classification.
qs.hint: 第二段第一句就點出怎麼安排。
qs.ev: The totem pole can be grouped into specific categories, depending on its location and the occasion for which it was carved.
qs.ex: 第二段第一句說圖騰柱可依位置與場合分成幾類，後面各段分別介紹各類。
why: (A) 沒有依重要性排序。
(B) 沒有時間順序。
(C) 沒有因果關係。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 結構題：找段首的 grouped into categories 這類關鍵詞，對應 classification。

qs.s: Which of the following is located at the edge of a body of water?
o: The house pole.
The shame pole.
The memorial pole.
The welcome pole.
qs.hint: 找哪一種柱子在 beachfront（海灘前）。
qs.ev: Welcome poles were traditionally placed on village beachfronts to greet visitors arriving by canoe.
qs.ex: 迎賓柱立在村落的海灘前，靠近水邊。
why: (A) 屋柱在屋內。
(B) 恥辱柱現在只在博物館。
(C) 紀念柱在屋前。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 同義題：把 edge of a body of water 換成 beachfront。

qs.s: Which is closest in meaning to the word “encroachment” in the last paragraph?
o: Invasion.
Appointment.
Objection.
Enrichment.
qs.hint: 看 encroachment 的前後：threats posed by … colonial forces。
qs.ev: Despite the threats posed by cultural and political encroachment of colonial forces
qs.ex: encroachment 與 threats、colonial forces 搭配，意思是侵入、侵犯。
why: (A) 對。
(B) appointment 是任命、約會。
(C) objection 是反對。
(D) enrichment 是豐富，語氣相反。
qs.strat: 字義題：從 threats、Despite 判斷詞語是負面的。

zh: 北美的圖騰柱是由西北海岸原住民族以符號或人像雕刻的柱子。圖騰柱由高大筆直的樹木雕成，並漆上鮮豔的顏色，它們不只是獨特的藝術作品。沿海民族長久以來透過口述傳統世代傳遞知識，而圖騰柱是述說個別家族或氏族故事的傳統方式。
圖騰柱可依位置與雕刻場合分成特定類別。迎賓柱傳統上立在村落的海灘前，迎接乘獨木舟抵達的訪客。屋柱則見於地位崇高的酋長家中。家族的歷史被仔細地刻在每根柱子上。屋柱立在房屋的後牆或前牆邊，也幫忙支撐屋頂的主樑。
紀念柱立在房屋前。它們是為紀念已故的酋長或地位崇高的氏族成員而豎立。柱子上描繪此人的成就或家族歷史。墓柱同樣為了緬懷逝者而豎立，但與紀念柱不同，柱頂放有一個埋葬盒，盒內是逝者的遺骸。
雖然許多這類柱子今天仍能在北美西岸各地找到，但有一種柱子現在只能在博物館見到——恥辱柱。傳統上，恥辱柱是一位酋長為了讓另一位做錯事的酋長難堪、嘲笑他而雕刻的。一旦錯誤被改正，柱子就會被拆下。
圖騰柱是特定原住民文化的重要表現。儘管面臨殖民勢力在文化與政治上的侵蝕威脅，圖騰柱雕刻藝術仍然存續。原住民雕刻家繼續雕刻圖騰柱，作為他們文化自豪與氏族親誼的象徵。
summary: 本文介紹北美西北海岸圖騰柱，中間三段依位置與用途分類說明迎賓柱、屋柱、紀念柱、墓柱與恥辱柱，最後強調它們是文化自豪的象徵並延續至今。

title: 洗腦神曲 Earworm
text: Music has a tendency to get stuck in our heads. Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop. This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists. They use a range of terms to describe it—stuck-song syndrome, sticky music, cognitive itch, or most commonly “earworm.” Earworms can run around our heads for several minutes to numerous hours. As the melody repeats, it becomes embedded into our mind. Even though our ears do not hear the tune, our brain continues to play it.

Earworms often take the form of song fragments rather than entire songs, and the song is usually a familiar one. Researchers are not sure why some songs are more likely to get stuck in our heads than others, but everyone has their own tunes. Often those songs have a simple, upbeat melody and catchy, repetitive lyrics, such as popular commercial jingles and slightly annoying radio hits. Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations, such as a phrase similar to the lyrics of a song.

While earworms might be annoying, most people who experience them nevertheless report that they are pleasant or at least neutral. Only a third of people are disturbed by the song in their heads. How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them. Those who have positive feelings about their stuck songs prefer to just “let them be,” while those with negative feelings turn to more behavioral responses, which include coping strategies such as singing, talking, or even praying.
pre: 這篇談「洗腦歌曲」現象。三段分別是：它是什麼、什麼會觸發它、人怎麼面對它。讀時分段想清楚各段功能。
gist: Earworm 是在腦中反覆播放的旋律，許多科學家研究它。
它常是熟悉歌曲的片段，簡單輕快、重複的歌詞或近期聽過的歌容易觸發。
多數人不覺得困擾，應對方式取決於對它的感受。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following is true about an earworm?
o: It is a creature living inside our ears.
It is a tune memorized in a personal way.
It is a melody repeating in our heads.
It is a commercial recalled through lyrics.
qs.hint: 第一段說明 earworm 的定義與運作。
qs.ev: Sometimes a tune intrudes on our thoughts and then plays, and replays, in a never-ending loop.
qs.ex: earworm 是闖入腦中、一再重播的旋律。
why: (A) 是比喻，並非真的蟲。
(B) 文中沒有提個人方式記憶。
(C) 對。
(D) 廣告歌只是例子之一。
qs.strat: 細節題：找文中對該名詞的定義，不要被字面（ear + worm）誤導。

qs.s: Which of the following best defines “subject” in the first paragraph?
o: A kind of mental disease.
A course being taken.
A participant in an experiment.
A matter being studied.
qs.hint: 看 subject 後面的 explored by many scientists。
qs.ev: This interesting phenomenon becomes a subject explored by many scientists.
qs.ex: subject 被科學家探討，是研究的主題、題目。
why: (A) 不是疾病。
(B) 課程是 subject 的另一義，但此處不符。
(C) 參與實驗者也是 subject 的意思，但此處是被研究的現象。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 字義題：同一個字有多義，用句子結構（subject explored by）決定。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a feature that would trigger earworms?
o: Tunes repeatedly encountered.
Melodies with smooth rhythms.
Fragments of songs recently heard.
Words similar to the lyrics of a song.
qs.hint: 第二段列出觸發因素：simple, upbeat melody、catchy lyrics、recent or repeated exposure、word associations。
qs.ev: Recent or repeated exposure to a song or even a small part of a song can also trigger earworms, as can word associations
qs.ex: 文中提到簡單輕快的旋律，但沒有提到「流暢的節奏」，所以 B 沒被提到。
why: (A) repeated exposure 有提到。
(B) 對（NOT 的答案）：沒有提 smooth rhythms。
(C) recent exposure 的片段有提到。
(D) word associations 有提到。
qs.strat: NOT 題：逐項在文中找出處，找不到的就是答案。

qs.s: What is the third paragraph mainly about?
o: Why people find earworms annoying.
How people react to earworms.
What people use to kill earworms.
When people start to notice earworms.
qs.hint: 看第三段 How people cope… 這句。
qs.ev: How people cope with their earworms seems to depend on how they feel about them.
qs.ex: 第三段說多數人覺得愉快或中立，並說明不同感受的人如何應對，主旨是人們的反應。
why: (A) 只有三分之一的人被困擾，且不是講原因。
(B) 對。
(C) 不是在談消滅它。
(D) 沒有提什麼時候開始察覺。
qs.strat: 段落主旨題：段落中的主題句常是 How…/Why… 開頭。

zh: 音樂有一種黏在我們腦袋裡的傾向。有時一段旋律闖入我們的思緒，然後在一個沒完沒了的循環中播放、再播放。這個有趣的現象成為許多科學家探討的主題。他們用一系列名稱來描述它——卡歌症候群、黏人音樂、認知搔癢，或最常見的「耳蟲」。耳蟲可能在我們腦中跑上幾分鐘到好幾個小時。隨著旋律反覆，它被嵌入我們的心智。即使我們的耳朵沒聽到旋律，大腦仍持續播放。
耳蟲通常以歌曲片段而非整首歌的形式出現，而且歌曲通常是熟悉的。研究者不確定為什麼有些歌比其他歌更容易黏在腦中，但每個人都有自己的曲子。這些歌通常有簡單輕快的旋律和順口、重複的歌詞，例如流行的廣告歌和有點惱人的電台熱門歌曲。最近或重複接觸一首歌，甚至只是歌的一小部分，也可能觸發耳蟲，詞語聯想也一樣，例如與歌詞相似的片語。
雖然耳蟲可能很煩人，但大多數經歷過的人仍表示它們是愉快的，或至少是中立的。只有三分之一的人被腦中的歌困擾。人們如何應付耳蟲，似乎取決於他們對它的感受。對卡在腦中的歌有正面感受的人偏好順其自然，而有負面感受的人則轉向更多行為反應，包括唱歌、說話，甚至祈禱等應對策略。
summary: 本文先說明耳蟲是什麼，再說明容易觸發它的歌曲特色與情境，最後談人們面對耳蟲的感受與應對方式。

title: 殺蟲霧彈真的有效嗎
text: Got a bug bite problem? Many people who are troubled by skin rashes caused by bug bites use “foggers,” or “bug bombs,” to get rid of the annoying crawlers in their homes. Many people think these bug killers or pesticides will penetrate every place where the insects hide. Actually, quite the opposite is true. Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they’ll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways, where you’ll never be able to treat them effectively.

Ohio State University researchers tested three commercially sold foggers in a study on the effect of foggers on bedbugs. After testing these brands on five different groups of live bedbugs for two hours, the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects. The researchers said bedbugs hide in cracks and crevices such as under sheets and mattresses, or deep in carpets where foggers won’t reach. Moreover, bugs that do come in contact with the mist may be resistant to the pesticide.

Foggers, or bug bombs, should really be a measure of last resort. First of all, the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion if the product is not used properly. Second, once a bug bomb is used, every surface in your home will be covered with the toxic pesticide. When you use a bug bomb, a chemical mixture rains down on your counters, furniture, floors, and walls, leaving behind oily and toxic substances. Your health might thus be endangered. Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
pre: 文章先推翻大家的想法（Actually, quite the opposite is true），再用研究與兩點理由支持。注意 First of all、Second 與最後的建議。
gist: 許多人以為殺蟲霧彈能滲入所有角落，其實蟲會躲起來。
研究顯示霧彈對臭蟲幾乎無效，因為牠們躲在縫隙，且可能有抗藥性。
霧彈易燃、有毒殘留，應是最後手段，建議交給專業人士。

qs.s: What is this passage mainly about?
o: Steps to get rid of bedbugs.
Ways to use foggers correctly.
The ineffectiveness of bug bombs.
The problems caused by insects.
qs.hint: 看第一段 Actually, quite the opposite is true，以及第二段研究結果。
qs.ev: the scientists saw that the foggers had little—if any—effect on the insects
qs.ex: 全文說明霧彈對蟲無效，並有危險，主旨是霧彈的無效。
why: (A) 只有最後提到請專家，沒有列出步驟。
(B) 沒有教怎麼正確使用。
(C) 對。
(D) 蟲造成的問題只是開頭。
qs.strat: 主旨題：找出作者推翻的觀點與支持的論點。

qs.s: How do bedbugs react to foggers?
o: They remain motionless.
They retreat to safe places.
They stop biting people.
They escape into another house.
qs.hint: 第一段：Once the pests detect the chemical fog…
qs.ev: Once the pests detect the chemical fog in the room, they’ll hide themselves in walls or other hideaways
qs.ex: 蟲偵測到化學霧後會躲進牆壁等藏身處，也就是退到安全的地方。
why: (A) 沒說不動。
(B) 對。
(C) 沒提停止叮咬。
(D) 沒說逃到別的屋子。
qs.strat: 細節題：用題幹動詞 react 對應原文 detect… hide。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following statements about foggers is true?
o: They can cause a fire.
They do not stay on furniture.
They can kill most insects.
They do not contain chemicals.
qs.hint: 第三段 First of all 與 Second。
qs.ev: the gases used in bug bombs are highly flammable and thus pose a serious risk of fire or explosion
qs.ex: 霧彈的氣體高度易燃，使用不當有起火或爆炸的風險。
why: (A) 對。
(B) 化學物質會落在家具上並留下殘餘。
(C) 研究說效果很小。
(D) 含有毒的殺蟲劑。
qs.strat: 是非題：逐項回原文，注意與原文相反的選項。

qs.s: What does the author advise people to do with bedbug problems?
o: Choose the right fogger.
Clean the house regularly.
Close the doors when using pesticides.
Consult a pest-control expert.
qs.hint: 看最後一句，有 suggested 的地方。
qs.ev: Therefore, it is suggested that people leave the problem to the professionals.
qs.ex: 作者建議把問題交給專業人士，也就是找除蟲專家。
why: (A) 作者反對用霧彈。
(B) 沒有提到。
(C) 沒有提到。
(D) 對。
qs.strat: 建議題：找 suggest / advise / should 的句子，通常在文末。

zh: 有被蟲咬的困擾嗎？許多受蟲咬引起皮膚疹所苦的人，會使用「霧化殺蟲器」，也就是「殺蟲炸彈」，來消滅家裡討厭的爬行小蟲。許多人以為這些殺蟲劑會滲透到昆蟲藏身的每個地方。事實上恰恰相反。一旦害蟲偵測到房間裡的化學霧，牠們就會躲進牆壁或其他藏身處，在那裡你永遠無法有效地處理牠們。
俄亥俄州立大學的研究人員在一項研究霧化殺蟲器對臭蟲效果的研究中，測試了三種市售的霧化殺蟲器。在對五組不同的活臭蟲測試這些品牌兩小時後，科學家發現霧化殺蟲器對昆蟲即使有效果也很小。研究人員說，臭蟲躲在縫隙和裂縫裡，例如床單和床墊下，或地毯深處，霧到不了那裡。此外，真的接觸到噴霧的蟲子可能對殺蟲劑有抗藥性。
霧化殺蟲器，或說殺蟲炸彈，真的應該只是最後手段。首先，殺蟲炸彈使用的氣體高度易燃，如果產品使用不當，會有嚴重的起火或爆炸風險。其次，殺蟲炸彈一旦使用，你家每個表面都會覆蓋有毒的殺蟲劑。使用殺蟲炸彈時，化學混合物會落在你的檯面、家具、地板和牆壁上，留下油膩有毒的物質。你的健康因此可能受到危害。因此，建議人們把問題交給專業人士。
summary: 本文推翻「殺蟲霧彈能殺光蟲」的想法，以研究顯示它對臭蟲幾乎無效，並指出易燃與有毒殘留的風險，最後建議交給專業除蟲人員。

title: 夾腳拖鞋的歷史與爭議
text: The flip-flop is the simplest shoe on the planet. It consists of a piece of rubber, plastic, leather, or woven material in the outline of a foot, with a strap holding the sandal to a wearer’s toes. The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.

The earliest record of people wearing the flip-flop comes from Egypt, but many ancient cultures had their own variants of the footwear. In the Greek version, the toe strap ran between the first and second toes, while Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes. The Mesopotamians wore the strap between the third and fourth toes. In India, “toe knob” sandals had a knob between the first and second toes.

Modern flip-flops derive from Japanese zōris, which were often worn with socks dividing the big toe from the rest, and were typically made of rice straw. During World War II, Japan seized much of Southeast Asia’s rubber. In 1945, devastated from the war, the country set about establishing a cheap industry that could rebuild its economy. The Japanese used their rubber reserves from the war to mass-produce the simplest Japanese footwear. Rubber thus replaced rice straw as the major material for the flip-flop.

In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home. The sandals have subsequently undergone redesign, often appearing in bright colors in line with Californian beach culture. They have remained popular due to their convenience, and are often worn with bathing suits or summer clothing. Some people also wear dressy versions for more formal occasions.

Despite their popularity, flip-flops provoke some questions. Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries. Another issue is the suitability of exposing feet on the street and places other than the beach. But even more serious is their environmental impact: Millions of plastic discards end up in landfills or the ocean, releasing chemicals and at the same time taking centuries to decompose.
pre: 這篇介紹夾腳拖鞋的由來、演變與優缺點。第 2 段比較各古文明的「腳趾帶位置」，讀的時候要把位置對應到文明。
gist: 夾腳拖鞋是最簡單的鞋，名稱來自走路時的拍打聲。
古埃及就有紀錄，各古文明的趾帶位置各不相同。
現代夾腳拖鞋源自日本草履，二戰後橡膠取代稻草。
1950 年代傳入美國，成為流行的休閒鞋。
儘管受歡迎，仍有受傷、場合合宜性與環境污染的問題。

qs.s: Which culture most likely created the sandals shown in the picture?
o: Indian.
Greek.
Mesopotamian.
Roman.
qs.hint: 圖中拖鞋的趾帶位置要和第 2 段逐一對照，找出對應的文明。
qs.ev: Roman sandals had the strap between the second and third toes.
qs.ex: 圖中的趾帶位於第二與第三趾之間，第 2 段說這是羅馬人的版本，所以選 (D)。
why: (A) 印度的是在第一、二趾間有「趾結」，不符。
(B) 希臘的趾帶在第一、二趾之間，不符。
(C) 美索不達米亞的趾帶在第三、四趾之間，不符。
(D) 羅馬的趾帶在第二、三趾之間，與圖相符。
qs.strat: 圖片題要先看清圖中的關鍵特徵，再回文章找對應描述。

qs.s: Why is the footwear discussed in the passage called “flip-flop”?
o: Because of the noise it makes.
Because of its changeable design.
Because of its simple structure.
Because of the comfort of wearing it.
qs.hint: 回到第 1 段，找 “The name comes from” 這句話。
qs.ev: The name comes from the sound the sandals make when they slap the walking feet.
qs.ex: 第 1 段直接說明名稱來自走路時拖鞋拍打腳的聲音，也就是它發出的噪音。
why: (A) 名稱來自拍打聲，正確。
(B) 文中沒說名稱與設計可變有關。
(C) 簡單是形容它的設計，不是命名原因。
(D) 舒適與命名無關。
qs.strat: 問「為什麼叫這個名字」時，找 name comes from / is called 的句子。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about the modern development of the flip-flop?
o: Modern flip-flops originated from Indian toe knob sandals.
Americans loved the Japanese flip-flop because of its bright colors.
Rubber became the major material of the flip-flop before World War II.
The sandals American soldiers brought home from Japan later became modern flip-flops.
qs.hint: 現代發展在第 3、4 段，注意時間點與因果。
qs.ev: In the 1950s, flip-flops became popular in the United States as soldiers returning from occupied Japan brought zōris home.
qs.ex: 第 4 段說美國士兵把日本草履帶回家，之後經過重新設計才成為現代夾腳拖鞋。
why: (A) 現代款源自日本草履，不是印度趾結涼鞋。
(B) 鮮豔色彩是美國後來才重新設計的，並非因此愛上日本款。
(C) 橡膠取代稻草是在二戰之後。
(D) 與第 4 段相符。
qs.strat: 是非題要逐項回原文核對時間與因果，小心張冠李戴。

qs.s: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a concern of wearing the flip-flop?
o: Personal health.
Poor quality.
Social appropriateness.
Marine pollution.
qs.hint: 所有顧慮都集中在最後一段，逐一對照選項。
qs.ev: Their simple design is responsible for many foot injuries.
qs.ex: 最後一段提到受傷（健康）、場合合宜性與塑膠污染海洋，但完全沒提品質差，所以選 (B)。
why: (A) 足部受傷屬於健康問題，有提到。
(B) 文中沒有談品質差，是答案。
(C) 在街上露腳是否合宜，有提到。
(D) 塑膠丟入海洋，有提到。
qs.strat: NOT 題：把每個選項在原文找到出處，找不到的就是答案。

zh: 夾腳拖鞋是地球上最簡單的鞋。它是由一片橡膠、塑膠、皮革或編織材料做成腳的輪廓，再用一條帶子把涼鞋固定在穿著者的腳趾上。這個名字來自涼鞋在走路時拍打腳所發出的聲音。
最早穿著夾腳拖鞋的紀錄來自埃及，但許多古文明都有自己的款式。希臘版本的趾帶穿過第一和第二趾之間，羅馬涼鞋則在第二和第三趾之間。美索不達米亞人把帶子穿在第三和第四趾之間。在印度，「趾結」涼鞋在第一和第二趾之間有個結。
現代夾腳拖鞋源自日本草履，草履常搭配把大拇趾與其他腳趾分開的襪子穿，通常由稻草製成。二戰期間，日本奪取了東南亞大部分的橡膠。1945 年，國家因戰爭而殘破，開始建立廉價產業以重建經濟。日本人用戰時的橡膠儲備大量生產最簡單的日本鞋類。橡膠因此取代稻草成為夾腳拖鞋的主要材料。
1950 年代，夾腳拖鞋在美國流行起來，因為從被占領的日本返國的士兵把草履帶回家。之後涼鞋經過重新設計，常以鮮豔的顏色出現，呼應加州的海灘文化。它們因為方便而持續受歡迎，常搭配泳裝或夏季服飾。有些人也會在較正式的場合穿著高雅的款式。
儘管受歡迎，夾腳拖鞋也引發一些疑問。它簡單的設計造成許多腳部受傷。另一個問題是在街上和海灘以外的地方露出雙腳是否合宜。但更嚴重的是它對環境的影響：數百萬被丟棄的塑膠鞋最終進了掩埋場或海洋，釋放化學物質，同時需要數百年才會分解。
summary: 本文先說明夾腳拖鞋名稱的由來，再追溯古代各文明的款式與日本、美國的現代演變，最後點出傷害腳部、場合適不適當與環境污染三個問題。

title: 海事引水人的特殊職業
text: Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships piloted by captains. But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor. The task of bringing the ship into the harbor and anchoring it is taken up by a different captain. This captain is called a marine pilot.

A marine pilot is a boat pilot with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where there are often deep water channels surrounded by shallower seabeds. Without the services of a marine pilot, docking ships would be hazardous. There would be a real chance of running aground and damaging the ship and the cargo, some of which might be dangerous if released into a water-based ecosystem.

In addition to the shallower seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. During different tides, currents may change from one direction to the other. The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.

Marine pilotage is a job that requires a high degree of proficiency as well as quick and independent thinking. Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and controls the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
pre: 這篇介紹一種你可能沒聽過的職業。讀的時候注意：這個人做什麼、為什麼需要他、工作上有哪些困難。
gist: 船長把船開到港口外，進港由另一種船長「引水人」負責。
引水人熟悉特定港口，能避免擱淺與貨物損害。
潮汐與風向讓靠港更困難。
引水人需要專業、反應快，核心是風險管理，並保護船與環境。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A special profession.
Shipping and trading.
Guidelines for safe docking.
Protection of the marine environment.
qs.hint: 看首段最後一句如何引出主角，再看每段是否都圍繞這個人。
qs.ev: This captain is called a marine pilot.
qs.ex: 全文介紹引水人這種職業：做什麼、為什麼需要、需要什麼能力，主旨是一種特殊職業。
why: (A) 全文圍繞引水人這個職業，正確。
(B) 航運貿易只是開頭背景。
(C) 安全靠港是引水人工作的一部分，不是整篇重點。
(D) 環境保護只在最後一句提到。
qs.strat: 主旨題看首段如何引入主題，排除只涵蓋部分細節的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following is part of the knowledge that a marine pilot must have?
o: The value of the ships.
The content of the cargo.
The weather conditions.
The diversity of marine life.
qs.hint: 到第 3 段找引水人面對的挑戰，想想需要懂什麼。
qs.ev: Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of anchoring the ship.
qs.ex: 第 3 段說潮汐與風是靠港的挑戰，引水人必須掌握這些，也就是天氣（風）與海況，所以選 (C)。
why: (A) 文中沒提船的價值。
(B) 貨物內容沒被列為所需知識。
(C) 風與潮汐屬於天氣海象條件，正確。
(D) 海洋生物多樣性沒提到。
qs.strat: 找「必備知識」就回到文中列出的挑戰與條件，再把選項換句話對應。

qs.s: What does “a crucial time” in the last paragraph refer to?
o: When the vessel hits a flat.
When the channel is not deep enough.
When there is a collision of two ships.
When a ship is waiting to enter the port.
qs.hint: 回到第 1 段，看引水人什麼時候接手船。
qs.ev: But the captain of a ship is responsible for guiding the vessel until they hit a port, waiting to enter the harbor.
qs.ex: 第 1 段說船長帶船到港口外等待進港，之後由引水人接手，所以關鍵時刻是船等待進港時。
why: (A) 撞上淺灘（擱淺）是要避免的事，不是引水人上船的時機。
(B) 水道不夠深是港口特色，非指時間點。
(C) 兩船相撞文中沒提。
(D) 船在港外等候進港時引水人上船，正確。
qs.strat: 指涉題要從上下文與全文線索還原該詞所指的情境。

qs.s: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?
o: By adding new details.
By predicting future development.
By summarizing the main points.
By giving advice to the general public.
qs.hint: 看最後一段是否在重述前面各段說過的內容。
qs.ev: The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
qs.ex: 最後一段重述引水人所需能力與責任（熟悉港口、風險管理、保護船與環境），是對前文要點的總結。
why: (A) 最後一段是重申，不是新增資訊。
(B) 沒有預測未來。
(C) 整合前文要點，正確。
(D) 沒有給大眾建議。
qs.strat: 結尾手法題：看結尾是重述、預測、建議還是新增，並與前文比對。

zh: 船舶是各國貿易的生命線。從食物到機器，幾乎所有東西都是由船長駕駛的巨輪經海路運來。但船長只負責把船引導到港口，也就是在港外等待進港為止。把船帶進港並停泊的任務，則由另一位船長負責。這位船長叫做引水人。
引水人是對特定港口有專門知識的領航員。需要引水人把大船導入港口，因為港口常有深水航道，周圍是較淺的海床。沒有引水人的服務，船隻靠岸會很危險，很可能擱淺而損壞船隻與貨物，其中有些貨物若洩漏到水域生態系中可能有害。
除了較淺的海床外，潮汐與風也對船隻進港構成進一步的挑戰。在不同的潮汐期間，水流可能從一個方向轉到另一個方向。漲潮時靠岸的策略到了退潮時可能不適用。此外，風會大幅改變船的方向與反應，增加停泊的難度。
引水工作需要高度的專業能力，以及迅速而獨立的思考。最重要的是，它是關於風險管理。引水人在關鍵時刻上船，並根據他或她對港口的知識與當下的情況來操控船隻。引水人不僅要對船的安全負責，也要保護港口與海洋環境。
summary: 本文介紹引水人：船長之外負責帶船進港的專家，因為淺水、潮汐與風使靠岸危險。這份工作需要專業與快速判斷，核心是風險管理。

title: 橄欖油的等級與保存
text: Probably the most widely used oil in cooking, olive oil is made by crushing olives with stone or steel blades to release the oil. Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%). To be qualified as “extra virgin,” the oil must also pass both an official test in a laboratory and a sensory evaluation by a trained tasting panel. It must be free from impurity, while exhibiting some fruitiness and creating a pleasant bitter flavor along with a peppery sensation in the mouth. Second on the ranking is virgin olive oil. It is also a first pressing, but has a slightly higher acidity level (under 2%). Lastly, pure olive oil is the cheapest olive oil. It is refined to remove its impurities and blended to improve flavor, and is recommended for all-purpose cooking.

Packaging and storage also have an impact on the quality of olive oil. Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C. Moisture and oxygen promote oxidation and therefore limit its shelf life. Plastic containers usually do not provide adequate protection from light, heat, or moisture; additionally, small particles in plastics can leak into the oil, which further reduces its quality.

Olive oil tasters have long adopted descriptive terms such as “pure” and “light” to evaluate the quality of olive oil. Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results. A redefinition of the term “olive oil” is also proposed to make a clear distinction between virgin olive oil and pure olive oil. Industry members of the IOC hope to promote the trade of olive oil by initiating these changes.
pre: 這篇談橄欖油的品質：等級怎麼分、怎麼保存、組織想怎麼改進。數字（酸度 1%、2%）和等級順序要特別留意。
gist: 橄欖油分特級初榨、初榨、純橄欖油三級，品質與酸度不同。
包裝與保存方式影響品質：避光、低溫、少接觸水氣與氧氣。
國際橄欖油協會要改進檢驗方法並重新定義名詞，以促進貿易。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The flavor of olive oil.
The trade of olive oil.
The promotion of olive oil.
The quality of olive oil.
qs.hint: 三段各談什麼？找出共同的主題詞（grade、storage、test）。
qs.ev: Packaging and storage also have an impact on the quality of olive oil.
qs.ex: 第 1 段談等級、第 2 段談保存對品質的影響、第 3 段談檢驗品質的方法，整篇圍繞品質。
why: (A) 風味只是等級的一個面向。
(B) 貿易只在最後一句提及。
(C) 促銷不是重點。
(D) 等級、保存與檢驗都與品質有關，正確。
qs.strat: 主旨題找各段共同的上位概念，避免選只涵蓋一小部分的選項。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true about extra virgin olive oil?
o: It is free from any bitter flavor.
It is refined to remove its impurities.
It requires mixing of more than one kind of oil.
It has a lower acidity rate than virgin olive oil.
qs.hint: 回第 1 段比較特級初榨與初榨的酸度數字。
qs.ev: Extra virgin oil, the finest grade, is made from the first pressing of the olives and has a very low acidity rate (under 1%).
qs.ex: 特級初榨酸度低於 1%，初榨則是低於 2%，所以前者酸度較低。
why: (A) 特級初榨會有令人愉悅的苦味。
(B) 精煉去雜質的是純橄欖油。
(C) 混合是純橄欖油的做法。
(D) 酸度 1% 以下低於初榨的 2% 以下，正確。
qs.strat: 比較題要把數字或等級排在一起對照。

qs.s: According to the passage, what is the best way to store olive oil?
o: In a plastic container in a damp cellar.
In a clear glass bottle near the kitchen stove.
In an airtight glass bottle in a kitchen cupboard.
In an airproof bottle next to a well-lighted window.
qs.hint: 第 2 段列出保存的禁忌：光、熱、水氣、氧氣、塑膠。
qs.ev: Olive oil spoils quickly when exposed to direct sunlight, so it should be stored in the dark at 16-18°C.
qs.ex: 要避光、避水氣與氧氣、避免塑膠，因此密封玻璃瓶放在櫥櫃（暗處）最合適。
why: (A) 塑膠容器與潮濕都不佳。
(B) 透明瓶、靠近爐子會受光與熱。
(C) 密封、不透氧、放暗櫥櫃，符合條件。
(D) 靠窗有光，不佳。
qs.strat: 最佳作法題：把文中所有禁忌反過來，逐項檢查選項。

qs.s: What is the IOC trying to do?
o: Train more qualified olive oil tasters.
Improve the ways of grading olive oil.
Look for new techniques to boost production.
Build better connections among industry members.
qs.hint: 第 3 段 Recently, however 之後說了 IOC 在做什麼。
qs.ev: Recently, however, the International Olive Council (IOC) is seeking input on test methods to improve the transparency of the testing process and boost the accuracy of the results.
qs.ex: IOC 想改進檢測方法並重新定義用語，也就是改善橄欖油分級的方式。
why: (A) 沒提要訓練更多品評員。
(B) 改進檢測與分級定義，正確。
(C) 目的是促進貿易，不是提升產量。
(D) 沒提要加強會員聯繫。
qs.strat: however 後面常是重點，注意轉折後的新動作。

zh: 橄欖油可能是烹飪中使用最廣的油，是用石頭或鋼製刀片壓碎橄欖，把油釋放出來而製成的。特級初榨油是最好的等級，由橄欖第一次榨取製成，酸度很低（低於 1%）。要符合「特級初榨」的資格，這種油還必須通過實驗室的官方檢驗，以及訓練有素的品評小組的感官評鑑。它必須不含雜質，同時帶有些許果香，並在口中產生宜人的苦味與辛辣感。排名第二的是初榨橄欖油。它同樣是第一次榨取，但酸度稍高（低於 2%）。最後，純橄欖油是最便宜的橄欖油。它經過精煉以去除雜質，並經調和以改善風味，建議用於各種用途的烹調。
包裝與保存也會影響橄欖油的品質。橄欖油暴露在直射陽光下很快就會變質，因此應存放在 16 至 18 度的陰暗處。水氣與氧氣會促進氧化，因而縮短其保存期限。塑膠容器通常無法提供足夠的防光、防熱或防潮保護；此外，塑膠中的微小顆粒可能滲入油中，進一步降低品質。
橄欖油品評員長期以來使用像「純」和「淡」這類描述性詞語來評估橄欖油的品質。然而最近，國際橄欖油協會正徵求檢測方法的意見，以提高檢驗過程的透明度並提升結果的準確性。協會也提議重新定義「橄欖油」一詞，以清楚區分初榨橄欖油與純橄欖油。協會的業界成員希望藉由這些改變來促進橄欖油的貿易。
summary: 本文先介紹橄欖油三個等級與差異，再說明避光低溫等保存方式，最後談國際橄欖油協會為提高檢驗透明度與準確性而推動的改革。

title: 用狗吠鹿鳴趕走鐵軌上的鹿
text: Researchers in Japan have installed on a train a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer in order to prevent collisions with animals on the tracks.

The country has been troubled by a problem with trains colliding with deer on its railways. According to Japan’s transport ministry, there were 613 cases of train services suspended or delayed for at least 30 minutes resulting from collisions with deer and other wild animals in 2016-17.

Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets. They lick the rails to pick up iron filings caused by the action of wheels against tracks. This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock. In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.

This new device has been invented by a team at the country’s Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI). RTRI officials explain that deer have a habit of repeatedly snorting short, shrill sounds to alert other deer when they perceive danger. The barking of the hound, which drives deer to panic, strengthens the effect of the warning noise, according to the RTRI. When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.

RTRI researchers say late-night tests, at times when deer are most frequently seen by railway tracks, have resulted in a 45 percent reduction of deer sighting. Future plans include static barking sites where deer are commonly seen, but “the noises will not be blared in areas where people live beside the tracks.”
pre: 這是一則科技新聞：問題是什麼、原因是什麼、舊方法失敗、新方法如何運作。注意 NOT 與 true 題要回原文核對。
gist: 日本在列車上裝了模仿狗吠與鹿鳴的喇叭，防止撞到動物。
鹿撞車造成許多班次停駛或延誤。
鹿為了攝取鐵質舔鐵軌，過去燈光和獅子臉都失敗了。
新裝置結合鹿的警戒聲與狗吠，使鹿恐慌逃離。
夜間測試使鹿的目擊減少 45%，未來將設固定播放點，但不在住宅區。

qs.s: Why are deer attracted to train tracks?
o: They mate at night near railways.
They need nutrition from train tracks.
They like to snort at the passing train.
They sharpen their horns rubbing against the rails.
qs.hint: 第 3 段第一句直接說原因。
qs.ev: Deer are attracted to railway lines because of a need for iron in their diets.
qs.ex: 鹿因為飲食需要鐵質而舔鐵軌上的鐵屑，也就是從鐵軌取得營養。
why: (A) 沒提交配。
(B) 需要鐵質營養，正確。
(C) 鹿鳴是警戒聲，不是喜歡。
(D) 沒提磨角。
qs.strat: Why 題找 because / due to 引導的原因句。

qs.s: What device has NOT been used to solve the railway problem in Japan?
o: Flashing lights.
Barking speakers.
Noisy train tracks.
Lion face paintings.
qs.hint: 第 3 段末句列舉舊方法，第 4 段是新方法。
qs.ev: In the past, flashing red lights and even lion faces have been unsuccessfully trialed in an attempt to keep deer off the tracks.
qs.ex: 閃光燈、獅子臉與狗吠喇叭都提過，唯獨沒有吵鬧的鐵軌。
why: (A) 閃爍紅燈用過。
(B) 吠叫喇叭是新裝置。
(C) 文中沒提吵鬧鐵軌，是答案。
(D) 獅子臉用過。
qs.strat: NOT 題逐項找出處，沒有的就是答案。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about the deer issue discussed in the passage?
o: RTRI’s new invention prompts deer to run away.
People living near the tracks complain about deer snorts.
45 percent of train delays in Japan was caused by deer collision.
A combination of sound and visual devices attracts more deer to the tracks.
qs.hint: 對照第 4、5 段，逐項檢查數字與對象。
qs.ev: When the deer hear a combination of a 3-second-long recording of a deer’s snort and 20 seconds of a barking dog, they panic and flee rapidly.
qs.ex: 新裝置的聲音讓鹿恐慌並快速逃離，所以新發明促使鹿跑開。
why: (A) 鹿聽到後逃跑，正確。
(B) 文中沒有居民抱怨，只說不在住宅區播放。
(C) 45% 是鹿目擊減少的比例，不是延誤比例。
(D) 聲音加視覺裝置並不是吸引鹿。
qs.strat: 有數字的選項要檢查數字說的是什麼。

qs.s: What does the author mean by “the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock” in the third paragraph?
o: The heavy weight of iron materials.
The cruelty of a barking hound.
The battle between deer and other animals.
The danger of a fast-moving train.
qs.hint: 拆開字面：tons of（數噸）+ onrushing（疾衝）+ rolling stock（車輛）。
qs.ev: This dietary need has led to a constant battle to keep the deer separate from the unforgiving nature of tons of onrushing rolling stock.
qs.ex: 指數噸重、高速衝來的列車毫不留情，對鹿很危險，因此要把鹿與列車隔開。
why: (A) 重點是列車，不是鐵材重量。
(B) 狗吠與此無關。
(C) 不是動物之間的戰鬥。
(D) 高速列車的危險，正確。
qs.strat: 詞組題先拆解字面，再放回上下文判斷比喻意義。

zh: 日本的研究人員在列車上裝設了一個會像狗一樣吠叫、像鹿一樣噴氣鳴叫的喇叭，以防止與軌道上的動物相撞。
該國一直受列車與鹿在鐵路上相撞的問題所困擾。根據日本運輸省的資料，2016 至 17 年間，因與鹿及其他野生動物相撞而導致列車停駛或延誤至少 30 分鐘的案例有 613 起。
鹿被鐵軌吸引，是因為飲食上需要鐵質。牠們舔鐵軌來攝取車輪與軌道摩擦產生的鐵屑。這種飲食需求造成人們得持續努力把鹿與數噸重、疾衝而來而毫不留情的車輛隔開。過去，閃爍的紅燈甚至獅子的臉都試過，但都沒能成功讓鹿遠離軌道。
這套新裝置是由該國鐵道技術研究所的團隊發明的。研究所人員解釋，鹿有個習慣，感覺到危險時會反覆發出短促尖銳的噴氣聲，以警告其他鹿。據研究所說，獵犬的吠叫會使鹿恐慌，並強化警告聲的效果。當鹿聽到 3 秒的鹿鳴錄音加上 20 秒的狗吠組合時，會驚慌並迅速逃離。
研究人員說，在深夜（也是鹿最常出現在鐵軌旁的時段）進行的測試，使鹿的目擊數減少了 45%。未來計畫包括在常見鹿的地方設置固定的吠叫站，但「不會在鐵軌旁有居民居住的地區大聲播放這些聲音」。
summary: 日本為了減少列車撞鹿，研發結合鹿鳴與狗吠的喇叭。文章依序說明問題、鹿舔鐵軌的原因、過去失敗的方法，以及新裝置的原理與成效。

title: 仙人掌變成綠色能源
text: The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on Mexico’s national flag. The plant was considered sacred by the ancient Aztecs, and modern-day Mexicans eat it, drink it, and even use it in medicines and shampoos. Now scientists have come up with a new use for the bright green plant: producing renewable energy.

Known locally as nopal, the prickly pear is farmed on a massive scale in Mexico. Over the years, only the edible soft inner flesh has been used. The cactus’s thick outer layer (i.e., husk), with all those spines, had always been viewed as a waste product until researchers developed a biogas generator to turn the husks into electricity.

The pilot project dedicated to developing the cactus biogas generator began in the south of Mexico City. The area produces 200,000 tons a year of prickly pear cactus—up to 10 tons of which ends up as waste on the floor of the cactus market each day. Then, a local green energy startup company got the idea to turn that waste into energy. The generator is now in place at the cactus market, where the vendors are enthusiastic about this new way to utilize the tons of cactus husks that once went directly into the trash.

The prickly pear has a number of advantages over other biofuel crops, such as wheat, sugarcane, and soybeans. For one thing, only the husk of the cactus is used for generating biofuel, while its inner flesh is still preserved for food. Therefore, using the plant as a fuel source will not put pressure on food prices. Moreover, the cactus requires minimum water, and thus is not grown on traditional agricultural pasture. This means that no increased competition arises for the water or land presently used for food production.
The project in Mexico City has brought new hope to reducing the use of fossil fuels. If it can be expanded, the prickly pear could be the key to Mexico’s energy future.
pre: 這篇介紹墨西哥人把仙人掌的「廢棄外皮」拿來發電。讀的時候注意：原本怎麼用、新用途是什麼、比其他生質燃料作物好在哪。
gist: 仙人掌是墨西哥的象徵，如今又有再生能源的新用途。
過去只吃果肉，外皮被當廢物，直到研究者造出沼氣發電機。
墨西哥市南部的試驗計畫把市場廢棄外皮變成能源。
仙人掌比其他生質燃料作物優：不影響糧價，也不搶水搶地。
此計畫為減少化石燃料帶來希望，可能成為墨西哥能源的關鍵。

qs.s: What is the purpose of this passage?
o: To argue for the benefits of nopales.
To introduce a new source of energy.
