pre: 這是一篇「破除刻板印象」的文章：開頭先提出一般看法，接著用歷史事實修正。讀時請注意 However、Thus、Meanwhile 等轉折，以及 This 這類指涉詞指向前一句哪件事。
gist: 俄羅斯常被視為酗酒之國，批評者說這是天性，但事情沒那麼簡單。
古俄羅斯並不盛行飲酒，伏特加源自法國的葡萄酒精，直到十八世紀中葉酒精濃度都不高。
十五、十六世紀對俄羅斯人飲酒的記載互相矛盾，中世紀歐洲最會喝的其實是德國人。
十九世紀國家專賣與工業化生產，使伏特加更便宜、更普及，國家也因此獲利。
同時期出現反酒精運動，但問題至今仍在，俄羅斯人均飲酒量雖非第一，也接近前段班。

qs.s: What is the main purpose of the second paragraph in the passage?
o: To discuss the content of alcoholic drinks in ancient Europe.
To highlight the French impact on Russians’ drinking habits.
To argue against the assumption that Russians are born drinkers.
To link Russians’ vodka consumption to their adoption of Christianity.
qs.hint: 先看第 1 段末提出的看法（天性愛喝酒），再看第 2 段以什麼事實反駁。
qs.ev: The consumption of alcoholic beverages was unusual in ancient Russia.
qs.ex: 第 1 段說批評者認為飲酒是俄羅斯人的天性；第 2 段指出古代俄羅斯並不常喝酒、伏特加也不是他們發明的，目的在反駁「天生愛喝酒」的假設。
why: (A) 錯：談的是古代俄羅斯，不是古歐洲的酒類內容。
(B) 錯：提到法國只是說明伏特加的起源，不是段落重點。
(C) 對：用歷史事實反駁俄羅斯人生來愛喝酒的想法。
(D) 錯：基督教只是時間點，並非要連結兩者。
qs.strat: 段落目的題要連結上下段：本段是在支持還是反駁前段提出的觀點。

qs.s: Which of the following is true about vodka production?
o: Vodka production in Russia started in the 15th century.
The first vodka made from wheat was imported from France.
Germany was the biggest vodka producer in medieval Europe.
Russian people were encouraged to make their own vodka in the 19th century.
qs.hint: 找 vodka 與年代一起出現的句子，第 2 段。
qs.ev: The first Russian-made vodka appeared in the 15th century, and the drink remained relatively low in alcohol content until the mid-18th century.
qs.ex: 第一批俄羅斯製的伏特加出現在 15 世紀，所以 (A) 正確。
why: (A) 對：15 世紀出現第一批俄製伏特加。
(B) 錯：從法國傳入的是葡萄酒精，不是小麥伏特加。
(C) 錯：德國人是最能喝的，不是最大生產者。
(D) 錯：19 世紀國家專賣，只有政府可生產。
qs.strat: 細節題要留意選項改動的細節（原料、時間、對象）。

qs.s: What does “This” in the fourth paragraph refer to?
o: The alcohol.
The government.
The illegal production.
The state monopoly.
qs.hint: 往前找 This 之前一句，看哪一件事「填滿國庫、卻也助長飲酒」。
qs.ev: Thus, only the government was permitted to produce the alcohol. This soon filled the state treasury with huge revenues, but it also encouraged vodka consumption.
qs.ex: 前一句說只有政府可以生產酒，這種專賣制度讓國庫迅速充盈卻助長飲酒，所以 This 指國家專賣。
why: (A) 錯：酒精本身不會「填滿國庫」。
(B) 錯：政府是做事的主體，但 This 指整個制度。
(C) 錯：非法生產是專賣的原因，不是造成國庫收入的事。
(D) 對：專賣制度帶來財政收入並助長飲酒。
qs.strat: This 常指前一句整件事，不一定是單一名詞；用語意代入檢驗。

qs.s: How does the author conclude the passage in the last paragraph?
o: By providing further facts.
By summarizing the main ideas.
By raising a new problem.
By making a future prediction.
qs.hint: 看最後一段的內容：是整理重點、提出新問題，還是補充事實？
qs.ev: Although Russia does not occupy first place when it comes to alcohol consumption per capita, it is still close to the top.
qs.ex: 最後一段補充反酒精運動與目前人均飲酒量的事實，並沒有總結全文、提新問題或預測未來。
why: (A) 對：以反酒精運動與統計事實作結尾。
(B) 錯：沒有回顧全文要點。
(C) 錯：沒有帶出新的問題。
(D) 錯：沒有預測未來。
qs.strat: 結尾手法題要看最後一段實際做了什麼，不要憑印象選。

zh: 俄羅斯被普遍描繪為世界上最依賴酒精的國家。批評者說，飲酒幾乎是俄羅斯人與生俱來的特質。然而，事情並不僅止於此。
在古代俄羅斯，飲用酒精飲料並不常見。在俄羅斯採用基督教（十世紀）之前，沒有葡萄園，因此也沒有葡萄酒。人們只喝低酒精含量的飲料。伏特加是俄羅斯的國飲，卻不是俄羅斯人的發明。這種液體原本是十四世紀末從法國傳入的葡萄酒精。第一批俄羅斯製造的伏特加出現在十五世紀，而這種酒的酒精含量直到十八世紀中葉都相對較低。
關於十五、十六世紀俄羅斯人對酒精的傾向，資訊互相矛盾。有些文件記載俄羅斯人「一有機會就縱情豪飲」，而另一些則聲稱俄羅斯人「很少喝酒」。中世紀歐洲最能喝的其實是德國人。有許多關於他們嗜酒的說法，例如「像德國人一樣醉」。
俄羅斯國家在酒精消費於該國擴散上扮演了重要角色。十九世紀時，沙皇開始建立國家專賣制度，主要是因為劣質伏特加的非法生產增加。於是只有政府被允許生產這種酒。這很快讓國庫充滿巨額收入，但也助長了伏特加的消費。當該國開始工業化生產伏特加時，情況更加惡化，價格急劇下降，連低收入的公民也買得起。
同時，十九世紀也展開了一場強而有力的反酒精運動。政府制定了政策，也成立了公共組織來防止酗酒在該國蔓延。這項運動持續多年，然而問題依然存在。雖然俄羅斯在人均酒精消費量上並不居首位，但仍接近榜首。
summary: 本文破除「俄羅斯人天生愛喝酒」的刻板印象，從古代少飲酒、伏特加源自法國，到十九世紀國家專賣與工業化使飲酒普及，最後說明反酒精運動與目前的現況。

title: 沙克爾頓與堅忍號
text: In March 2022, the Endurance—the lost vessel of the famed polar explorer Ernest Shackleton—was found in Antarctica, 107 years after it sank. The news made headlines around the world, not only for the incredible achievement of the search team, but because the discovery marked the final chapter in a legendary story of extraordinary courage and perseverance.

On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica. From Plymouth, UK, the team arrived in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and on November 5 reached South Georgia Island, the last settlement of civilization en route to Antarctica. There, the real challenge began. Two days after leaving South Georgia in December, the Endurance encountered floating ice, and was soon completely trapped in pack ice.

The worthy vessel held up for nine months, drifting down south slowly and then pushed northward by the ice. Gradually, the pressure from the ice buckled the planks. Freezing water rushed in and exacerbated the situation. On October 27, 1915, Shackleton ordered his crew to abandon the ship, pitching tents on the ice a mile and a half away. Weeks later, they watched the Endurance sink beneath the Weddell Sea.

The next five months, the crew camped out on the pack ice as it drifted north, surviving on penguins, seals, and seaweed. Finally, the ice broke up enough for them to escape in lifeboats. For seven days, they sailed more than a hundred miles to the uninhabited Elephant Island. But the crew couldn’t survive long there. So, Shackleton made a dangerous attempt to get help: With five crew members, he sailed 800 miles over 16 days across freezing, stormy seas to South Georgia Island. Then the group hiked for 36 hours across the island to reach a whaling station.

Help was almost at hand, but ice and bad weather hindered their return. On August 30, 1916, Shackleton finally got back to Elephant Island with a ship big enough to rescue the rest of his men. All the members of the expedition team survived, but the Endurance remained lost under the sea until its discovery in 2022.
pre: 這是一篇依時間順序敘述的探險故事，開頭先說 2022 年找到沉船，接著回到 1914 年。閱讀時請標出日期、地點與每一次行動（出發、被困、棄船、求救、獲救）。
gist: 2022 年失落 107 年的堅忍號在南極被尋獲，為傳奇故事畫下句點。
1914 年沙克爾頓率隊出發橫越南極，離開南喬治亞島後遇到浮冰，船被困住。
船被冰擠壓進水，1915 年棄船，不久沉入威德爾海。
船員在冰上露營數月後乘救生艇到象島，沙克爾頓帶五人航向南喬治亞島求援。
沙克爾頓 1916 年帶船返回象島救出全員，堅忍號則沉睡海底直到 2022 年被發現。

qs.s: What is this passage mainly about?
o: A renowned Antarctic explorer.
The extreme weather in Antarctica.
A challenging voyage to Antarctica.
The amazing discovery of a sunken ship.
qs.hint: 看全文大部分篇幅在說什麼事件：出發、被困、棄船、求救、獲救。
qs.ev: On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica.
qs.ex: 第 1 段只是引子，第 2 至 5 段詳述堅忍號探險的艱辛歷程，所以主旨是一次充滿挑戰的南極航行。
why: (A) 錯：以人物為中心太窄，文章重點是整個航程。
(B) 錯：天氣只是困難之一，不是全文主題。
(C) 對：全文描述充滿挑戰的南極探險之旅。
(D) 錯：發現沉船只是開頭與結尾的小部分。
qs.strat: 主旨題要看絕大部分段落在談什麼，開頭的新聞引子不一定是主旨。

qs.s: Which of the following idioms is closest in meaning to “exacerbated the situation” in the third paragraph?
o: Broke the ice.
Cost an arm and a leg.
Missed the boat.
Added fuel to the fire.
qs.hint: 先判斷上下文：船已被冰壓壞，冰水又灌進來，情況是變好還是更糟？
qs.ev: Freezing water rushed in and exacerbated the situation.
qs.ex: 船板已被冰壓扭曲，再加上冰冷的水湧入，使情況更糟，與 add fuel to the fire（火上加油）意思相同。
why: (A) 錯：break the ice 是打破僵局。
(B) 錯：cost an arm and a leg 是代價昂貴。
(C) 錯：miss the boat 是錯失良機。
(D) 對：火上加油，使情況惡化。
qs.strat: 慣用語比對題先把原詞組意思用中文說出來（使惡化），再找意思相近的慣用語。

qs.s: According to the passage, which of the following is true about Shackleton and his Antarctic expedition?
o: His journey lasted more than two years.
He was the first man to cross over the Antarctic.
His team camped out on Elephant Island for five months.
He sent five crew members on a lifeboat to get help from a whaling station.
qs.hint: 算一算出發與獲救的日期：第 2 段與第 5 段。
qs.ev: On August 4, 1914, Sir Ernest Shackleton, along with a skilled crew of 27, set sail on the Endurance toward the South Pole, hoping to make the first land crossing over Antarctica.
qs.ex: 1914 年 8 月 4 日出發，1916 年 8 月 30 日才返回象島救出船員，時間超過兩年（兩年又 26 天），故 (A) 正確。
why: (A) 對：1914 年 8 月出發到 1916 年 8 月底，超過兩年。
(B) 錯：他只是「希望」首度橫越，並沒有成功。
(C) 錯：五個月是在浮冰上露營，不是在象島。
(D) 錯：是他本人帶五名船員去求援，並非派五人去。
qs.strat: 算日期題要從文中的起訖時間推算，並留意「more than」是否成立。

qs.s: Which of the following shows the correct route of the Endurance after leaving South Georgia?
o: 圖 (A)
圖 (B)
圖 (C)
圖 (D)
qs.hint: 回到第 2、3 段找路線：往哪個方向漂？後來被冰往哪裡推？最後在哪片海沉沒？
qs.ev: The worthy vessel held up for nine months, drifting down south slowly and then pushed northward by the ice.
qs.ex: 堅忍號離開南喬治亞島後駛入威德爾海，被浮冰困住、沿南極大陸漂流後沉沒，船本身沒有到過象島；圖 (C) 的路線從南喬治亞島往東南進入威德爾海、停在南極半島附近，故選 (C)。
why: (A) 錯：路線繞一大圈回到 South Georgia，但 Endurance 在 Weddell Sea 被浮冰困住後沉沒，並沒有開回去。
(B) 錯：方向繞反了，且同樣回到 South Georgia。
(C) 對：離開 South Georgia 後往東南進入 Weddell Sea，沿南極大陸漂流，最後停在南極半島附近（船被冰擠沉），沒有到 Elephant Island。
(D) 錯：直接經過 Elephant Island，那是船沉後船員搭小船才抵達的地方，不是船本身的航線。
qs.strat: 路線圖題把文字轉成方向箭頭（南→北），再檢查每張圖的起點、轉折點與終點。

zh: 2022 年 3 月，著名極地探險家歐內斯特・沙克爾頓失落的船「堅忍號」，在沉沒 107 年後於南極被尋獲。這則消息登上全球頭條，不僅因為搜尋團隊的驚人成就，更因為這項發現為一則充滿非凡勇氣與毅力的傳奇故事寫下了最後一章。
1914 年 8 月 4 日，歐內斯特・沙克爾頓爵士與 27 名技術嫻熟的船員啟航，乘坐堅忍號前往南極點，希望完成首次陸路橫越南極洲。團隊從英國普利茅斯抵達阿根廷布宜諾斯艾利斯，並在 11 月 5 日抵達南喬治亞島，也就是前往南極途中最後一個文明聚落。在那裡，真正的挑戰才開始。12 月離開南喬治亞兩天後，堅忍號遇上浮冰，不久便完全被困在冰群中。
這艘堅固的船撐了九個月，先是慢慢向南漂，後來被冰推向北方。漸漸地，冰的壓力使船板扭曲變形。冰冷的海水湧入，使情況更加惡化。1915 年 10 月 27 日，沙克爾頓下令船員棄船，在一英里半外的冰上搭帳篷。幾週後，他們看著堅忍號沉入威德爾海底。
接下來的五個月，船員在隨冰向北漂的浮冰上露營，靠企鵝、海豹與海草維生。最後，冰裂開到足以讓他們乘救生艇脫身的程度。他們航行七天，超過一百英里，抵達無人居住的象島。但船員無法在那裡撐太久。於是，沙克爾頓做了一次危險的嘗試以求救：他帶著五名船員，在冰冷、暴風雨的海上航行 16 天、800 英里，抵達南喬治亞島。接著這群人徒步 36 小時橫越全島，抵達一座捕鯨站。
救援近在眼前，但冰與惡劣天氣阻礙了他們返回。1916 年 8 月 30 日，沙克爾頓終於帶著一艘足以救出其餘人員的船回到象島。探險隊全員都存活了下來，但堅忍號仍沉沒在海底，直到 2022 年才被發現。
summary: 本文以堅忍號被尋獲開頭，回溯沙克爾頓探險隊出發、被困、棄船、求救與全員獲救的過程。結構是「現在→過去（依時間順序）→回到現在」。

title: 螺旋樓梯的歷史
text: In many old castles in Europe, visitors often find a fantastic spiral staircase, which provides a captivating focal point as it winds up the building. This prominent structure actually has a long and rich heritage.

In the Old Testament, reference is made to spiral staircases in the Temple of Solomon, suggesting that they were already in use by around 1,000 BC. The oldest spiral staircase still standing today is at Trajan’s Column in Rome. The staircase was built in 113 AD, with a total of 185 steps carved in stone and marble. Around this time, spiral staircases began to find much wider use in Roman architecture and across Europe.

Throughout the Middle Ages, winding staircases became a well-established feature of European castles, mainly for their advantages in helping to defend against attackers. To begin with, these staircases were quite narrow, so attackers would have to ascend one at a time, making it impossible to launch a mass attack. Also, the stairs were designed to turn clockwise upwards. This means that ascenders would have their right hand tight against the narrowest part of the staircases, close to the central pole, and as a result were unable to use their sword effectively. The attackers’ challenge was further complicated by the uneven steps of the staircase, often strategically designed by the castle owners. The defenders, living in the castles, were familiar with the stair pattern and could retreat up them very swiftly; while the attackers were much more likely to stumble and fall, particularly in the dimly lit confines of the staircase.

Being associated with medieval castles and kings, spiral staircases gradually won popularity in European architecture, with new materials emerging to cope with customers’ needs. In Victorian times, cast iron spiral staircases were popular for public buildings and homes for the rich. In the latter half of the 20th century, steel frames became cost-effective, and thus affordable for a much wider staircase market. Then, steel spiral staircases as fire escape stairs appeared in many buildings. Today, spiral staircases come in a wide variety of materials: steel, wood, concrete, and recently even glass. The timeless appeal of their classical design makes spiral staircases a much-desired feature in luxury homes, offices, and public buildings nowadays.
pre: 這是一篇依時間順序介紹螺旋樓梯的說明文：古代起源、中世紀城堡的防禦設計、近代材料的演變。讀時請圈出年代與材料，並理解中世紀設計為何對守城者有利。
gist: 歐洲古堡中常見迷人的螺旋樓梯，它有悠久的歷史。
聖經中已提到螺旋樓梯，現存最古老的在羅馬圖拉真圓柱，之後在羅馬與歐洲廣泛使用。
中世紀城堡用它來防禦：狹窄、順時針、不規則台階，使攻擊者難以揮劍又易跌倒。
因與城堡及國王有關而受歡迎，材料從鑄鐵、鋼到木、混凝土與玻璃，至今仍是豪宅與公共建築的熱門設計。

qs.s: Which question can the passage answer?
o: Where was the first spiral staircase constructed?
Who was the first designer of the spiral staircase?
What is the world’s most famous spiral staircase?
Why is the spiral staircase popular in modern times?
qs.hint: 看哪個疑問詞的答案出現在文中；最後一句常是作者的結論。
qs.ev: The timeless appeal of their classical design makes spiral staircases a much-desired feature in luxury homes, offices, and public buildings nowadays.
qs.ex: 最後一段說明螺旋樓梯因其歷久不衰的經典設計，如今仍是豪宅、辦公室與公共建築的熱門特色，回答了現代為何受歡迎。
why: (A) 錯：文中只說現存最古老的在羅馬，沒說「最早建造」的地點。
(B) 錯：沒有提到最早的設計者。
(C) 錯：沒有討論最著名的螺旋樓梯。
(D) 對：因經典設計永不過時。
qs.strat: 「這篇文章能回答什麼問題」要逐一確認文中是否有明確答案，不能只憑猜測。

qs.s: What does “them” in the third paragraph refer to?
o: Stairs.
Confines.
Attackers.
Defenders.
qs.hint: 把選項代回句子：守城者能「往上撤退」的是什麼？
qs.ev: The defenders, living in the castles, were familiar with the stair pattern and could retreat up them very swiftly
qs.ex: 守城者熟悉樓梯的形式，能沿著它們迅速向上撤退，所以 them 指樓梯（stairs）。
why: (A) 對：retreat up them = 沿著樓梯往上撤退。
(B) 錯：confines 是句尾的名詞，不能「被爬上去」。
(C) 錯：撤退的是守城者，不是爬他們。
(D) 錯：them 與主詞 The defenders 不可同指。
qs.strat: 指涉題往前找可被「up」的東西，並檢查單複數與語意。

qs.s: According to the passage, which is a correct time sequence of the materials used in making spiral staircases?
o: stone → iron → steel → glass
stone → wood → iron → steel
iron → marble → wood → glass
marble → wood → stone → concrete
qs.hint: 把文中材料依年代排：1,000 BC／113 AD、中世紀、維多利亞、20 世紀下半、今日。
qs.ev: In Victorian times, cast iron spiral staircases were popular for public buildings and homes for the rich.
qs.ex: 最早用石與大理石（113 AD），維多利亞時代用鑄鐵，20 世紀後半用鋼，近年出現玻璃，因此順序為石→鐵→鋼→玻璃。
why: (A) 對：與文中時間順序一致。
(B) 錯：木材是「今日」多樣材料之一，沒有排在鐵之前。
(C) 錯：鐵並非最早，石與大理石更早。
(D) 錯：石頭比木頭早，且混凝土是近代才有。
qs.strat: 時間順序題把文中的時間點做成時間軸，再去比對選項順序。

qs.s: Which of the following statements can be inferred about spiral staircases in the Medieval Ages?
o: The staircase was too narrow to allow any quick retreat.
The clockwise design favored right-handed castle defenders.
The uneven steps made it easier to ascend than descend the stairs.
The staircase was dark enough for defenders to hide from attackers.
qs.hint: 想想攻擊者往上時，右手靠中柱；那守城者往下時，右手會在哪一側？
qs.ev: This means that ascenders would have their right hand tight against the narrowest part of the staircases, close to the central pole, and as a result were unable to use their sword effectively.
qs.ex: 順時針向上的設計讓向上攻的人右手被中柱卡住，無法有效揮劍；反過來，由上往下守的人右手在外側，揮劍空間大，所以有利於慣用右手的守城者。
why: (A) 錯：守城者熟悉階梯，能迅速撤退。
(B) 對：攻擊者的右手受限，推論守方（右撇子）占優勢。
(C) 錯：文中沒說上下樓難易的比較，而是對不熟悉者不利。
(D) 錯：只說昏暗使攻擊者易跌倒，沒說守城者躲藏。
qs.strat: 推論題要把文中描述的因果延伸一步，但不能超出證據；排除文中沒有依據的選項。

zh: 在歐洲許多古堡裡，遊客常會看到一座奇妙的螺旋樓梯，它盤繞著建築向上，成為迷人的焦點。這個顯眼的結構其實有著悠久而豐富的傳統。
《舊約聖經》中提到所羅門聖殿裡有螺旋樓梯，顯示它們早在約西元前 1000 年就已被使用。現今仍屹立的最古老螺旋樓梯位於羅馬的圖拉真圓柱。這座樓梯建於西元 113 年，共有 185 級階梯，以石頭與大理石雕成。大約在這個時期，螺旋樓梯開始在羅馬建築與整個歐洲得到更廣泛的使用。

整個中世紀期間，螺旋樓梯成為歐洲城堡中一項確立已久的特色，主要是因為它們有助於防禦攻擊者。首先，這些樓梯相當狹窄，攻擊者必須一次一個往上爬，使大規模攻擊成為不可能。此外，樓梯被設計成向上順時針旋轉。這表示往上爬的人，右手會緊貼著樓梯最窄的部分，靠近中央支柱，因此無法有效地使用劍。攻擊者的挑戰還被樓梯高低不平的台階進一步增加，這些台階常由城堡主人策略性地設計。居住在城堡中的守衛熟悉樓梯的樣式，能很迅速地沿著它們向上撤退；而攻擊者則更容易絆倒跌落，尤其是在昏暗的樓梯間裡。

由於與中世紀城堡與國王相連，螺旋樓梯逐漸在歐洲建築中受到歡迎，也出現新材料以因應顧客需求。維多利亞時代，鑄鐵螺旋樓梯在公共建築與富人住宅中很流行。二十世紀後半，鋼架變得符合成本效益，因而更廣大的樓梯市場也買得起。接著，作為防火逃生梯的鋼製螺旋樓梯出現在許多建築中。今天，螺旋樓梯有各種各樣的材質：鋼、木、混凝土，近來甚至有玻璃。其經典設計歷久不衰的魅力，使螺旋樓梯如今成為豪宅、辦公室與公共建築中備受渴望的特色。
summary: 本文依時間說明螺旋樓梯：古代已有、羅馬時期廣泛使用，中世紀城堡利用其設計防禦敵人，近代材料不斷演變，如今仍因經典設計而受歡迎。

title: 地圖為什麼上北下南
text: Have you ever wondered why north comes at the top of a map? Well, north may seem a natural choice for the top spot today, but that wasn’t always the case.

Documents from ancient times indicate that many maps in early ages were pointing to the east, where the sun rose. In ancient India, for example, maps were most likely oriented to the east. Though there is no physical evidence to support this, the word dakshina “south” in Indian languages also means “right,” suggesting that ancient Indians were oriented toward the east, and therefore south was on their right-hand side. Ample evidences from the Old Testament also suggest that east was at the top of maps in pre-Biblical and Biblical eras, a reason why east is still referred to as the “Orient” today.

In the oldest surviving maps, south is at the top, and north points down. Early Egyptian maps showed south on top, most likely because the Nile, vital to Egyptian livelihood, originated in the south. As rivers were believed to flow downward, “up” was therefore south. Map makers in Arabia also drew maps with south on top since the earliest Muslims lived north of Mecca, and a south-oriented map would show the followers looking up toward their holy city.

The preference for north arose during the European age of exploration. At the time, sailors relied on the North Star to find their way across the Mediterranean and later the Atlantic. By the 16th century, when Europe’s search for trading routes was at its peak, maps became Eurocentric, with north on top. The expansion of European imperialism in the following centuries further established the “north up” practice as the standard.

Today, map orientation is taking on a new perspective. In perhaps our most common interaction with maps—the use of GPS systems on our phones and in our cars, directions have ceased to be as important. The layouts are dynamic, oriented toward our travel path.

So, perhaps the north-on-top practice is less a rule and more a blip. After centuries of technological advancements, it seems we’ve ended up right where we began in ancient times: with ourselves in the middle, and our destinations at the top.
pre: 這是一篇談地圖「上方」方位如何隨時代改變的文章：東在上、南在上、北在上、再到 GPS。讀時請整理每個時期（地區）的方位與原因，並留意最後兩段的比喻。
gist: 提出問題：為什麼地圖上方是北？過去並非一直如此。
早期地圖多以東方為上，古印度與聖經時代都有跡象。
最古老的存世地圖以南為上，如埃及（尼羅河）與阿拉伯（朝向麥加）。
歐洲大航海時代水手靠北極星，加上歐洲勢力擴張，使北在上成為標準。
如今 GPS 地圖依行進方向動態呈現，方位已不那麼重要。
北在上或許只是一段插曲，今日地圖又回到以自己為中心、目的地在上方。

qs.s: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why east is referred to as the “Orient.”
How maps differ from GPS in function.
How map orientation evolved over time.
Why maps were important during the age of exploration.
qs.hint: 看每一段是哪個時期、哪個方位在上，全文是在談什麼變化。
qs.ev: The preference for north arose during the European age of exploration.
qs.ex: 全文依序談東在上、南在上、北在上與 GPS 動態方位，說明地圖上方的方位如何隨時間演變。
why: (A) 錯：Orient 只是第 2 段的一個細節。
(B) 錯：GPS 只在第 5 段出現，且不是比較功能。
(C) 對：地圖方位隨時代演進。
(D) 錯：只是北在上興起的背景之一。
qs.strat: 主旨題要選能涵蓋全部段落的選項，避免只涵蓋單一細節的選項。

qs.s: What does “this” refer to in the second paragraph?
o: The word dakshina.
Physical evidence.
Ancient India.
East-orientation of maps.
qs.hint: 看 Though there is no physical evidence to support this 前面一句在主張什麼。
qs.ev: In ancient India, for example, maps were most likely oriented to the east. Though there is no physical evidence to support this
qs.ex: 前一句說古印度地圖很可能以東為上，接著說「沒有實物證據支持這個說法」，this 指的是這個以東為上的看法。
why: (A) 錯：dakshina 是後面用來補充的語言線索。
(B) 錯：physical evidence 本身不能被「證據支持」。
(C) 錯：古印度是地點，不是需要被支持的主張。
(D) 對：地圖以東為上的說法。
qs.strat: this 指的常是前一句的整個主張，而非單一名詞。

qs.s: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “a blip” in the last paragraph?
o: A temporary state.
An urgent need.
A critical decision.
An advanced system.
qs.hint: 看 less a rule and more a blip；再看後面說最後又回到古代的狀態。
qs.ev: So, perhaps the north-on-top practice is less a rule and more a blip.
qs.ex: 作者認為北在上不是永遠的規則，只是漫長歷史中的小插曲，因為現在又回到「以自己為中心、目的地在上」，所以 blip 是暫時的狀態。
why: (A) 對：blip 即短暫的小起伏、暫時的狀態。
(B) 錯：沒有「迫切需要」的意思。
(C) 錯：不是重大決定。
(D) 錯：不是先進的系統。
qs.strat: 生字題看對比：less a rule（長久規則）↔ more a blip（短暫現象）。

qs.s: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Sailors took the North Star as their final destination.
The GPS system has a fixed direction for orientation.
South was placed at the top of maps in the pre-Biblical era.
Old Islamic maps put south at the top for religious purposes.
qs.hint: 逐項回到相關段落核對：第 2、3、4、5 段。
qs.ev: Map makers in Arabia also drew maps with south on top since the earliest Muslims lived north of Mecca, and a south-oriented map would show the followers looking up toward their holy city.
qs.ex: 阿拉伯製圖者把南放在上方，因為最早的穆斯林住在麥加北邊，這樣信徒就能「向上」望向聖城，是出於宗教因素。
why: (A) 錯：北極星是用來導航，不是終點。
(B) 錯：GPS 的版面是依行進路徑動態調整。
(C) 錯：聖經與先聖經時代是以東在上。
(D) 對：為使信徒望向聖城麥加。
qs.strat: 是非題要注意時代與地區的對應（pre-Biblical 是東在上，不是南在上）。

zh: 你是否曾好奇，為什麼地圖的上方是北？嗯，北今天看起來似乎是上方位置的自然選擇，但情況並非一直如此。
古代文獻顯示，早期許多地圖是朝向東方，也就是太陽升起的地方。例如，在古印度，地圖很可能以東為方向。雖然沒有實物證據支持這點，但印度語言中的 dakshina「南」同時也有「右」的意思，暗示古印度人是面朝東方，因此南方在他們的右手邊。《舊約聖經》中也有充分證據顯示，在聖經之前與聖經時代，東方位於地圖上方，這也是為什麼東方至今仍被稱為「Orient」的原因之一。
在現存最古老的地圖中，南方在上，北方朝下。早期埃及地圖把南放在上方，很可能是因為對埃及人生計至關重要的尼羅河發源於南方。由於人們相信河水向下流，因此「上」就是南方。阿拉伯的製圖者也把南放在上方繪製地圖，因為最早的穆斯林住在麥加以北，南向的地圖會讓信徒向上望向他們的聖城。
對北方的偏好出現在歐洲大航海時代。當時，水手們依靠北極星在地中海，後來在大西洋上找路。到十六世紀，歐洲尋找貿易路線的熱潮達到頂點時，地圖變成以歐洲為中心，並以北為上。在接下來的幾個世紀，歐洲帝國主義的擴張進一步將「上北」的做法確立為標準。
今天，地圖的方位正出現新的視角。在我們也許最常與地圖互動的方式，即在手機和車上使用 GPS 系統中，方向已不再那麼重要。版面是動態的，朝向我們的行進路線。
所以，也許上北下南與其說是規則，不如說是一段小插曲。經過幾世紀的技術進步，我們似乎又回到了古代的起點：以自己為中心，目的地在上方。
summary: 本文依時間順序說明地圖上方的方位從東、南變成北，再到 GPS 以行進方向為上，並以「回到起點」作結，說明北在上只是一段歷史插曲。
